- Transition plan integration and governance:
  - Decarbonization targets embedded in Group strategic objectives; each business line created a roadmap aligning commercial and climate targets.
  - Execution managed short-to-medium term within divisions; overall monitoring by the Executive Committee; progressive incorporation of transition projects into strategic and budget reviews with tracking of execution, costs, and value creation; strengthens integrated financial and non-financial planning.
  - Construction led by the Sustainability Department; iterative validation by the Executive Committee; Supervisory Board kept informed; Mission Committee contributed and approved final content.
  - Subsidiary governance: CNP Assurances’ plan approved/monitored by its Board; LBP AM’s plan slated for approval in 2025 by the Sustainable Finance Committee and Supervisory Board; Louvre Banque Privée’s plan adopted in 2024, to be co-published with La Banque Postale’s in 2025.
- Monitoring and review:
  - Annual public progress reporting in the sustainability report; formal management mechanisms to assess progress and allow adjustments; full plan review every 3–5 years to reflect regulatory and strategic developments.
- Climate policies (mitigation, adaptation, energy efficiency):
  - Mitigation: Reduction of GHG emissions across activities, with sector policies for coal, oil and gas, and aeronautics; decarbonization targets/pathways for carbon-intensive sectors (real estate, automotive transport, air transport, cement), focused on Corporate and Investment Banking.
  - Adaptation: Caisse des Dépôts Group adopted an adaptation policy in 2024; La Banque Postale Group to develop an aligned adaptation policy starting 2025.

  - Application of the parent Group’s climate policy: strict framework for high-emission sectors, progressive alignment to a 1.5°C pathway, and financing supportive of environmental transition.

text:
2.1.3 Climate change mitigation 
and adaptation  policies
Through its climate policies, La  Banque  Postale Group
aims to  address the  following sustainability issues:
•mitigation of environmental impacts through policies to
reduce  greenhouse gas (GHG)  emissions across all
activities. The mitigation component relates in particular
to Corporate and Investment Banking, and is achieved
through actions such  as establishing sector-specific
policies (coal, oil and gas, aeronautical) or by establishing
decarbonisation 
targets and pathways for certain
carbon-intensive 
sectors (real estate, automotive transport,
air transport and cement);
•climate change adaptation: in 2024, the Caisse des
Dépôts Group adopted an adaptation policy that targets
both operational  activities and  investments and
financing. Work will be initiated in 2025 to eventually
equip La Banque Postale Group with a climate change
adaptation 
policy aligned with that of the Caisse des
Dépôts Group;
•energy efficiency,  which  is addressed in the  operational
scope  through  commitments related to building
management. [E1_2_01]Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1192Sustainable performance
Environmental information
These  issues are addressed within the operational scope
through actions  and commitments  to improve  energy
efficiency,  use renewable energy and reduce emissions
related  to transport or  purchases. These commitments are
detailed in  Section 2.2.1.5 “Decarbonisation  levers  and
action  plans”.
As a subsidiary of Caisse des Dépôts and La  Poste,
La Banque Postale applies the Group’s Climate policy in
the financing and investment scope. This policy aims for
a 
strict framework for high-emission activities, decarbonisation
of activities and portfolios based on a pathway which
gradually  aligns with a 1.5°C ambition, and financing to be
deployed  in favour  of the environmental  transformation.
In addition, La  Banque  Postale has established sector-
specific  policies,  intervention  principles  and a  Responsible
Financing  and  Investment  Charter.
Sector -specific  policies
These  policies form part of La Banque Postale’s  “net zero
emissions " by 2040 ambition. Their  provisions apply to all
financing  and investments in the banking  scope relating
to the coal, oil, gas and aeronautics sectors. They concern
in particular the activities of the Corporate  Banking andLocal Development division. The activities of the bancassurance
divisions in France and  abroad, as well as those  of the
Wealth and Asset Management division, are excluded
from 
these policies to date. The policies specific to these
scopes  are presented below.
The business lines are responsible for  implementing these
policies, with the support of the Sustainability Department.
These policies are available on the La Banque Postale website.

title: Risk Management Policy – Coal sector
heading: Risk Management Policy – Coal sector
start_phrase: This policy establishes the principles to be applied in order to fulfil its commitment to completely exit the coal sector by 2030.
summary:
- Scope and intent: The section outlines La Banque Postale’s environmental and climate strategy within its universal registration document, referencing a glossary for CSR terms and linking to detailed decarbonization levers and action plans.
- Group alignment: As part of Caisse des Dépôts and La Poste, the bank applies the Group Climate Policy across financing and investments to set strict rules for high-emission activities, progressively align portfolios with a 1.5°C pathway, and channel financing toward environmental transformation.
- Net zero by 2040 sector policies (banking scope): 
  - Coal: Commitment to a complete coal exit by 2030; financing only for companies publicly committed to exit coal before 2030 with science-based, Paris-aligned transition plans; financing allowed for renewable projects and renewable subsidiaries.
  - Oil & gas: Commitment to a total exit by 2030; exclusion and gradual divestment from companies, including those on GOGEL, unless they have a credible public exit strategy before 2040; exceptions only for health/safety or regulatory compliance; no collaboration with entities opposing the energy transition.
  - Aeronautics: Financing limited to newest aircraft and companies with 1.5°C-aligned strategies from 2025; support for SAF and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except specific French law provision), with support for modernization that advances energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.
  - Note: Policies apply to Corporate Banking and Local Development; bancassurance and Wealth & Asset Management are out of scope here and have separate policies.
- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: Embeds decarbonization in corporate and investment banking; imposes exclusions for fossil fuel activities and environmental law violators; controversy assessment procedures in place.
- Operational commitments: Additional responsible commitments span mobility, building energy performance, digital, and purchasing.
- Market initiatives: Active participation in UNEP FI Principles for Responsible Banking since 2019, aligning strategy with SDGs and the Paris Agreement; PRB reporting referenced.
- Subsidiary focus (CNP Assurances): 
  - Frameworks: Compliant with Article 29 of the Energy-Climate Law and SFDR; aligned with UN Global Compact and PRI.
  - Targets: Member of the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance (carbon neutrality in the investment portfolio by 2050).
  - Levers: Portfolio Paris alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and public policy advocacy.
  - Policies: Coal phase-out (zero exposure by 2030 EU/OECD; 2040 elsewhere); extended oil and gas investment restrictions (2021–2022); due diligence policy (2024) organized around exclusion, engagement, and ESG-based selection; governance and oversight by Investment Department and asset management committees.

Risk Management Policy  – Coal  sector
This policy establishes the principles to be applied in order
to 
fulfil its commitment to completely exit the coal sector

summary:
- Overview of La Banque Postale’s environmental and sustainable finance commitments within its 2024 Universal Registration Document.
- Oil and Gas Risk Management Policy: commitment to fully exit oil and gas by 2030; exclusion of companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries; conditional engagement only with firms having credible public exit strategies before 2040; limited exceptions for health/safety/regulatory financing; no collaboration with companies obstructing the energy transition.
- Aeronautics sector principles: financing limited to newest aircraft and companies aligned with a 1.5°C pathway from 2025; support for SAF and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except in France if permitted by Climate and Resilience law); support for modernization projects that advance energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.
- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: integrates decarbonization into corporate and investment banking; excludes fossil fuel activities and companies breaching environmental laws; controversy assessment procedures for environmental issues; cross-reference to detailed charter.
- Participation in market initiatives: alignment with UNEP FI Principles for Responsible Banking, SDGs, and Paris Agreement; reference to PRB reporting section.
- Subsidiary commitments (CNP Assurances): adherence to LEC Article 29, SFDR, UN Global Compact, PRI; member of Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance targeting portfolio net zero by 2050; three levers—portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and advocacy for supportive public policies; 2024-updated due diligence policy with pillars of exclusions, engagement, and ESG-based selection; coal phase-out by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (rest of world); extended oil and gas investment restrictions (2021–2022); governance and oversight by the Investment Department and asset management committees.
text:
Risk  Management Policy  – Oil and Gas sectors
This  policy establishes the principles  to be  applied to
achieve a total exit commitment from these sectors by
2030 in order  to support  its climate  commitments.
Under  this policy, La  Banque  Postale undertakes to
exclude oil and  gas companies from its financial services
by 2030,  including  those  listed in the  Global Oil and  Gas
Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries, and to gradually
divest 
from these companies. Nevertheless, it will maintain
its commercial relationships with the companies listed in
GOGEL  and their subsidiaries if they have  a public and
credible exit strategy for the oil and gas sectors before 2040.
Financing 
required for health or safety reasons, or to comply
with  regulatory  standards , is excluded from  this policy.
In addition, La Banque Postale rules out any collaboration
with 
companies which are opposed to the energy transition,
particularly those that slow down or block efforts to exit
the fossil  fuels  sector.

title: The Bank’s principles of intervention in the aeronautics sector
heading: The Bank's principles of intervention in the aeronautics sector
start_phrase: In line with its climate commitments, the principles establish the rules to be applied in order to participate in and encourage the decarbonisation of the aeronautics sector.
summary:
- Sets a Risk Management Policy for Oil & Gas with a full exit by 2030: exclusion and gradual divestment from companies, including those on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries; maintains ties only if firms have a public, credible pre-2040 exit strategy; allows financing solely for health/safety or regulatory needs; rejects collaboration with companies obstructing the energy transition.
- Defines climate-aligned principles for the aeronautics sector: financing limited to newest aircraft and, from 2025, companies on a 1.5°C pathway; supports SAF and electric aircraft projects; stops financing new airports (except where allowed by France’s Climate and Resilience law); backs upgrades to existing airports that advance energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.
- Outlines the Responsible Financing and Investment Charter guiding Corporate and Investment Banking: exclusions for fossil fuel activities and environmental law violators; controversy assessment procedures; integrates decarbonization into financing and lending decisions.
- Highlights participation in market initiatives, notably UNEP FI’s Principles for Responsible Banking since 2019, aligning strategy with the SDGs and the Paris Agreement, with PRB reporting referenced in the URD.
- Details subsidiary policies, chiefly CNP Assurances: climate strategy aligned with Article 29 LEC and SFDR; adheres to the UN Global Compact and PRI; member of the Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance targeting net-zero by 2050; three levers—portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and policy advocacy; a 2024-updated due diligence policy centered on exclusions, engagement, and ESG-based selection; coal phase-out to zero by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (elsewhere); extended oil and gas investment restrictions in 2021–2022; governance and monitoring handled by the Investment Department and asset management committees.
text:
In line  with its climate commitments, the principles
establish the  rules to be applied  in order  to participate  in
and encourage the decarbonisation  of the aeronautics
sector.  They  are aligned  with  the Paris  Agreement.
Based  on its  principles, La  Banque Postale undertakes to
finance 
only the newest aircraft and aeronautics companies
which, 
from 2025, have strategies aligned with the pathway
of 1.5°C of global warming. Moreover, to support the energy
transition, 
La  Banque  Postale is able to finance projects
which promote the use of sustainable fuel (SAF) and
electric  aircraft. In addition, La Banque Postale  has stated
that it  will not finance new airports, except in France if
explicitly provided for by the French Climate and Resilience
law. However, it will support projects aimed at modernizing
existing infrastructures, provided  that they contribute  to
the energy transition, the preservation of biodiversity, or
the improvement of the environmental performance of
airport  platforms.

title: Responsible Financing and Investment Charter
heading: Responsible Financing and Investment Charter
start_phrase: La Banque Postale is well aware of the need to incorporate decarbonisation matters into its Corporate and Investment Banking activities, and also works with other sectors.
summary:
- Focus: Environmental information within La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, outlining sustainable performance policies, risk management, and responsible financing to meet climate goals.

- Oil and gas risk management policy:
  - Commitment to fully exit oil and gas by 2030.
  - Exclusion of companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries, with phased divestment.
  - Continued engagement only with firms having a credible, public exit strategy before 2040.
  - Exceptions limited to financing for health/safety or regulatory compliance.
  - No collaboration with companies opposing the energy transition.

- Aeronautics sector principles:
  - Financing restricted to newest aircraft and companies with strategies aligned to a 1.5°C pathway from 2025.
  - Support for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and electric aircraft projects.
  - No financing of new airports (except in France where permitted by the Climate and Resilience law).
  - Support for modernization of existing infrastructure that advances energy transition, biodiversity, and environmental performance.

- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter:
  - Integrates decarbonization into corporate and investment banking.
  - Exclusions for fossil fuel activities and companies violating environmental laws.
  - Procedure to assess companies involved in serious or repeated environmental controversies.
  - Provides guidance for financing and lending to business clients.

- External initiatives:
  - Active participation in the UN’s Principles for Responsible Banking (UNEP FI), aligning strategy with the SDGs and the Paris Agreement; PRB reporting referenced in the document.

- Subsidiary policies (CNP Assurances):
  - Climate policy aligned with Article 29 of the Energy-Climate Law, SFDR, UN Global Compact, and PRI.
  - Member of the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance; commitment to net-zero investment portfolio by 2050.
  - Three levers: portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure; shareholder engagement; advocacy for pro-transition public policies.
  - 2024 due diligence policy centered on exclusion, engagement, and ESG-based selection.
  - Coal phase-out: zero exposure by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (rest of world); extended oil and gas investment restrictions (2021–2022).
  - Oversight by the Investment Department and asset management committees.
text:
Responsible  Financing and Investment Charter
La Banque Postale is well aware of the need to incorporate
decarbonisation matters  into  its Corporate and Investment
Banking activities, and also works with other sectors. In order
to achieve this, La  Banque  Postale's Responsible Financing
and Investment Charter derived from its risk management
policy  provides  guidance  on its financing operations and
lending  to business  customers.
The Charter imposes exclusions for companies operating
in fossil fuels sectors or  that have violated environmental
legislation. In the event of serious or repeated controversies
over environmental issues,  a procedure  is in  place to
assess the  companies  concerned. For more information,
please  refer to  the focus  point: La   Banque  Postale’s
Financing and Investment Charter.

text:
Other  initiatives
For several years now, La  Banque  Postale  has chosen to
actively collaborate in market discussions and to participate
in various benchmark initiatives such as the  Principles for
Responsible Banking (PRB),  a global initiative coordinated
by the  United Nations Environment Programme Finance
Initiative (UNEP FI). By signing these principles in 2019,
La Banque Postale committed to  aligning its strategy with
international and national reference frameworks, in particular
the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Climate
Agreement. 
The PRB report can be found in Section 8.1
“Principles for  Responsible  Banking”  of the Universal
Registration Document.

title: Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
heading: Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
start_phrase: In addition, La Banque Postale’s subsidiaries have established climate change mitigation policies for their activities.
summary:
The excerpt outlines La Banque Postale’s environmental risk management, sector policies, responsible financing framework, subsidiary commitments, and science-based decarbonization targets.

- Oil and gas risk policy: commitment to fully exit the oil and gas sectors by 2030; exclusion of companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries, with gradual divestment; continued relationships only with firms having a public, credible pre-2040 exit strategy; allowance for financing strictly needed for health/safety or regulatory compliance; no collaboration with companies obstructing the energy transition.

- Aeronautics sector principles: financing restricted to newest aircraft and companies aligned with a 1.5°C pathway from 2025; support for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except possible cases in France per the Climate and Resilience law); support for modernization of existing infrastructure when it advances the energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.

- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: embeds decarbonization in corporate and investment banking; excludes fossil fuel companies and those violating environmental laws; controversy assessment process for serious/repeated environmental issues.

- Industry initiatives: active participation in market frameworks; PRB (UNEP FI) signatory since 2019, aligning strategy with SDGs and the Paris Agreement; PRB reporting referenced in the document.

- Subsidiaries’ policies and governance:
  - CNP Assurances: climate strategy aligned with LEC Article 29 and SFDR; UN-convened Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance member (2050 portfolio net zero); three levers—portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and advocacy for supportive public policies; 2024 due diligence policy built on exclusion, engagement, and ESG integration; coal exit by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (rest of world); extended exclusions to oil and gas (2021–2022); climate risk mitigation via reinsurance for excess mortality (including pandemics and heat waves).
  - LBP AM: exclusion policy covering thermal coal and oil & gas (updated 2023), validated by the Sustainable Finance Committee; oversight by ESG and GREaT committees; applies to all open-ended funds; harmonization in progress with La Financière de l’Échiquier (voting, engagement, coal already aligned; oil & gas combining underway); engagement policy to improve portfolio climate performance, with weekly ESG committee monitoring; Governance Committee oversees voting policy.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: integrates sustainability risks under SFDR and Energy-Climate Act Article 29; ESG Charter sets targets; operational responsibility lies with the Director of Discretionary Management and the Chief Sustainability Officer; Executive Board approves annual sustainability roadmap; aims to balance ESG integration with diversification and risk control; key ESG documents publicly available.

- Climate targets and performance trajectory (operational scope):
  - Net zero ambition by 2040, using science-based trajectories.
  - 100% renewable electricity by 2030.
  - Reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 43.6% over 2021–2030 (vehicle fleet and buildings; excludes Banking Advice Line, CNP Assurances, and La Poste Network buildings), aligned to a 1.5°C scenario using the Absolute Contraction Approach.
  - Reduce partial Scope 3 emissions (categories 1 partial, 3, 6, 7) by 25%.
  - Expected absolute reductions by 2030: Scope 1 −2,219 tCO2e; Scope 2 (market-based) −736 tCO2e; Scope 3 (partial) −7,757 tCO2e.
  - Targets aligned with SBTi pathway validated in March 2024 for La Poste SA and implemented for La Banque Postale SA.
text:
Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group
subsidiaries
In addition, La  Banque Postale’s subsidiaries have established
climate change mitigation policies for their activities.
CNP  Assurances  focuses its climate policies and actions
around 
recent regulations, such as Article 29 of the
Energy-Climate law (LEC) and the SFDR regulation, and
also relies on the Global Compact and the Principles for
Responsible Investment (PRI). In 2019, CNP  Assurances
joined  the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance, committing to
achieving carbon neutrality in its investment portfolio by
2050. 
This  international alliance, bringing  together more
than 80 institutional investors, aims to limit global warming
to 1.5°C . CNP  Assurances  relies on  three main levers:
•regularly  measuring the alignment of the investment
portfolio with the Paris Agreement  and publishing the
progress made;
•conducting shareholder dialogue with companies to
ensure that they are also moving towards carbon neutrality;
•demanding  public policies in favour of a transition to a
low-carbon economy.
All of CNP  Assurances’ commitments  are presented in its
due diligence policy concerning the negative impacts of
investment  decisions on sustainability factors. Revised in
2024, it presents the three pillars of CNP  Assurances’
investment  strategy: policy of  exclusion, commitment and
selection of investments based on  ESG criteria.
In 2020, CNP  Assurances adopted a plan to phase out
thermal coal,  setting  zero exposure by 2030 in the EU  and
the OECD, and by 2040 elsewhere. This exclusion policy
was 
extended in 2021 and 2022 to include  restrictions on
investments 
in fossil oil and  gas, thus reinforcing its
responsible  investment  strategy.
The due diligence policy is subject to operational oversight
and  implementation by the Investment Department.
Management  committees with the asset management
companies ensure this  regular monitoring. Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1212Sustainable performance
Environmental information
In addition, to  reduce the consequences of climate risks
on 
its insurance business, CNP Assurances has implemented
a global protection approach to incorporate climate risks
through  reinsurance coverage against the risk  of excess
mortality. All causes of excess mortality are covered: this
coverage  provides protection  against  both  pandemics
and  heat  waves.
LBP  AM  has  adopted an exclusion policy  in order to limit
its exposure to issuers whose activities, policies or practices
are not compatible with its vision of a responsible economy.
The policy includes  regulatory,  standards-based  and
sector-specific  exclusions  for  thermal coal (updated  in
April  2021) and the oil and gas sectors (validated in
June  2022). This exclusion  policy was updated in May 2023.
It is validated and updated by the LBP  AM Sustainable
Finance Committee. The ESG Committee is regularly informed
of the  work  carried  out under  this policy, and the GREa T
Committee oversees its implementation. The exclusion policy
applies to all open-ended funds managed by LBP AM and
is available on its website.
As part of the integration of La Financière de  l’Échiquier
into  LBP AM, the  oil and gas  policies are in  the process of
being combined. The other policies (voting, engagement
and  coal) have  been  harmonised.
In addition, LBP AM’s commitment  policy aims  to improve
the climate performance of its portfolios. Through dialogue,
LBP  AM seeks  to better understand the policies and
practices of  the  companies  to improve  the analyses
carried  out by its teams . Through the ESG commitment,
LBP   AM encourages the integration of sustainable
development  matters, including  climate-related matters,
into  companies’ strategies, and setting out robust policies
to help  prevent  ESG risks.  The policy applies  to the two
asset  management companies of LBP  AM (LBP  AM and
La Financière de l’Échiquier(1)). Engagement campaigns
are monitored during weekly ESG management committee
meetings  and,  where applicable, GREaT  committee
meetings. This policy is approved by the Sustainable
Finance  Committee. In particular, the Governance
Committee  approves the development  and updates of
the voting  policy  at Shareholders’  Meetings.
Louvre   Banque  Privée, as part of its discretionary
management, incorporates sustainability risks in accordance
with  the SFDR regulations and Article 29 of the Energy-
Climate  Act.  The  targets  of its ESG  policy are established in
its ESG charter.  The policy is under  the operational
responsibility of the Director of Discretionary Management
and the Chief Sustainability Officer,  who reports to the
Chairman  of the Executive Board. The Executive Board
approves the sustainability roadmap  on an annual basis.
In its management,  the B ank takes into account the
interests of its customers. It aims to reconcile ESG integration
with  the maintenance of  sectoral and geographical
diversification  and the control of sustainability risks. The
main  documents,  such  as the ESG  Charter, the Article 29
report,  the sustainability documents related to each
mandate  (SFDR) and the annual statement of negative
impacts,  are freely  accessible on  its website. [E1_MDR_P_01_06]2.2.1.4 Climate change mitigation 
and adaptation  targets

title: Presentation of decarbonization targets
heading: 2.2.1.4.1 Presentation of decarbonization targets
start_phrase: To monitor and achieve its reduction targets, and in particular the achievement of its “zero net emissions” ambition by 2040, La Banque Postale has developed science-based trajectories.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s sustainable performance and environmental strategy, with emphasis on climate risk management, portfolio decarbonization, governance, methodologies, and progress against targets.

- Climate risk and exclusion policies:
  - CNP Assurances implements global reinsurance to mitigate excess mortality risks (pandemics, heat waves).
  - LBP AM applies and regularly updates an exclusion policy (thermal coal; oil and gas), validated by the Sustainable Finance Committee, overseen by ESG and GREaT committees; applies to all open-ended funds and published online.
  - Integration of La Financière de l’Échiquier into LBP AM: oil and gas policies being combined; voting, engagement, and coal policies harmonized.
  - LBP AM’s engagement policy promotes climate and ESG integration in investee strategies, with campaign monitoring and voting policy governance.
  - Louvre Banque Privée integrates sustainability risks per SFDR and Article 29 LEC, with an ESG charter, defined responsibilities, annual roadmap approval, and public disclosures.

- Operational decarbonization targets (SBTi-aligned, validated March 2024 within La Poste SA scope):
  - 100% renewable electricity by 2030.
  - Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions: -43.6% (2021–2030), excluding CNP Assurances, Banking Advice Line, and La Poste Network buildings.
  - Scope 3 (partial: categories 1 partial, 3, 6, 7): -25% (2021–2030).
  - Targeted absolute reductions by 2030: Scope 1 (-2,219 tCO2e), Scope 2 (-736 tCO2e), Scope 3 partial (-7,757 tCO2e).

- Financed portfolio targets and frameworks:
  - Dual approach using SBTi and NZBA.
  - Real estate and corporate portfolios:
    - Home loans (retail): -73.7% kgCO2e/m² (2022–2035), equating to -53% by 2030 (CRREM 1.5°C; PCAF); new target filed with SBTi in 2024.
    - Commercial real estate: -65% kgCO2e/m² (2022–2030).
    - Large corporate equity and bonds: portfolio “temperature” from +3.14°C (2019) to 2.2°C (2025) for Scopes 1–2.
    - Large corporate medium/long-term loans: 3.14°C (2019) to 2.3°C (2025) for Scopes 1–2.
  - NZBA sectoral targets (Scope 3 Category 15 intensity):
    - Automotive: -7% gCO2e/vehicle.km (2020–2030).
    - Aviation: -56% gCO2e/passenger.km (2020–2030).
    - Cement: -30% kgCO2e/tonne (2020–2030).
    - No exposure to coal; power generation financing limited to renewables; oil & gas policy aligned with a 1.5°C pathway from 2030.
  - Acknowledged trade-off: decarbonization of real estate portfolios may conflict with affordability and inclusion goals (e.g., lending to low-income households and social housing).

- Financed emissions and coverage (as of 30 June 2024):
  - Total measurable Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions: 10,920 ktCO2e; 95% from corporate portfolios, 5% from retail residential real estate.
  - €71bn of exposures covered by SBTi pathways (79% residential real estate; 11% commercial real estate; 7% large corporate equity/bonds and MLT loans; 3% asset/project financing in renewables).
  - Of €106bn eligible for Scope 3 calculation, 67% managed by low‑carbon pathways.

- Subsidiary targets:
  - CNP Assurances:
    - Operations: -50% Scopes 1–2 (2019–2030; location-based).
    - Investment portfolio: net zero by 2050 (NZ AOA), 1.5°C alignment with asset-class targets; coal exit by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (RoW).
    - By 2029: -53% Scopes 1–2 for directly held equities/corporate bonds/infrastructure; -32% for directly owned real estate; -17% carbon intensity for electricity producers by end‑2024.
  - LBP AM (including LFDE): NZAMi commitment; 1.5°C IPCC P2 alignment; milestones—80% of technical reserves aligned by 2030, 100% by 2040, economy-wide neutrality by 2050; SBTi-based validation share methodology.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: implied temperature pathway targeting 1.5°C alignment by 2040 (LEC Article 29-compliant).

- Methodological framework:
  - Use of SBTi, NZBA, PCAF, CRREM 1.5°C, and IPCC SR15 temperature scoring (ROTS).
  - Current strategy based on IPCC SSP1‑1.9 (Paris 1.5°C), with disclosure of any future baseline adjustments.
  - Revised real estate pathways filed with SBTi at end‑2024; broader methodological review planned in 2025.

- Progress against operational targets (selected metrics):
  - Scope 2 decreased 23% from 2023 to 2024, driven by energy efficiency, building management systems, renovations, and renewable electricity sourcing.
  - Scope 1 slightly increased in 2024 due to vehicle fleet; new fleet policy being rolled out.
  - Scope 3 (partial) down 4.9% in 2024 vs 2023.

- Governance and disclosure:
  - Clear committee oversight (Sustainable Finance Committee, ESG Committee, GREaT, Governance Committee).
  - Annual approval of sustainability roadmaps; broad public disclosure of ESG charters, Article 29 reports, SFDR documentation, and adverse impact statements.
text:
2.1.4.1 Presentation of decarbonization  targets
To monitor and  achieve its reduction targets, and in
particular 
the achievement of its “zero net emissions”
ambition  by 2040,  La  Banque  Postale has developed
science-based trajectories.
Operational  scope
For its operational scope, La Banque Postale is committed to:
•sourcing 100%  of its electricity from  renewable sources
by 2030.
•reducing its Scope  1 & 2  GHG  emissions by  43.6% over
the 2021-2030  period.  This commitment  covers GHG
emissions  from the Bank's  vehicle fleet and buildings,
excluding the Banking Advice Line and CNP Assurances.
The 
buildings of the La Poste  Network are not included
in 
this pathway, but within  the scope of the La  Poste
Group Consumer and Digital Services business unit
(BGPN).  This pathway, aligned with  a 1.5°C scenario, was
charted using the Absolute Contraction Approach  (ACA).
The pathway aims to reduce its operational footprint by
2,219 tCO₂e for Scope 1 and by 736 tCO₂e for Scope 2 by 2030;
•reducing 
its emissions by 25% on Scope 3 (partial:
categories 
1 partial, 3, 6 and  7), i.e. an expected reduction
of 7,757 tCO₂e.
La  Banque  Postale’s commitment is part of a scientific
approach. All reduction targets for the operational scope
(i.e. outside Scope 3 Category 15) correspond to the targets
of the SBTi pathway validated in March 2024 for the
La Poste SA scope, which includes La  Banque Postale. The
targets correspond to the implementation of this pathway
for the La  Banque  Postale SA scope. [E1_4_01] [E1_MDR_T_01_13]

Corporate  and Investment Banking portfolios
In the banking sector, carbon-reduction targets can be set
based  either  on asset class (portfolio)  or on the sector of
the activities being financed. Different frameworks and
indicators apply depending on which of these twoapproaches is used.  For reasons of timing and coverage,
La  Banque  Postale has chosen to combine these two
approaches 
by relying on two market initiatives,  the
Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and the Net Zero
Banking Alliance (NZBA).
For its Corporate and Investment Banking activities,
La Banque  Postale SA  undertakes to:
•continue  to finance only those energy projects that are
based on renewable energy ;
•reduce  indirect greenhouse  gas emissions  in Scope 3 –
Category  15, relating to  its portfolio  of home loans for
retail  customers, by 73.7% per sq.m. over the 2022-2035
period to achieve  a 53% reduction per sq.m. by 2030.
This pathway was created using the Global GHG Accounting
and  Reporting  Standard  for  the  Financial Industry
(PCAF)  methodology and the "CRREM 1.5" scenario.
Although  the establishment  of a target for  this asset
class is considered  optional by  the SBTi, the Bank
wished  to propose  one, given  the significant weight of
real estate loans to retail customers in its total financing
technical  reserves. This  target was submitted to the SBTi
for validation in  2024. It replaces the previous target,
validated 
in 2021 for this asset class. This new target
reflects both  a change  in the baseline data due to a
better quality of data on the financed assets,  and the
Bank’s ambition  to align it with a  1.5°C scenario;
•reduce  indirect Scope 3 – Category 15 GHG emissions
from its commercial property portfolio by 65% per sq.m
over the 2022-2030  period ;•align  the temperature of its large corporate equity and
bond portfolio from +3.14°C in 2019 to 2.2°C in 2025
(Scopes  1 and  2).
This pathway was built based on the temperature rating
methodology developed by the SBTi, using the revenue
owned 
emissions temperature score (ROTS) aggregation
option. The scenarios used are those developed in the
IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR15).
•align  the temperature of its medium/long-term large
corporate  loan portfolio  from 3.14°C in 2019  to 2.3°C
in 2025 (Scopes 1 and 2).
This pathway was built based on the temperature rating
methodology developed by SBTi, using the revenue
owned emissions temperature score (ROTS) aggregation
option. The scenarios used are those developed in the
IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR15).
At the  end of  2024,  La  Banque  Postale SA filed revised
pathways for its real estate portfolios (retail customers,

pathways on  the large corporate equity and bond
portfolios and those on the large corporate medium/long-
term loan  portfolios maturing at the end  of 2025.

La Banque Postale SA has filed these pathways with SBTi
as a financial institution, in addition to its contribution to
the pathways  filed  by La Poste SA. As  compliance with the
targets for reducing  the carbon footprint of  financing and
investment portfolios is  essential for a financial institution,
this subject is specifically  monitored in the  context of the
mission-led  Company  commitments.
It should be noted that the decarbonisation  ambitions of
real estate portfolios may prove incompatible with the
accessibility targets of the Group’s  banking  services,  in
particular  with  regard  to home  loans.
Granting loans to low-income households raises the question
of the  financial resources required  to buy  energy-efficient
homes.  The Group’s societal commitment may thus have
a negative effect on the low-carbon pathway of the home
loan  portfolio. The same applies  to financing for social
housing and social landlords, for which the  pace of energy
renovation  of their  stock is  sometimes too slow, even
though  this financial support represents an important
component  of the Group’s positive societal impact. More
details on commitments to social housing operators and
customers  experiencing  financial difficulties are available
in paragraphs 2.3.3.3.1 “Financing  of local authorities,
charities  and the local economic sector” and 2.3.4.5.2
“Actions implemented to  generate  positive impacts”.
This  tension between reducing carbon emissions and the
Group’s  commitment to accessibility  and support for
disadvantaged groups is  a real strategic challenge  that
could  lead to arbitration on a case-by-case basis when
making  loan decisions.
In addition, as part of its  commitment to the NZBA,
La  Banque  Postale , like all the signatory banks, has
established scientifically credible low-carbon  pathways in
relation to  its portfolios,  aimed  at limiting  the rise in  global
temperature to 1.5°C by the  end  of the century. The efforts
to be  made  focus  on the  sectors that emit the most
greenhouse gases (GHG) and play a key role in the transition
to a low-carbon  economy. The NZBA has identified nine
priority sectors: agriculture, aluminium,  cement, coal,  iron
and steel, real  estate, oil  and gas, electricity generation
and  transport.
Among  these sectors, the signatory banks must present
trajectories  for those  to which they are most significantly
exposed.  This commitment complements  and reinforces
the SBTi commitment made by La  Banque  Postale inorder 
to provide a more granular sector-specific dimension,
and an ambition to align with more demanding scenarios.
La Banque Postale is  therefore committed to:
•reducing indirect Scope 3 – Category 15 greenhouse gas
emissions in its automotive sector investments (expressed
in gCO₂eq per vehicle per  kilometre) by 7% over the
2020-2030 period;
•reducing indirect Scope 3 – Category 15 greenhouse gas
emissions in its aviation sector investments (expressed in
gCO₂eq per passenger per kilometre) by 56% over the
2020-2030 period;
•reducing indirect Scope 3 – Category 15 greenhouse gas
emissions  in its cement sector (expressed in kgCO₂eq
per tonne  of cement  produced)  by 30% over  the 2020-
2030 period.
These pathways  were established  based  on a sector-
specific approach using the NACE codes(1)  of the counterparties
in the Corporate portfolio. La Banque Postale has developed
a 
proprietary method based on in-depth analysis of its
counterparties’ climate transition plans and  on the
International Energy Agency (IEA) “Net Zero 2050” scenario.
For 
the coal  sector,  La  Banque   Postale is already in line
with scientific recommendations, as it is not exposed. It is
also already aligned for power generation, as the Bank
only finances  projects based on  renewable energy.
Finally, with regard to the oil and gas sector, the policy it
has implemented guarantees alignment with  the +1.5°C
pathway from 2030 onwards.
The 
first step is to establish and validate these pathways
while  waiting for new and more in-depth work that  will
enable La Banque Postale to reach  its net zero  emissions
by 2040  target.  [E1_4_01] [E1_MDR_T_01_13]  [E1_4_22]
La Banque Postale has established its low-carbon pathways
for financed emissions in the most significant scopes for
which benchmark methodologies exist. This concerns real
estate loan portfolios (residential and commercial), financing
and investment loans to companies (excluding real estate).
Large companies account for most of the emissions measured.
Retail  banking technical reserves  (excluding real estate),
equity securities and exposures  to sovereigns  (sovereign
bonds,  technical reserves at the Banque de France and
centralisation 
of passbook savings accounts) are currently
excluded from this  scope.  [E1_4_18]

Environmental information
The financed emissions that La Banque Postale is able to
calculate  for Scope 3 Category 15 total 10,920 KtCO2e as of
30 June 2024. 95%  of these financed  emissions come from
its corporate  portfolios  (large corporates,  SMEs, VSEs,
commercial  real estate and financing of renewable energy
projects), while the remaining 5% are financed emissions
linked to the  retail banking portfolio, and more specifically
to residential real  estate.
At 30 June 2024, the total technical reserves covered by
low-carbon  pathways amounted to €71 billion. 79% of
these  technical reserves are related  to the residential real
estate  portfolio, 11%  to the  commercial real estate portfolio,
and  7% to the equity and bond portfolios and large
corporate  medium/long-term loans, while 3%  are related
to the  asset  financing  portfolio  and renewable  energy-
based  projects.
Targets  of La Banque  Postale’s  subsidiaries
La  Banque  Postale’s subsidiaries have also established
reduction  targets:
CNP  Assurances SA and its subsidiaries have committed
to reducing direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions
(Scopes  1 and  2 based  on location) related  to their  internal
operations by  50%  between  2019 and  2030. This target is
aligned  with  the IPCC 1.5° pathways.
As a member of the Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance since 2019,
CNP 
Assurances is committed to achieving carbon neutralityin its investment portfolio by 2050. CNP   Assurances has
established 
decarbonization trajectories for the investment
portfolio 
with an alignment with the  1.5 ° C trajectories and
specific targets for certain asset classes (equities, bonds,
real estate, electricity producers) held by CNP Assurances.
and  its French  subsidiaries. CNP  Assurances also aims to
completely exit the coal sector by 2030 in  the EU and the
OECD, and by  2040 in the rest of  the world.
Within its investment scope, CNP  Assurances SA and its
French subsidiaries aim to:
•reduce  the Scope  1 and 2 carbon  footprint  of the directly
held equity, corporate bonds and infrastructure portfolio
by 53% by the  end  of 2029;
•reduce  the Scope  1 and 2 carbon  footprint  of the directly
owned real estate portfolio via club deals and the Lamartine
fund by 32% by the end of  2029;
•reduce  the carbon intensity of electricity producers in
which 
they are direct shareholders or bondholders by
17% by the end of  2024.
CNP   Assurances has not set itself a low-carbon pathway
for the other asset classes or for Scope 3 emissions for the
other companies in  which it  invests due to the lack of
methodologies or sufficient data to process them.
Nevertheless,  the shareholder engagement policy  covers
all three scopes and  covers the strategy of companies in
their value chain.

LBP   AM joined the Net  Zero Asset Manager Initiative
(NZAMi)  in 2021 to align the management  of its assets
with  a pathway  for reducing  greenhouse gas emissions in
line with  the  Paris  Agreement  target, and aims to align its
investments with a 1.5°C pathway using the IPCC P2
scenario
(1). In 2022, LBP AM established and published an
ambitious decarbonisation trajectory for the investment
portfolios 
managed by its  two management companies,
LBP   AM and Tocqueville  Finance, including open-ended
and  dedicated funds for all eligible asset classes.
This   pathway, aiming for carbon neutrality by 2050, was
extended  in 2023 to La Financière de l’Échiquier, also a
member  of NZAMi.
The main  milestones  of this trajectory  are:
•by 2030, alignment of 80% of technical reserves  on a
carbon pathway  compatible with the Paris Agreement;
•by 2040,  alignment  of 100%  of technical  reserves;
•by 2050, the initiative estimates that companies will have
deployed their targets, therefore enabling a transition  to
carbon neutrality in the economy.
The NZAMi  provides for  a review of the Net Zero target
every five years, or in the  event of a change in investment
profile. The methodology used is  based on  the framework
established by the Science Based Targets initiative for Financial
Institutions (SBTi). The approach consists of measuring
the share of technical reserves invested in companies
whose  decarbonization  trajectory  is validated by the SBTi.
For discretionary  managem ent, Louvre  Banque  Privée’s
pathway was expressed as an “implied temperature rise
pathway”,  with a target of portfolios aligned with the
targets of the Paris Agreement, i.e. a maximum increase of
1.5°C  in 2040.  This  method  was chosen in accordance  with
the methodologies authorised by Article 29 of the Energy-
Climate law (LEC).  [E1_4_01]  [E1_MDR_T_01_13] [E1_4_22]Methodological  details
The starting points chosen for  the various pathways were
those 
considered to be the most relevant with regard to
the date of the work to establish the pathways, the
availability 
of data to carry out the calculations and the
scenarios used.  [E1_4_20]
In the event of  an adjustment in the baseline value set for
its 
targets in the coming years, La  Banque  Postale will
specify this in its sustainability report. 
[E1_4_21]
Currently, La  Banque  Postale ’s decarbonisation strategy
and the resulting  actions are  based on  the new IPCC SSP1-
1.9 scenario, in line  with the 1.5°C  target under the Paris
Agreement. This  scenario envisages a 50% probability of
limiting  the  increase  in temperatures to  2°C and 1.5°C by
2100 respectively, compared  to the pre-industrial era , and
a peak in global  emissions in 2020.  It therefore has a
reduced financial impact. [E1_4_24]

title: Detail of decarbonization targets
heading: 2.2.1.4.2 Detail of decarbonization targets
start_phrase: Additional information on GHG emissions and the actions implemented to achieve the targets is available in Sections 2.2.1.5 “Decarbonisation levers and action plans” and 2.2.1.7 "Group greenhouse gas emissions".
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s environmental strategy and performance within its 2024 Universal Registration Document, covering net-zero commitments, methodology, operational and financed emissions targets, progress, and decarbonisation levers.
- Net-zero and alignment initiatives:
  - LBP AM joined the Net Zero Asset Managers initiative (NZAMi) in 2021; decarbonisation trajectory set for LBP AM and Tocqueville Finance (open-ended and dedicated funds, all eligible asset classes), extended in 2023 to La Financière de l’Échiquier.
  - Milestones: 80% of technical reserves aligned with a Paris-compatible carbon pathway by 2030; 100% by 2040; economy-wide carbon neutrality by 2050.
  - Five-year review cycle under NZAMi; methodology anchored in SBTi for Financial Institutions, tracking the share of technical reserves invested in SBTi-validated companies.
  - Louvre Banque Privée uses an “implied temperature rise” approach targeting 1.5°C alignment by 2040, per Article 29 of France’s Energy-Climate law.
- Methodology and scenarios:
  - Targets set using the IPCC SSP1-1.9 (1.5°C-aligned) scenario; assumes a 2020 peak of global emissions and lower financial impact; baseline choices reflect data availability and relevance; any future baseline changes will be disclosed.
- Operational emissions targets and performance (SBTi scope, excluding Banking Advice Line and CNP Assurances):
  - 2021 baselines and 2030 targets: Scope 1: 5,089 tCO2e to 2,870 (-43.6%); Scope 2: 1,689 to 953 (-43.6%); partial Scope 3: 31,026 to 23,270 (-25%). Average annual cuts: S1/S2 -4.84%, S3 -2.78%.
  - 2024 progress vs 2023: Scope 2 down 23% (exceeds 2030 trajectory) due to building energy efficiency (BMS, renovations) and renewable electricity; Scope 1 slightly up from vehicle fleet, with a new policy being rolled out; example of footprint reduction via site consolidation in Orléans.
- Financed emissions targets (sector intensity and portfolio temperature):
  - Sector intensity targets/pathways:
    - Residential real estate (retail): 2022 baseline 28 kgCO2e/m²; 2024 at 28.5; 2030 target 13.16 (-53%). New 2035 SBTi submission targets -73.7% over 2022–2035 with -53% by 2030.
    - Commercial real estate: 2022 baseline 32.6; 2024 at 29.6; 2030 target 11.41 (-65%).
    - Automotive: 2020 baseline 111 gCO2e/vehicle-km; 2024 at 173; 2030 target 103.23 (-7%).
    - Aviation: 2020 baseline 143 gCO2e/passenger-km; 2024 at 103; 2030 target 62.92 (-56%).
    - Cement: 2020 baseline 511 kgCO2e/tonne; 2024 at 375; 2030 target 357.7 (-30%).
  - Pathways: Real estate and corporate portfolios aligned to SBTi; automotive, aviation, cement aligned to NZBA using IEA NZ2050 scenarios. Data primarily from counterparties’ annual reports; sectoral proxies used as needed; intensities for some issuers above sector averages; 2024 car and airline portfolio intensities increased vs 2023 but remain aligned with decarbonisation trajectories.
  - Portfolio temperature alignment:
    - Large corporate equities and bonds (customer Scopes 1&2): improved from 3.1°C (2019) to 1.6°C (2024), outperforming the 2025 target of 2.19°C.
    - Medium/long-term loans to large corporates (customer Scopes 1&2): 3.1°C (2019) to 2.4°C (2024), on track to meet 2.32°C by end-2025.
- Data and coverage developments:
  - Enhanced methodology and precision in calculating real estate intensities through broader collection of energy performance assessments; amount of technical reserves analyzed rose 15.4% (30 Jun 2024 vs 31 Dec 2023) due to better data processing; challenging real estate market limited shifts toward better energy ratings.
- Renewable energy commitments and targets:
  - 100% renewable electricity for major sites since 2015; green electricity share rose again in 2024; target remains 100% by 2030 (92.5% in 2024).
  - Mission-led financing goal: €5.6bn in renewable energy project financing by 2025; €5.039bn originated in 2024; energy financing limited to renewables.
- Decarbonisation levers and action plans:
  - Actions span own operations and Corporate & Investment Banking; detailed Transition Plan to be published in 2025.
  - Operational levers include buildings, vehicles, digital footprint, business travel and commuting; Sustainability Department oversees implementation.
  - Buildings: rollout of BMS; energy renovations (LEDs, replacing gas boilers with more efficient tech); renewable electricity with guarantees of origin; collaboration with La Poste Immobilier; 16 energy audits at key sites; measures continue through 2026.
  - 2030 buildings abatement target: reduce 1,732 tCO2e from 2021 level (3,972 tCO2e), via renovations and BMS/impact fund (-1,212), efficient use (-173), and decarbonising residual consumption (-346).
- Key quantitative snapshots:
  - Renewable electricity supply: 95.2% (2022), 92% (2023), 92.5% (2024), 100% target (2030).
  - Renewable energy financing originations: €4,586m (2023), €5,039m (2024), €5,600m target (2025).

2.1.4.2 Detail  of decarbonization targets
Additional  information on GHG emissions and the actions
implemented  to achieve the targets is available in
Sections 2.2.1.5 “Decarbonisation levers  and action plans”
and  2.2.1.7  "Group greenhouse gas emissions" .
Targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions
Decarbonisation targets for La Banque Postale's operational
activities are detailed here in the scope of SBTi commitments,
which excludes the Banking Advice Line and CNP Assurances.
La  Banque  Postale is making  progress in reducing its
greenhouse  gas emissions in accordance with its targets
as validated  by the  SBTi initiative.
Scope  2 emissions decreased by 23% between 2023 and
2024,  exceeding the target for 2030. This decrease is the
result  of energy  efficiency actions carried out with the
deployment  of technical  building  management systems,
energy renovation  and the supply of renewable electricity.
It includes, for  example,  the  impact  of the release  in 2024
of an energy-intensive  30,000 sq.m.,  replaced by a 10,000
sq.m.  energy-efficient building for the Orléans Customer
Relations  and  Expertise  Centre.Scope  1 emissions increased slightly in 2024 in line with
the increase in vehicle emissions. The new policy concerning
the vehicle  fleet  is gradually  being  implemented.
Decarbonisation targets concerning financed activities
are expressed in intensity or in portfolio temperature. They
correspond  to La  Banque  Postale SA's SBTi pathways for
the real estate sector  and the corporate  portfolio, and to
the NZBA commitments for the  automotive,  aviation  and
cement sectors.

heading: 2.2.1.5.1 Operational scope
start_phrase: Reducing the carbon footprint of operational activities is based on targeted actions for buildings, vehicles, the digital footprint, and business travel and commuting.
summary:
- Portfolio alignment and temperature targets: 2024 portfolio temperature for large corporate equities and bonds (Scopes 1 & 2) is already below the 2025 target; large corporate medium/long‑term loans (Scopes 1 & 2) are on track to reach 2.32°C by end‑2025.

- Renewable energy commitments:
  - Operations: 100% renewable electricity for major sites since 2015; share of green electricity rose again in 2024; on an SBTi pathway (excluding CNP Assurances and the Banking Advice Line); target 100% renewable electricity by 2030 (2024: 92.5%).
  - Financing: Mission-led target of €5.6bn in renewable energy project financing by 2025, with progress of €4.586bn in 2023 and €5.039bn in 2024; only finances renewable energy projects.

- Decarbonisation strategy and governance: Group-wide levers across operations and Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB), implemented by La Banque Postale and subsidiaries (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée); actions driven by the Sustainability Department; full Transition Plan to be published in 2025.

- Operational scope action plans and 2030 targets (vs 2021 baseline):
  - Buildings (target: –1,732 tCO2e from 3,972 tCO2e): energy audits, BMS rollout, energy renovation (LEDs, replacing energy‑intensive equipment), efficient use, and decarbonising residual consumption; 98% renewable electricity under La Poste Immobilier contract; actions continue through 2026; Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund mobilised.
  - Vehicles (target: –1,223 tCO2e from 2,806 tCO2e): full transition of internal fleet to electric/plug‑in hybrids by 2030; eco‑driving training; potential fixed compensatory allowance for company vehicles; deployment in subsidiaries.
  - Travel and commuting (target: –6,566 tCO2e from 26,264 tCO2e; 17% modal shift, 16,224 SOV trips avoided): prioritize public transport (incl. park‑and‑ride in soft mobility pass), active modes (bike purchase/rental and repair support), car‑sharing and car‑free days, remote meetings, and train over air; “soft mobility pass” since 2023 (50% public transport reimbursement + up to €220/year sustainable mobility package); teleworking policy (2 fixed days/week + 10 floating days/year) with measured GHG savings (~6 tCO2e/year per 2023 survey insight).
  - Digital: “Responsible digital by design” with ESG criteria embedded in IT procurement; responsible design of solutions; reduction of workstation and infrastructure footprint (incl. data centre cooling); 30% hardware reuse, ending hard‑drive destruction; ongoing awareness and full digital footprint measurement across IT and related building infrastructure.
  - Responsible purchasing and suppliers: RFAR-certified approach to mitigate environmental impacts; enhanced supplier carbon footprint measurement focused on top 50 emitters; contributions of digital and responsible purchasing to overall targets not yet allocated.

- Corporate & Investment Banking decarbonisation:
  - Sector policies: strict exclusions for coal, oil, and gas with divestment commitments by 2030.
  - Green/impact financing: expansion of green and impact loans (e.g., interest‑free energy renovation loans, impact real estate loans); Group connection to Caisse des Dépôts’ €100bn commitment to France’s environmental transition (2023–2028).
  - Stewardship: active shareholder engagement and voting by LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier to align investees with Net Zero pathways.
  - ESG integration: systematic E, S & G criteria in investment decisions using tools like LBP AM’s GREaT methodology; alignment with decarbonisation objectives; further details to come in the 2025 Transition Plan.
text:
2.1.5.1 Operational scope
Reducing the  carbon  footprint of  operational activities is
based on targeted actions for buildings, vehicles, the digital
footprint,  and business travel and commuting.
The actions are driven and  monitored by the Sustainability
Department  and implemented by  the departments in
question.
Buildings
La  Banque  Postale carries out energy efficiency actions
with  the deployment of  technical building management
systems, energy renovation (replacement of energy-intensive
equipment, installation of LEDs) and the supply of renewable
electricity.The 
2030 target is to reduce the carbon impact  by
1,732 tCO₂e compared to the 2021 base year (3,972 tCO₂e), by:
•renovating 
the existing real estate  portfolio to reduce
energy consumption (reduction of 1,212 tCO₂e by 2030),
including  performing  energy audits, deploying the
Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund and installing the
Technical Building Management System (BMS);
•efficient use to limit energy consumption (reduction of
173 tCO₂e by 2030);
•decarbonising residual consumption (reduction of 346
tCO₂e  by 2030), with specific action plans  for the sites
with the  highest emissions.
La Banque Postale, in conjunction with La Poste Immobilier,
La Poste Group's real estate company responsible for the
technical management  of its buildings, has implemented
energy saving initiatives by optimising the operation of its
facilities, mainly by managing  heating, air conditioning
and  ventilation equipment. 16 energy audits were carried
out on the main Customer Relations and Expertise Centres
(CRECs) in order to identify ways to optimise energy
consumption 
with the aim of facilitating the transition to
less carbon-intensive energy. S ince 1 January 2022,
La Banque Postale has entered into an electricity contract
with certificates of guarantee of origin (electricity production
from 
renewable energy in France) for  98% of its supply
within the scope managed by La  Poste Immobilier.
Technical Building Management (BMS) is being rolled out
on La  Banque  Postale ’s sites, with a  priority  on the  sites
emitting  the most CO₂. In addition, as part of regular
maintenance 
operations, La Banque Postale and La Poste
Immobilier are systematically seeking energy performance.
For 
example, when replacing technical equipment (mainly
gas boilers), the choice is made  for the less energy-
intensive equivalent. The implementation of actions to
improve  the energy  performance and efficiency  of
buildings will continue until 2026.

Vehicles
A commitment to transition to plug-in hybrid or electric
vehicles  has  been  put in place,  aiming  in particular  to
conv ert La Banque  Postale’s entire internal fleet by 2030.
In addition to the deployment of this vehicle policy,
dedicated support is planned for eligible employees.
The 2030  target is to reduce the carbon impact by
1,223  tCO₂e compared to  the 2021 baseline year
(2,806  tCO₂e),  by:
•continuing  to deploy the vehicle policy for the
La Banque Postale SA scope (reduction of 841 tCO₂e by
2030)  with, in particular, the continuation of eco-driving
training , as well as the possibility of extending the fixed
compensatory  allowance  to company vehicles;
•deploying  a vehicle policy for the subsidiaries concerned
(reduction  of 383 tCO₂e by  2030).
La  Banque  Postale is continuing  to replace the vehicle
fleet  to reach 100% electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles in
the service  and  company vehicle fleet.
Travel
Sustainable mobility initiatives favour  public transport for
business 
travel and offer incentives such as the sustainable
mobility  package for commuting. Teleworking is also
encouraged.
The 2030  target is to reduce the carbon impact by
6,566  tCO₂e compared to the 2021 baseline year
(26,264   tCO₂e). This  target is  accompanied by  a modal
shift target of 17% (i.e. 16,224 single-occupancy vehicles
targeted),  and  is broken  down  as follows:
•the use of public transport (target of 2,298 tCO₂e reduction
in CO2 by 2030) by including park and ride subscription
fees 
in the "soft mobility pass", or by launching discussions
on the terms  of additional  financial incentives;
•developing  the use of  active modes (target  of 591 tCO₂e
reduction  by 2030) by facilitating the purchase or rental
of bicycles, including bicycle  repair and maintenance
costs into the "soft mobility pass", and by organising
campaigns  to promote  cycling,  including in urban areas;
•optimising motorised travel (target of 2,495 tCO₂e reduction
by 2030), mainly by organising car-free days and
implementing a car-sharing system between employees;
•supporting  the rollout of working from home (target of
1,182  tCO₂e  reduction by  2030).
La Banque Postale has  been managing arrangements for
business  travel since 2021 in  order to reduce the
associated carbon footprint, and opting for remote
meetings  wherever  possible. When business travel isnecessary, train travel (and more generally, the use of
public 
transport) should be used over air travel. For
commuting, 
La  Banque  Postale has been offering its
employees the "soft mobility pass" since 2023.  This is a
comprehensive offer that includes compensation of 50%
of 
the amount of the public transport subscription, the
sustainable mobility  package  of up to €220 per year and
the dissemination of useful information on commuting
and  employee safety.  In addition, La  Banque  Postale’s
home working agreement allows employees who are
eligible to benefit from 2  fixed  days of home  working  per
week in their roles, as well as a fixed rate of 10  annual
floating  days of  home working. This measure saved an
average of 6 tCO₂e per year according to the working
from home survey conducted in 2023.
Digital
Digital  efficiency  actions are  in place, in particular on the
responsible design of solutions, reducing the consumption
of IT  architecture and increasing the reuse of  equipment.
La Banque Postale aims to deploy a “responsible digital by
design” 
strategy, which incorporates ESG from the IT
consultation  and tendering phase.  Teams from the Bank
and  Network Information  Systems  Department (DSIBA)
work with the Purchasing Department to set ESG criteria.
An assessment grid of criteria is systematically included in
the specifications, and the main requirements are set out
in the contract.
Work 
is also being done on the responsible design of
digital solutions to ensure that they are always useful,
usable, used and  reusable.
In the use phase, targeted actions are carried out to reduce
the environmental footprint  of workstations (efficient
purchases and hardware settings), and on infrastructure
to manage consumption related to data centre  cooling.
Lastly, for end  of life, La Banque Postale is increasing the
reuse of its hardware (currently 30% of hardware is reused)
by making changes to the way in which asset managers
work, for example by discontinuing the destruction of
hard drives. In addition, awareness-raising among IT
sector  stakeholders and IT users is currently being rolled
out within La Banque  Postale ’s business  lines.
La  Banque  Postale  measures and  manages its  digital
footprint to guide the effectiveness of its actions. This
footprint 
includes the greenhouse gas emissions related
to its IT equipment, including computers, printing systems,
hubs, routers, switches and other network equipment,
telephony,  video projection equipment  and data centre
hardware, and building infrastructure such as air conditioning,
security and lighting.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1292Sustainable performance
Environmental information
Other  levers  in the operational  scope
La Banque  Postale  has  launched a  responsible purchasing
approach,  consolidated and formalised as part of its RFAR
(Supplier 
Relations and Responsible Purchasing) certification,
which aims to  reduce the  negative impact of purchases
by La Banque Postale and its suppliers on the environment,
as 
well as encouraging positive impacts. La Banque Postale
is also  providing  more  detailed measurements of the
carbon  footprint of its suppliers, specifically targeting its
50 suppliers  with  the highest emissions.
The transition plan also includes additional actions for
better  management of the various components of the
operational  footprint.
The breakdown of the contributions of digital technology
and  responsible purchasing to  decarbonisation targets in
the operational scope has not yet been assessed. [E1_1_03]

summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document covering Sustainable performance and Environmental information, focused on the Group’s transition plan and decarbonisation actions across business lines and operations.
- Operational scope levers: Formalised responsible purchasing under RFAR certification to reduce environmental impacts; enhanced supplier carbon-footprint measurement targeting the 50 highest-emitting suppliers; ongoing work to better manage the operational footprint; contributions from digital and responsible purchasing not yet quantified.
- Corporate & Investment Banking: Strict sectoral exclusion/divestment policies for coal, oil and gas by 2030; expansion of green and impact financing (e.g., energy-renovation loans, impact real estate loans); active shareholder engagement via LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier; systematic ESG integration using LBP AM’s GREaT methodology; actions aligned with the Group Transition Plan (published 2025).
- Retail Banking 2030 plan: 
  - Internal systems: qualify consumer loans; calculate carbon footprints for consumer and very small business loans; deploy decision-support tools; explore virtual cards and process dematerialisation.
  - Customer offers: finance sustainable consumption (energy renovations, low-emission vehicles); promote responsible savings with ESG-based segmentation and emissions disclosure; launch impact passbook; expand housing renovation support with partnerships and potential offers for collective housing; dedicated solutions for professionals (impact account, Bpifrance green loans, advisory).
  - Governance/tools: carbon footprint measurement for residential property; use of Impact Weighting Factor in mortgage granting; sustainability-preference questionnaires; portfolio allocation/management rules.
- Corporate & Local Development Banking 2030 plan:
  - Monitoring: calculate financed and facilitated emissions; industrialise data tools (e.g., Impact Weighting Factor); assess company and national transition plans.
  - Portfolio steering: transition-linked granting/pricing criteria; track green bond impact; optimise/rotate low-carbon energy loan portfolios to free capital for new green assets.
  - Offers: support commercial property renovation; tailored ESG services and coordination (green loan structuring); impact factoring; impact banking and e-payments (citizen term account); PV leasing for the public sector.
  - Enablers: staff training needs review; sectoral policies and responsible financing charters; carbon footprint measurement for key portfolios.
- Private Banking (Louvre Banque Privée) 2030 plan:
  - Asset management: consider quantitative constraints on alignment to progressively exclude non-aligned issuers; extend exclusions to conventional fossil fuels; mandates meet SFDR Article 8 and monitor negative impact metrics; active issuer dialogue; sectoral disengagement policies; SRI “citizen” range.
  - Residential real estate: automate retrieval of energy performance data (EPD/DPE) and CO2 by class; integrate energy efficiency into pricing; align mortgage policy with the 2021 Climate & Resilience law for rental properties (e.g., class G renovation commitments).
- Asset Management (LBP AM) 2030 plan: Define and regularly review Net Zero alignment targets (80% of total assets by 2030 toward 100%); align voting/engagement with Net Zero; continue fossil energy policy updates; embed decarbonisation objectives in SRI segmentation and day-to-day management using research tools; transparent reporting.
- Insurance (CNP Assurances) 2030 plan:
  - Investments: implement exclusions (coal, oil, gas); strengthen financed-emissions coverage and ESG integration across asset classes; include transition-plan analysis in engagement; pursue green investments (bonds, certified buildings, forests, green infrastructure); set a new green investment target by 2026 after reaching €30bn in 2025; prior green (2019) and sustainable (2023) bond issues.
  - Insurance business: integrate climate into strategy and incentives; expand sustainable unit-linked products; progressively green Euro funds; improve customer non-financial disclosures; sustainable retirement savings offer.
- Support functions: All corporate functions (governance, HR, finance, sustainability, risk, data/IT, compliance, legal, public affairs, reporting, communications) to develop their own transition plans and provide training/awareness to embed sustainability in practices.
- Measurement approach: Quantifying GHG reductions beyond operational scope remains difficult due to data gaps and sector variability; impacts are currently assessed qualitatively with annual management to adjust actions; the transition plan will be updated within three years as data and methodologies improve.

environmental, social and governance criteria in investment
decisions  ensures alignment  with decarbonisation
targets.  Tools such as LBP  AM’s GREaT methodology

title: Support functions
heading: 2.2.1.5.3 Support functions
start_phrase: All of La Banque Postale Group’s support functions will be called on to support the decarbonisation efforts implemented by each activity, including the following functions: governance, human resources, finance, sustai nability, risks, data and information technology, compliance, legal, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, reporting and communications.
summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document on sustainable performance, environmental information, and insurance.
- Role of support functions: All support areas (governance, HR, finance, sustainability, risk, data/IT, compliance, legal, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, reporting, communications) are mobilized to back decarbonization and must create their own transition plans; awareness and training are used to embed sustainable behaviors.
- Measuring decarbonization: Quantifying GHG reductions beyond operational scope is challenging due to data gaps and sector variability; current impact assessment is largely qualitative, with projects to improve measurement; annual management reviews guide course correction; the transition plan will be updated within three years as data/methods improve.
- Investment activities (near-term actions): Update exclusion criteria per evolving climate scenarios; expand financed-emissions coverage; deepen ESG integration across asset classes; continue property-specific decarbonization work plans; factor companies’ transition plans into shareholder engagement; set a new green investment target by 2026 after meeting €30bn outstanding by 2025.
- Insurance business (near-term actions): Broaden sustainable unit-linked offerings; progressively increase sustainability of legacy Euro funds; enhance non-financial (sustainability) disclosures to customers on their investments.
- CNP Assurances 2030 action plan – investments: Enforce exclusion policies for coal, oil, and gas; apply active ownership (voting and dialogue) to drive transition; select investments using ESG criteria across listed/unlisted equity, bonds, infrastructure, real estate, and forests; scale green investments (green bonds, certified buildings, forests, green infrastructure); noted green bond (2019) and sustainable bond (2023) issuances to finance transition.
- CNP Assurances 2030 action plan – insurance: Embed climate in business strategy (market positioning, incentives); provide ongoing sustainability information at subscription and annually; offer sustainable retirement savings built on ESG-driven pillars.
- Reporting references: Includes tagged indicators/citations (e.g., E1_1_03, E1_3_01, E1_MDR_A_01_12, E1_3_03, E1_3_04, E1_4_23) indicating alignment with standardized sustainability reporting frameworks.

2.1.5.3
Support  functions
All of La Banque Postale Group’s support functions will be

title: Contributions to decarbonisation actions
heading: 2.2.1.5.4 Contributions to decarbonisation actions
start_phrase: As part of the transition plan, the precise quantification of actions and associated GHG reductions remains a significant challenge beyond the operational scope.
summary:
- Mobilization of support functions for decarbonization: governance, HR, finance, sustainability, risk, data/IT, compliance, legal, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, reporting, and communications each to develop their own transition plans, supported by awareness and training initiatives.
- Decarbonization actions and measurement: current impact assessment beyond the operational scope is primarily qualitative due to data gaps and sector variability; annual monitoring used to adjust actions; the transition plan will be updated within three years as data and methodologies improve.
- Planned actions in investment and insurance:
  - Investments: update exclusion criteria in line with climate scenarios; expand financed emissions coverage; deepen ESG integration across asset classes; continue property-specific work plans; embed transition-plan analysis in shareholder engagement for high-sustainability sectors; set a new green investment target by 2026 after achieving €30bn by 2025.
  - Insurance: broaden sustainable unit-linked offerings; enhance sustainability of legacy Euro funds; improve non-financial information shared with customers.
- CNP Assurances 2030 action plan:
  - Investments: exclusion policies for coal, oil, gas; active shareholder engagement (voting, dialogue); ESG-based selection across listed/unlisted, real assets; green investments (green bonds, forests, certified buildings, green infrastructure); green bond (2019) and sustainable bond (2023) issuances to fund transition.
  - Insurance business: integrate climate change into strategy and incentives; provide sustainability information at subscription and annually; offer sustainable retirement savings based on ESG pillars.
- Financial resources and budgeting:
  - 2025–2029 transition projects phased into annual budgets; 71% of 2025 strategic projects already budgeted.
  - Dependencies include stable ESG data supply, vehicle fleet electrification, and cost-bearing capacity; no current warnings on capacity.
  - Carbon Budget oversight within La Poste Group for operational decarbonization.
  - 2025 plan: 2,188 tCO₂e reduction for €7.2m net CapEx/OpEx (€10.7m gross, including €3.1m for CNP Assurances; €3.5m costs avoided via space optimization). Allocation: 69% buildings (energy efficiency, CNP IT server outsourcing), 31% vehicles (fleet greening). In 2024, €3.4m for 139 vehicles and €5.8m for buildings.
- Consideration of locked-in (irreducible) emissions:
  - Operational: future emissions tied to IT servers and building depreciation are not a material transition risk (<1% of Group footprint) at Group level; CNP Assurances estimates ~2,691 tCO₂e/year locked-in for its scope.

summary:
