title: Consideration of irreducible emissions
heading: 2.2.1.5.6 Consideration of irreducible emissions
start_phrase: The strategic and investment choices made today can lock in the pathway of a company’s GHG emissions for years to come.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale Group’s environmental transition planning, financing, and regulatory alignment (2025–2029), with emphasis on 2025 budgets, decarbonisation levers, locked-in emissions, and EU Green Taxonomy metrics.
- Transition plan financing and execution:
  - Annual integration of projects; for 2025, 71% of strategic projects already budgeted.
  - Key dependencies: stable ESG data supply, vehicle fleet electrification, and cost absorption; no identified warnings on capacity.
  - Annual budgeting will assess dependency of actions on available resources (financial, human, etc.).
  - Monitoring via La Poste Group’s annual Carbon Budget, validated by the Board on 13 June 2024.
- 2025 decarbonisation budget and impacts (operational scope):
  - Targeted reduction: 2,188 tCO₂e in 2025; full benefits accrue in future years.
  - Net CapEx/OpEx: €7.2m; gross spend €10.7m (incl. €3.1m for CNP Assurances); €3.5m in avoided expenses (e.g., freed-up m² at La Banque Postale).
  - Allocation: 69% to buildings (energy efficiency at La Banque Postale, outsourcing CNP Assurances’ IT servers); 31% to vehicles (fleet greening).
  - Real estate CapEx based on a multi-year estimate (Nov 2024) refined in Q1 2025 by La Poste Immobilier.
  - 2024 indicative spend: €3.4m for vehicles (139 vehicles ordered) and €5.8m for buildings.
- Consideration of irreducible/locked-in emissions:
  - Operational scope assets (IT servers, building depreciation) generate future emissions but represent <1% of Group footprint; not treated as a transition risk to 2030–2050 and not quantified at Group level.
  - CNP Assurances: estimated locked-in emissions ≈2,691 tCO₂e/year (servers and buildings).
  - Financed portfolios: locked-in emissions not yet quantifiable due to:
    - Need for counterparties’ own locked-in emission data (expected via CSRD from 2025).
    - Uncertain asset lives and loan prepayment dynamics preventing robust loan-level lock-in assessments.
  - No significant CapEx in economic activities related to coal, oil, or gas (all reported as €0).
- Link to the European Green Taxonomy:
  - Transition plan CapEx/OpEx for banking activity not directly captured by EU 2021/2178 KPIs; effects materialize through portfolio exposures.
  - Methodology aligns with regulation: assessment via counterparties’ turnover/CapEx alignment for general financing and project analysis for specialized financing.
  - At 31 Dec 2024: Green Asset Ratio (GAR, consolidated prudential scope) = 5.7% (€10.3bn) based on turnover.
    - Total assets: €321.3bn; covered assets (denominator): €180.1bn.
    - Assets analyzed for eligibility: €148.0bn; eligible assets: €92.5bn.
    - GAR contribution breakdown highlights: Real estate households 4.9 pts; unallocated exposures 0.8 pt.
  - Data limitations constrain taxonomy alignment assessment; enhanced data collection is underway per the transition plan.
  - Further detail provided in Section 2.2.6 “European Green Taxonomy.”
text:
2.1.5.6 Consideration of irreducible emissions
The strategic and investment choices made today can
lock in the pathway of a company’s GHG emissions for
years to  come. The concept of locked-in emissions helps to
focus on this risk by identifying future GHG emissions
likely 
to be  caused  by the Company’s main assets, or by
products sold during the lifetime of these assets.
In seeking to apply this concept to its financial institution
activities, La Banque Postale reached the following conclusions:
Within 
the operational scope: the energy consumption of
IT servers and the depreciation of La  Banque  Postale’s
buildings 
generate future emissions associated with the
Company’s assets. However, in line with  the strategic
choices linked to locked-in emissions, as the operational
scope  constitutes less than 1% of La  Banque  Postale
Group’s 
carbon footprint, they are  not considered as a
transition 
risk by 2030-2050. They were therefore not
quantified at Group level.
CNP  Assurances has estimated locked-in emissions for its
scope  of approximately 2,691 tCO₂e per year related to the
consumption of IT servers and the depreciation of buildings.
Concerning 
the portfolios of financed activities,
La Banque Postale is not yet in a position to quantify the
locked-in emissions associated with its portfolios for two
main reasons:
•firstly,  the locked-in emissions should include the
locked-in  emissions  of portfolio companies. These are
not yet  available and will be published in the CSRD
publications of these  companies  from 2025;
•secondly, the life of an asset,  particularly in a portfolio of
loans, is uncertain, and this volatility does not allow
these  loans to  be considered as “locked-in”. Indeed, a
company 
or a retail customer can choose different
repayment terms  and can pay off a loan at any time.
While it is possible to estimate the evolution of the
portfolio 
with an average repayment term, it becomes
uncertain whether a specific loan term is associated
with an asset or company.  [E1_1_07]
La Banque Postale Group has not, moreover, invested any
significant  CapEx in connection with economic activities
related to coal, oil or gas.
(1) Figures  October  2024.
(2) The Carbon  Budget,  which is  rolled out annually, identifies all of La Poste Group’s decarbonisation levers and values the emissions to be
reduced  annually by combining the financial resources  (OpEx and CapEx) pledged by all activities committed to achieving the Group 2030
pathway.  This tool was validated by the Board of Directors of La Poste Group on 13 June 2024.

title: Link with the European Green Taxonomy
heading: 2.2.1.5.7 Link with the European Green Taxonomy
start_phrase: In the context of the banking activity, the CapEx and OpEx related to the action plans of the Bank’s transition plan are not directly affected by “the key performance indicators provided for by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178”.
summary:
- Link with the European Green Taxonomy:
  - The Bank’s transition plan CapEx/OpEx are not directly covered by KPI rules under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178; impacts are instead reflected through portfolio exposures.
  - La Banque Postale calculates and publishes its Green Asset Ratio (GAR) and related taxonomy-alignment metrics, using pillars such as counterparties’ turnover and CapEx alignment for general financing and project-level analysis for specialized financing.
  - At 31 Dec 2024, regulatory GAR (prudential scope) is 5.7% (€10.3bn) based on turnover, with key contributors including Real Estate Households (4.9 pts) and 0.8 pt unallocated.
  - Scope and methodology highlights: total assets €321.3bn; covered assets €180.1bn (excluding sovereigns, central banks, trading book); assets analyzed for eligibility €148.0bn; eligible assets €92.5bn. Covered assets further exclude companies not subject to NFRD and derivatives in the banking book. Ongoing data collection aims to address current data limitations on taxonomy alignment.

- Climate change adaptation:
  - Operational adaptation work underway with EcoAct to assess site adaptability and inform a geographically tailored adaptation plan; no standalone adaptation policy yet—work aligned with Caisse des Dépôts and set to begin in 2025.
  - CNP Assurances is executing adaptation plans to mitigate physical climate risks: reducing exposure across sovereigns, corporates, real estate, and forests; integrating climate risk into reinsurance strategy with close monitoring of treaty changes; and reinforcing resilience via regularly updated business continuity plans.

- Energy consumption and mix (Group, buildings and vehicles):
  - Reporting distinguishes fossil (natural gas, non-renewable electricity, fuel oil, propane, petrol, diesel, district heating—classified as fossil in 2024 due to unavailable source split) and renewable (purchased/produced renewable electricity, firewood, steam, cooling).
  - 2024 totals: total energy 188,360 MWh; fossil 90,125 MWh (48%); renewable 98,235 MWh (52%).
    - Of renewables: renewable fuels 2,393 MWh; purchased/acquired renewable electricity, heat, steam, cooling 95,400 MWh; self-generated non-fuel renewable 442 MWh.
  - Renewable energy production managed at Group level: 1,086 MWh total in 2024, from solar on Lemnys D and Nantes sites and 821 MWh from CNP Assurances (partly fed back to the grid).
text:
2.1.5.7 Link with the European Green Taxonomy
In the  context  of the banking  activity, the  CapEx and OpEx
related to the action plans of the Bank’s transition plan
are 
not directly affected by “the key performance indicators
provided  for by Commission  Delegated Regulation (EU)
2021/2178”.  However, the actions concerning the financing
and  investment portfolios are reflected in the evolution of
the Bank’s  exposures.
In accordance with the requirements of the European
Green Taxonomy, La Banque Postale calculates and publishes
the proportion of its exposures to activities that comply
with the criteria established by the regulation, in particular
the Green  Asset  Ratio or GAR.
These  analyses are conducted based on a number of
pillars, in particular on the basis of turnover and CapEx
aligned  with counterparties for general financing, and on
an analysis  of projects  for specialised  financing.In line with other regulatory  and internal initiatives,
La  Banque  Postale relies on these components to
strengthen its commitments  to sustainable finance.
Additional information on  the work carried out and the
quantitative indicators relating to the Green Taxonomy is
available in Section 2.2.6  “European Green Taxonomy”.
[E1_3_07]
At 
31 December 2024, La  Banque  Postale’s regulatory
green asset ratio (consolidated prudential scope) was 5.7%
(€10.3 billion)  based  on turnover.
The GAR obtained for this  financial year reflects the lack of
reliable data to determine whether customers’ projects
are aligned with  the Taxonomy.
In order to provide a more comprehensive view of the coming
financial years, data collection work is in progress, in line
with the  work included in  the Bank’s transition  plan.
Additional information on the GAR is available in Section 2.2.6
“European Green Taxonomy”. [E1_1_08]

title: Actions for climate change adaptation
heading: 2.2.1.5.8 Actions for climate change adaptation
start_phrase: Regarding climate change adaptation, in the operational scope, La Banque Postale is currently working with EcoAct to establish the degree of adaptability of its sites.
summary:
- Climate change adaptation: La Banque Postale is working with EcoAct to assess the adaptability of its sites and build a geography-based adaptation plan to strengthen climate resilience by understanding vulnerabilities to climate hazards and regional interactions. A dedicated adaptation policy for La Banque Postale is not yet in place; work coordinated with Caisse des Dépôts will begin in 2025.
- CNP Assurances’ adaptation measures: Reduces exposure to physical climate risks in investments (states, companies, buildings, forests), integrates climate risks through reinsurance coverage management and close monitoring of treaty changes, and updates its business continuity plan to enhance resilience to extreme events.
- Energy consumption and mix (2024): Reporting covers buildings and vehicles across La Banque Postale Group. Fossil sources include natural gas, non-renewable electricity, fuel oil, propane, petrol, diesel, and district heating (classified as fossil due to group methodology and lack of source breakdown in 2024). Renewable sources include purchased/produced renewable electricity, firewood, steam, and cooling. Renewables account for 52% of the energy mix; fossil fuels 48%. Key figures: total energy consumption 188,360 MWh; fossil 90,125 MWh; renewable 98,235 MWh (of which 2,393 MWh renewable fuels; 95,400 MWh purchased renewable electricity/heat/steam/cooling; 442 MWh self-generated non-fuel renewable).
- Renewable energy production (2024): Managed at group level, including solar at Lemnys D and Nantes and 821 MWh from CNP Assurances; some output is fed back to the grid. Total renewable energy produced: 1,086 MWh.
text:
2.1.5.8
Actions  for climate  change adaptation
Regarding  climate change adaptation,  in the operational
scope,  La Banque Postale is currently working with EcoAct
to establish the degree of adaptability of its sites. The target
is to build an adaptation plan to strengthen the Group’s
climate  resilience based on  its different geographical
locations  by integrating an in-depth understanding of its
vulnerability to climate hazards and all regional interactions. 
La  Banque  Postale has not yet established a policy
specifically dedicated  to the challenges of climate change
adaptation . This is, however, part of the work carried out
by Caisse  des Dépôts , and  will begin in 2025.
CNP   Assurances  is implementing various  adaptation
plans to reduce the  risks related to climate change, in
particular  exposure to physical climate risk that could
have  consequences for human health and an  increase in
the loss ratios of insurance contracts. The  main actions
concern the reduction  of the  exposure to  climate hazards
of investments in States, companies, buildings or forests,
as well  as the  integration of  climate  risks  into  its global
protection approach via the management of reinsurance
coverage  and a specific close monitoring of  changes in
reinsurance  treaties. Internally, climate risk is managed by
regularly  updating the business continuity plan to ensure
resilience in the face of extreme climate events. [E1_MDR_A_01_12]

heading: 2.2.1.7.1 Greenhouse gas emissions by scope
start_phrase: In order to manage its low-carbon pathway, La Banque Postale Group measures the GHG emissions relating to all of its activities across its entire value chain.
summary:
- Purpose and perimeter: La Banque Postale Group presents its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the full value chain to manage its low‑carbon pathway, with results shown for the entire Group (not limited to the SBTi operational target scope).
- Targets context: Operational SBTi targets (excluding CNP Assurances and LCB and only partly Scope 3) and financed emissions targets (intensity/portfolio temperature) are referenced but not detailed here; see Section 2.2.1.4.2.
- 2024 scope expansion and comparability: Operational Scope 3 coverage was broadened in 2024 (purchased goods/services across all groups, capital goods, upstream energy, plus first-time calculations for waste and business travel), improving transparency but limiting year‑on‑year comparability.
- Entities covered for financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15): La Banque Postale SA, CNP Assurances, Louvre Banque Privée, LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier; methodologies are entity‑specific and detailed in the methodological section.
- Key 2024 GHG results by scope:
  - Scope 1: 17,544 tCO2e (‑11% vs 2023: 19,699).
  - Scope 2: 5,219 tCO2e (location‑based); 1,865 tCO2e (market‑based, ‑50% vs 2023: 3,705).
  - Scope 3 total: 62,945,457 tCO2e, including:
    - Cat. 1 Purchased goods/services: 227,595 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 2 Capital goods: 84,824 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 3 Fuel/energy‑related (upstream): 2,036 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 5 Waste: 1,637 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 6 Business travel: 2,442 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 7 Employee commuting: 29,218 tCO2e (stable vs 2023).
    - Cat. 15 Investments: 62,597,706 tCO2e, of which banking 10.92 Mt, insurance 18.919 Mt, wealth and asset management 32.759 Mt.
  - Total Group GHG: 62,968,220 tCO2e (location‑based) and 62,964,867 tCO2e (market‑based).
- CNP Assurances specificities: Only counterparties’ Scopes 1 and 2 included in the table; for information, additional financed Scope 3 upstream/downstream for listed equities, corporate bonds and infrastructure is estimated at 82 MtCO2e.
- Emissions intensity metrics:
  - Total GHG intensity: 1,532 tCO2e per €m of Group income (both location‑ and market‑based).
  - Financed emissions intensity (per covered exposures): banking 132; insurance 399; asset management 396; not calculated for Wealth Management due to portfolio size.
- Methodology and reporting scope: Environmental reporting includes consolidated subsidiaries and those under operational control; subsidiary 115K excluded (immaterial). Emission factors are supplied by La Poste Group based on ADEME references and updated annually; CNP reports Scopes 1–2 directly in tCO2e using ADEME factors.
- Uncertainty approach: Qualitative levels (low/medium/strong) tied to data type and extrapolation; strong uncertainty for monetary factors and indirect sources (e.g., Scope 3 Cat. 15). ADEME factor uncertainties are not directly applied except for monetary factors.
- Cross‑references: Detailed methodologies in Section 2.2.1.7.3; decarbonisation targets in Section 2.2.1.4.2; glossary of CSR terms on page 808.
text:
2.1.7.1 Greenhouse gas emissions by scope
In order to  manage its low-carbon pathway, La Banque Postale
Group measures the GHG emissions relating to all of its
activities  across  its entire  value chain.
Targets  for the operational scope are defined based on
the SBTi scope (excluding CNP Assurances, LCB and only
partially taking into account the Scope 3 categories). They
are therefore not detailed  in the tables below, which cover
the entire  La Banque  Postale  Group scope.
The targets for  financed emissions (Scope 3 Category 15)
are also  not  detailed  in this paragraph, as they are defined
in terms  of intensity or portfolio  temperature. Information
on targets is presented in  Section 2.2.1.4.2 “Detail of
decarbonisation  targets”.The methodology used for each  category is explained in
Section 2.2.1.7.3 “Methodological information”.
For 
the sake of transparency, the total financed emissions
(Scope 3 Category 15) cover La  Banque  Postale SA,
CNP  Assurances,  Louvre Banque Privée, as well as LBP AM
and La Financière de l'Échiquier for assets under management.
However, the methodologies used are specific to each
entity, 
and are  detailed in the section  on methodological
information, in particular concerning the portfolios of
technical  reserves amounts covered and the counterparty
scopes  taken into account.
For CNP Assurances , only Scopes 1  and 2 of counterparties
are taken into account in the table below. For information,
the 
upstream and downstream Scope 3 financed emissions
for listed shares, listed corporate bonds and infrastructure
is estimated by CNP Assurances at  82 million tCO2e based
on the information available  from its data suppliers.
In 2024, for the first time,  La  Banque  Postale calculated an expanded scope for its operational Scope 3 emissions. This
indicator is therefore more transparent and representative of actual emissions, although it does not allow for inter-annual
comparability.

title: GHG emissions intensity
heading: 2.2.1.7.2 GHG emissions intensity
start_phrase: The GHG emissions intensity is calculated on the basis of the total GHG emissions presented above, divided by La Banque Postale Group's total income(1).
summary:
- Section focus: Sustainable performance and environmental information from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, centered on GHG emissions intensity and methodology.
- Definition of GHG emissions intensity: total Group GHG emissions divided by total income; highlights that financed emissions are the dominant component, requiring a specific financed-emissions intensity metric.
- Portfolio-specific intensity approaches:
  - Banking portfolio: intensity includes counterparties’ Scopes 1, 2, and 3; residential real estate exposures use Scopes 1 and 2 only.
  - Insurance portfolio: intensity includes Scope 3 upstream and downstream financed emissions for comparability (notably 82 million tCO2e for listed equities, listed corporate bonds, and infrastructure).
  - Asset Management: includes counterparties’ Scopes 1, 2, and 3; Wealth Management excluded due to small size.
- 2024 scope and boundary updates:
  - Environmental reporting covers consolidated subsidiaries and non-consolidated entities under operational control; consolidation rules detailed elsewhere.
  - Subsidiary 115K excluded in 2024 due to very small size and office move; no material impact on comparability.
  - Major expansion of Scope 3 coverage with La Poste Group:
    - Category 1 (purchased goods and services) extended to all purchase groups.
    - Category 2 (capital goods) added.
    - Category 3 (upstream energy-related emissions) added.
    - Categories 5 (waste) and 6 (business travel) calculated for the first time.
  - Scope 3 Category 15 (investment emissions) consolidates data from CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée (including La Financière de l’Échiquier), and La Banque Postale SA.
  - These methodological changes limit year-on-year comparability for the affected categories.
- Methodology and emission factors:
  - Emissions calculated using La Poste Group emission factors based on ADEME benchmarks; updated annually and applied consistently across entities.
  - Exception: CNP Assurances reports its own tCO2e figures using ADEME factors.
- 2024 GHG emissions intensity results:
  - Total GHG intensity per income: 1,532 tCO2e/€m (both location-based and market-based).
  - Financed emissions intensity per covered exposures:
    - Banking scope (Scopes 1–3): 132 tCO2e/€m.
    - Insurance scope (Scopes 1–3): 399 tCO2e/€m.
    - Asset management scope (Scopes 1–3): 396 tCO2e/€m.

GHG  emissions intensity
The GHG emissions intensity is calculated on the basis of
the total GHG emissions presented above, divided by
La  Banque Postale Group's total income(1). The financed
emissions represent  a significant  weighting compared to
the other  categories of emissions.
For a bancassurance provider,  this  metric must therefore
be supplemented by the intensity specifically linked to the
financed  emissions, and which is calculated as the total
financed emissions for  the exposures  covered.
For the banking  portfolio, this  intensity is calculated by
including  Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions for counterparties,
with the exception of exposures to residential real estate,
where only Scopes 1 and 2 are considered according to
marketplace practice.

by adding Scope 3 counterparty components for the
purpose 
of comparability (Scope 3 upstream and downstream
financed  emissions for listed  equities, listed corporate
bonds  and  infrastructure, 82 million  tCO 2e).
For 
the Asset Management portfolio, the intensity is calculated
by including  counterparty Scope 1,  2 and  3 emissions.
Due to the size of the portfolio, the intensity is not calculated
for the Wealth  Management activity.

title: Methodological information
heading: 2.2.1.7.3 Methodological information
start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group’s environmental reporting scope for the calculation of GHG emissions includes subsidiaries consolidated in the Group’s financial statements and non-consolidated subsidiaries over which La Banque Postale has operational control.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale Group’s 2024 environmental reporting on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, intensity metrics, methodologies, Scope 1–3 coverage (including financed emissions), data sources, limitations, and climate-related projects.

- GHG emissions intensity:
  - Overall intensity calculated as total Group GHG emissions divided by total income; financed emissions dominate the footprint.
  - Portfolio-specific intensities provided to complement the Group-level metric:
    - Banking (financed emissions, Scopes 1–3 for counterparties; Scopes 1–2 only for residential real estate): 132 (per covered exposure).
    - Insurance (financed emissions incl. counterparty Scope 3 for comparability): 399.
    - Asset management (financed emissions incl. counterparty Scopes 1–3): 396.
  - Gross emissions intensity relative to income: 1,532 tCO2e/€m (identical location- and market-based).

- Reporting scope and 2024 methodological updates:
  - Environmental scope includes consolidated subsidiaries and non-consolidated entities under operational control; minor entity (115K) excluded without affecting comparability.
  - 2024 expansion of operational Scope 3 with La Poste Group:
    - Category 1 (purchases) extended to all spend groups; inclusion of Category 2 (capital goods) and upstream energy in Category 3; Categories 5 (waste) and 6 (business travel) now calculated.
    - These changes break comparability with prior year for affected categories.
  - Emission factors primarily from ADEME via La Poste Group; updated annually; CNP Assurances reports Scopes 1–2 directly.

- Scope 1 and 2 specifics:
  - Scope 1: company fleet fuel, building thermal energy (gas, fuel oil, propane, wood) and, new in 2024, refrigerant leaks.
  - Scope 2: electricity and district heating; both market- and location-based methods applied. Renewable electricity backed by guarantees of origin; supplier-specific factors used market-based.
  - Data gaps addressed via surface area extrapolation for select French service entities (Django, Lyon Financial Centre, Poitiers Financial Centre).
  - Contractual instruments coverage:
    - 87% of Scope 2 emissions covered by renewable electricity contracts.
    - 100% via bundled energy with attributes; 0% via non-pooled instruments.

- Scope 3 coverage, exclusions, and methods:
  - Included: Categories 1 (purchases), 2 (capital goods), 3 (fuel- and energy-related activities), 5 (waste), 6 (business travel), 7 (employee commuting), and 15 (investments).
  - Excluded/not yet reported: 4 (upstream transport/distribution—work in progress for cash transport), 8 (upstream leased assets—none reallocated), 9 (customer travel—unable to calculate 2024), 11 (use of products—method alignment ongoing), 12 (end-of-life of sold products—work ongoing, with bank card LCA noted), 10/13/14 (not applicable).
  - Methods rely on monetary emission factors (ADEME), allocation keys, extrapolations; lower reliability vs. primary data. Only 2% of operational Scope 3 uses primary data (fuel/energy-related activities, waste, business travel).
  - Employee commuting based on a 2023 mobility survey; ADEME factors applied with modal shift assumptions.
  - Data collection aligns with sustainability reporting period; no significant events affecting financed emissions; timing notes provided where reporting dates differ.

- Financed emissions (Scope 3 Category 15):
  - La Banque Postale SA scope includes residential real estate (home loans), commercial real estate, and corporate portfolios; excludes retail technical reserves (non-real estate), equities, and sovereign exposures.
  - Coverage at 30 June 2024: 26% of total technical reserves (€83bn).
  - Methods aligned with PCAF, SFDR, and Pillar III; financed share typically based on revenue (enterprise value preferred but harder to obtain).
  - Corporate emissions data prioritized from reported sources; otherwise estimated by Bloomberg/Sustainalytics; if unavailable, PCAF sector factors applied. Real estate emissions based on EPC/energy data.
  - Scope 3 of counterparties dominates financed emissions and carries higher uncertainty (e.g., for Large Corporates, ~82% of financed emissions are counterparty Scope 3).
  - Subsidiary methodologies:
    - CNP Assurances: covers equities, corporate bonds, sovereigns (domestic/Scope 1), real estate, and direct infrastructure; uses S&P Trucost and reported data; ~€331bn (80%) in scope, €254bn (60%) with data; estimates Scope 3 financed emissions for listed equities/bonds/infrastructure at ~82.3 MtCO2e; acknowledges double counting and disclosure gaps.
    - LBP AM: uses MSCI (and Carbon4Finance for LFDE); asset eligibility 74% (LBP AM) and 92% (LFDE); calculates carbon intensity/footprint incl. Scopes 1–3; data as of 31 Dec 2023.
    - Louvre Banque Privée: direct securities via Sustainalytics; UCITS via SFDR PAI published by managers at end-2024.
  - Financed emissions for LBP SA updated semi-annually; figures as of 30 June 2024.

- Biogenic emissions:
  - Not quantified for Scopes 1–3 in 2024.

- GHG reduction/offset projects:
  - Value chain: no carbon absorption projects; internal “Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund” supports emission-reduction initiatives (buildings, mobility). CNP Assurances’ forests absorbed 483,653 tCO2 in 2024 (not used for offsetting).
  - Outside value chain: since 2015, participation in La Poste Group’s “Climate + Regions” supporting French Low Carbon Label projects (mainly forestry). At La Banque Postale, 20 projects (10 certified; 2 already generating credits); also supports methodology development (e.g., hedges). Estimated sequestration: 11,455 tCO2e over project lifetimes; average cost €29/t; no reduction projects included in this portfolio.
text:
Methodological  information
La 
Banque Postale Group’s environmental reporting scope
for the calculation of GHG emissions  includes subsidiaries
consolidated in the Group’s financial statements and non-
consolidated  subsidiaries over which La  Banque  Postale
has operational control. The scope of financial consolidation
is 
detailed in Note 3.1 Consolidation scope and rules in
Section 
5.2 “Notes to the consolidated financial statements”
of the Universal Registration Document.
In 
2024, the GHG emissions of  the subsidiary 115K were  not
included due to its small size (eight employees in flex offices)
and  its move at the end of 2024 to a co-working space
entirely  managed by La Poste Immobilier. These changes
have no significant impact on the inter-annual comparability
of the disclosed  emissions.
The scope of emissions included in Scope 3 also changed
significantly in  2024.
The methodological work carried out with La Poste Group has
allowed an extension of operational Scope 3 coverage:
•extension of the scope covered for Scope 3 Category 1
(purchased  goods  and  services) to  all purchase  groups;
•inclusion of emissions related to Scope 3 Category 2
(capital goods);
•inclusion of upstream emissions related to energy
consumption in  Scope 3 Category 3.
In addition, Categories  5 (waste) and 6 (business travel)
were calculated for the first time  by La  Poste Group  on
behalf of La Banque  Postale  Group.
For Scope 3  Category 15 investment emissions, the
consolidated data of CNP  Assurances, LBP  AM and
Louvre 
Banque Privée (including La Financière de l’Échiquier)
are taken into account with those of La Banque Postale SA.
These 
methodological changes do not allow comparability
with the previous year for the categories mentioned. [E1_6_14]
The methodology 
for calculating  La  Banque  Postale’s
greenhouse  gas (GHG) emissions is based on the emission
factors  provided by La Poste Group, which are themselves
based 
on ADEME’s benchmarks. These factors are updated
annually and applied to all entities to ensure data consistency
and traceability  across the  Group.
For Scopes 1 and 2, an exception is made for CNP Assurances,
which 
sends its emissions in tonnes of CO2 equivalent
directly to La  Banque  Postale Group in accordance with
the carbon footprint structure. The  emission factors used
are those of ADEME,  updated  annually.

Environmental information
Scope  1 emissions represent direct emissions from fixed or
mobile facilities located within  the organisational scope.
For La Banque  Postale Group, these are emissions related
to the fuel consumption of vehicles in the owned or
operated internal fleet, and the energy consumption of
buildings  (excluding  electricity  and  district  heating).
For vehicle travel emissions, CO₂ emissions are calculated
on the basis of the volumes of fuel consumed (gasoline
and  diesel). The emission factors are then applied to this
consumption  to  establish the associated  emissions.
For  building emissions, the consumption of natural gas,
domestic 
fuel oil, propane gas and wood energy for heating
is converted into CO₂ emissions using ADEME emission
factors. 
For the first time, in 2024, fugitive emissions related
to refrigerant  leaks  were also  included.
Scope 2 emissions represent indirect emissions associated
with the production  of electricity, heat or imported steam
for the organisation’s activities. For La Banque Postale Group,
these are emissions related to electricity  and district heating
consumption. Emissions related to self-generated renewable
energy from  solar  panels  on buildings are  also  included.
For the calculation of Scope 2 emissions according to the
market-based  methodology,  a specific  emission factor is
applied  depending on the source of electricity consumed.
Regarding  the consumption of  renewable electricity, the
emission factor for electricity from renewable sources is
provided  by the  energy supplier  as part  of the  system  of
guarantees  of origin. If there  are several energy suppliers,
the emission factor is the average of the factors provided
by the energy suppliers weighted according to the
supplier  mix.  For non-renewable  electricity  consumption,
the associated  emission factor corresponds  to the energy
mix of the country  concerned.
The calculation of Scope 2 emissions according to the
location-based methodology is done  by converting all
electricity  consumption,  renewable  and  non-renewable,
into GHG emissions using the emission factors of the
countries’ average  energy mix.
Emissions related to district heating are calculated by applying
ADEME’s specific emission factor for the network in question,
based  on the  local consumption of La   Banque  Postale’s
administrative and commercial buildings.
To estimate the energy consumption of the buildings of
certain La Banque Postale entities for which this data was
not available, we used a surface area-based extrapolation
method. This method,  established at  La Poste  Group level,
applies only to entities located in France with a service
activity. The energy consumption of buildings is thus
estimated  on the  basis of La  Poste  Immobilier’s energy
mix per square  metre.
For 2024, data has been extrapolated for the following entities:
•Django  (225 sq.m.);
•Lyon  Financial  Centre (9, 229 sq.m.);
•Poitiers  Financial  Centre  (1,026  sq.m.).
The calculation methodology for Scope 3 emissions is detailed
below  in the section: Focus on  Scope 3 emissions. [E1_6_15]The period for collecting data on GHG emissions is identical
to the operational scope sustainability reporting period.
Concerning financed  emissions, when the reporting date
differs from 31 December 2024, this is indicated in the
Scope  3 Category 15 methodological notes for the relevant
entities.  For this category of emissions, no significant
events or changes in circumstances were identified during
the time  period  under consideration. [ E1_6_16]
Focus on scope  2 emissions - contractual instruments
In 
order to reduce the emissions related to its energy
consumption (Scope 2), La Banque Postale Group has  entered
into 
a number of contracts for electricity from renewable
sources 
100% covered by the system of guarantees of
origin,  primarily for its Biôme and ICV B2 sites. [E1_6_19] [E1_6_23]
The 
GHG emissions covered by a contractual instrument
correspond  to the emissions  from the consumption of
renewable electricity purchased with guarantees of origin
in relation to the total Scope  2 energy  consumption.
Focus  on Scope 3 emissions
The Scope 3 categories of GHG emissions included in the
inventory are as  follows:
•Category 1:  Purchases;
•Category 2: Capital  goods;
•Category 
3: Fuel- and energy-related activities (not
included in  Scopes  1 and  2);
•Category 5: Waste generated  in operations;
•Category 6:  Business travel;
•Category 7:  Employee commuting;
•Category 15: Investments.  [E1_6_27]
Some  categories of S cope 3 have been excluded:
•Category 4: “Upstream  transportation and distribution”:
work is in progress to establish the  applicability of
the  calculation of emissions in this category to cash
transportation;
•Category 
8: “Upstream leased assets”:  at the  end of the
alignment workshops carried out, La  Poste Group did
not 
reallocate any emission amounts to La Banque Postale’s
activities in this  category;

•Category 
9 “Customer travel”: emissions include customer
travel  to post offices based on an estimated share of
travel 
related to banking transactions. This share is estimated
by La Poste  Group and could  not be calculated in 2024;
•Category  11: “Use of  products”: work between
La  Banque   Postale and La   Poste is  in progress  on the
methodological alignment of the calculation of GHG
emissions  associated with this category. It should be
noted  that the Bank’s products are mainly services
provided  to customers  and that Scope 3 Category 15
emissions are calculated;
•Category  12: "End-of-life treatment of  sold products":
La  Banque   Postale is  not  in a position  to publish  the
2024  GHG emissions associated  with the end-of-life
treatment  of sold  products. Work must be continued to
produce this data, specifically in connection with the
footprint  of bank cards where a life cycle analysis has
been carried out. The total bank card footprint is published
in Section 2.1.6.1 “The  impact-awareness culture at the
heart of the mission-led  company”;
•Categories 10 “Processing of sold products”, 13 “Downstream
leased  assets” and 14 “Franchises”: these categories  are
not applicable to the activ ities of La  Banque  Postale
Group,  which sells  its products  to direct users, and
which  already records the footprint of GHG technical
reserves leases granted to Business customers in Scope 3
Category 15, and whose activities do not include franchises.
[E1_6_26]
Methodology for estimating  Scope 3 emissions
The calculation of Scope 3 emissions has several limitations.
Emissions related to Categories 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 are calculated
at La  Poste Group  level and are then reallocated to
La Banque Postale Group. Scope 3 emission measurement
methods 
require the integration of assumptions, allocation
keys, extrapolation and monetary factors in order to
compensate  for the  lack of actual and  operational data.
This method, although accepted by the GHG Protocol, has
a lower  level  of reliability than the use of actual data, so
La  Poste Group  continues to  work on improving the
method  for the  coming years in  order to increase the level
of reliability  of Scope 3 emissions.
More  specifically, for  each of the categories included in
Scope 3:
Operational Scope  3:
•Category  1 “Purchases”: emissions  related to purchases
of goods  and  services  correspond  to emissions  not
included  in the  14 other Scope 3 categories. Calculations
are made on the  basis of expenses  identified via the
consolidated financial statements at La  Poste Group
level.  These expenses, expressed in euros, are grouped
by purchase category so  that they can  be converted into
tCO₂e  by  applying average  sector-specific  emission
factors from the ADEME  database. This methodology
was applied by La   Banque  Postale Group  for the first
time  in 2024.  To calculate  the emissions in this  category,
CNP Assurances breaks down its general operating expenses
into  12 categories based on its Purchasing information
systems, and applies the  monetary emissions factors
from  ADEME. For this  reason, the figures  related to the
GHG  emissions estimates for this  Scope 3  category may
be different in the  CNP Assurances sustainability report;•Category  2 “Capital goods”: the data is taken from the
assets 
recognised in the consolidated financial statements
of 
La Poste Group for La Banque Postale Group entities.
The 
gross acquisition  value in euros of the asset is used,
then, as for Category 1,  these values are first sorted into
the purchasing category before being converted  into
tCO₂e using the corresponding ADEME factor. Emissions
are allocated in full to the year of acquisition of the fixed
asset. 
CNP  Assurances uses the carbon footprint
methodology ©, and  amortises emissions over the  life of
the assets, which differs from the GHG  Protocol method,
which does not provide for amortisation and recognises
all emissions in the year of acquisition. For this  reason,
the figures related to the GHG emissions estimates
for  this Scope 3 category may be different in the
CNP  Assurances  sustainability  report;
•Category 3 “Fuel- and energy-related activities not included
in Scope 1 or  Scope 2”: emissions are calculated by
applying the upstream phase of the emission factors to
the Group’s energy and fuel consumption;
•Category  5 “Waste”: emissions are calculated on the
basis of the weight of waste collected  by the  Group. The
emission factors used are those of the ADEME (average
end-of-life emission factors);
•Category 6 “Business travel”: e missions  are  calculated
based  on data provided by travel agencies. This data
relates to the kilometres travelled by employees during
business trips made in France  and other countries by
train, plane  and  by car , if travelling in a short-term rental
vehicle. To calculate emissions in this category, CNP Assurances
uses a single emissions factor for short -, medium- and
long-haul flights. For this reason, the figures related to
the GHG emissions estimates for this Scope 3 category
may  be different in the CNP  Assurances sustainability
report;
•Category 7 “Commuting”: data on commuting is taken
from 
the 2023 La Banque Postale Group mobility survey
conducted  with IFOP. This survey was sent to all
La Banque Postale and Ligne Conseil Bancaire employees
(30,045 
employees) and recorded 9,445  respondents.
The survey carried out in 2023 took into account the
relocation of the CNP  Assurances ’ head office. When
calculating the  commuting footprint, the ADEME
emissions  factors are used (updated in 2023 when
necessary). 
For internal combustion vehicles, the same
methodology  as for electric mobility  is applied  as the
emissions factor is only for the fuel item. As a result, for
electric mobility such  as electric  bikes or scooters, the
emissions  factor is negligible and is  set to 0. For electric
vehicles, the emissions factor is only for the use phase.
The 
modal shift assumptions, as well as the associated
carbon  footprint reduction targets,  are consolidated on
the basis of  the analysis  of the responses to  the mobility
survey and the shift potential expressed by employees,
as well as on the data obtained from the mobility
studies published by  ADEME.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1412Sustainable performance
Environmental information
Scope  3 Category  15 Investments :
This  item corresponds to financed emissions. It includes
the direct and  indirect emissions  of La  Banque  Postale
Group’s  counterparties. To date, the portfolios included in
the 
Scope 3 Category 15 calculation for La Banque Postale SA
are 
"residential real estate" (home) loans (excluding subsidiaries),
"commercial real estate" loans and the Corporate portfolio.
Retail  banking technical reserves (excluding real estate),
equity  securities  and  exposures  to sov ereigns (sovereign
bonds,  technical reserves  at the  Banque de France and
centralisation  of passbook savings  accounts) are currently
excluded from this  scope. At 30 June 2024, La Banque Postale
SA calculated its  financed emissions  on 26%  of its total
technical reserves, i.e. €83 billion (see infographic Financed
emissions
 in Section 2.2.1.4.1 “Presentation of decarbonisation
targets”).
The 
calculation of emissions financed by La Banque Postale
SA includes  Scopes 1 and  2 of the "residential real estate"
and "commercial real estate" portfolios, and takes into
account  direct and indirect emissions in the Corporate
scope  when  the data is available.
Scope 3 of  financed emissions, i.e. Scope 3 of La Banque Postale
SA's  customers, which presents the highest level of
uncertainty  due  to a higher proportion  of extrapolated
data,  is also the one that has the most substantial
weighting  in the  total financed emissions. By way of
illustration,  at 31  December 2023, the emissions of the
Large Corporates scope can be divided into 18% generated
by the  Scope  1 and 2  emissions  from  La Banque Postale’s
counterparties,  while 82% of the  total of these financed
emissions correspond to Scope 3 emissions from customers.
The carbon accounting of banks is standardised  by the
PCAF (Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials)  and by
regulations (SFDR, Pillar III).  The calculation formulas
depend on the asset classes and are essentially composed of
two 
factors: asset emissions and the portion attributable
to the Bank  (financed  portion).
For the Corporate scope, La Banque Postale uses the data
provided  by Bloomberg, Sustainalytics  and ADEME on
corporate Scopes 1, 2 and 3, prioritising the use of published
emissions , if there are any. In the  absence of published
data,  emissions estimated by the data providers’ models
are used. Finally, if  there is no other information, sector-
specific  PCAF emissions factors are  used, subject  to the
availability of the NACE sector  code and revenue.
With   regard to the real estate scope, GHG emissions are
calculated  based on the collected or estimated energy
performance  diagnos tic.
To calculate the portion financed by the Bank, most
standards, including the FBF, recommend using the enterprise
value, which makes it the most common approach.
As  enterprise value is difficult  to collect,  revenue is
currently the data used. The  financed portion is therefore
calculated  as the ratio of  exposure to the Company’s
revenue.  For La  Banque  Postale SA, Scope 3 Category  15
information is  calculated  half-yearly. The information
disclosed in this report is dated  30 June  2024.Concerning Scope 3 Category 15, the subsidiaries apply
the following  methodologies:
•CNP Assurances: the measurement of financed emissions
covers equities and corporate bonds, sovereign  bonds,
real estate as well as direct  infrastructure.
CNP  Assurances ' financed emissions include:
•Scope 1 and 2 emissions for  directly or indirectly held
listed equities and bonds invested in the euro, capital
and unit-linked  portfolios;
•Scope  1 and 2 emissions for directly held infrastructure
invested in the euro, capital  and  unit-linked portfolios;
•Scope  1 and 2 emissions for directly or  indirectly held
real estate assets (excluding debt) invested in  the
euro, equity and unit-linked portfolios;
•domestic emissions (Scope 1) for directly or indirectly
held sovereign bonds invested in the euro, capital and
unit-linked portfolios.
Thus, 
€331 billion (80%) of investments are included, of
which €254  billion (60%) have available  data.
Scope 3 financed emissions have many limits. Scope 3 is still
not widely disclosed by issuers and is often based on
estimates, introducing a significant margin of uncertainty.
In addition, the same emissions are counted several times
among 
different issuers of the same value chain, leading
to an overestimation of total emissions. Scope 3 financed
emissions for listed equities, listed  corporate bonds and
infrastructure are estimated by CNP  Assurances at
82.3  million  tCO₂e.
Carbon  footprint  of the corporate  and infrastructure  portfolio :
The data required to calculate absolute investment emissions
are Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions data provided by S&P Trucost
for listed companies, and emissions published in the
annual 
reports for infrastructure. S&P Trucost provides
data reported by companies and/or estimates.
CNP  Assurances uses the latest available information.
Thus, absolute emissions at 31 December 2024 are calculated
based 
on the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of companies
in 2023. CNP   Assurances estimates the greenhouse gas
emissions  of the portfolio companies without restating
any 
duplication between Scopes 1, 2 and 3, and relates
them to the market value of the portfolio. The measurement
is 
carried out on all  listed shares  and bonds, regardless of
the method  of ownership  (direct  or indirect).
The calculation formula used, in line with NZAOA and SFDR
recommendations,  corresponds to the sum of the market
value 
of the investment over the value of the company
concerned, multiplied  by the Company's  GHG emissions.142 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Environmental information
Carbon  footprint  of the sovereign  portfolio : the data
necessary to calculate the absolute emissions of the
sovereign  portfolio is the estimated  domestic  emissions
data  provided by the UNFCC, as well as the Gross
Domestic  Product  (GDP) by purchasing  power parity of
each country, as provided by the World Bank. The measurement
is carried out on all sovereign bonds, regardless of the
method  of ownership  (direct  or indirect).
The calculation formula used, in line with  NZAOA and
PCAF recommendations, corresponds to the sum of the
nominal 
value of the investment in sovereign gross domestic
product by purchasing power parity  of the  sovereign, all
multiplied by the  sovereign’s domestic  GHG emissions.
Carbon  footprint  of the real estate  portfolio : Scope  1 and 2
emissions  are  estimated  using  available information
(actual  consumption,  energy  performance assessment,
location,  asset type, etc.) for each asset, prioritising actual
data. Estimates are made when necessary, in line with
PCAF  recommendations.
•LBP   AM: t o measure the financed emissions of listed
assets,  LBP   AM  uses underlying emissions data from
an  external  data provider,  MSCI. For  its subsidiary
La Financière  de l’Échiquier, data  from  Carbon4Finance
is used.
The share  of assets eligible for this  calculation is 74% for
LBP  AM and 92% for La Financière de l’Échiquier.
Carbon 
intensity  and  carbon  footprint calculations are
carried  out for this scope of assets in order to assess the
financed  emissions for  each s cope  (1, 2 and  3).
For LBP  AM, the av ailable  data is  emissions calculated
as of 31 December  2023.
•Louvre   Banque   Privée: f or the  direct securities scope,
data  is shared by the data provider Sustainalytics.
The  data is reported for most companies (from annual
reports). 
However, Sustainalytics may estimate this value
if the data  is not available from reporting.
For the UCITS scope, data is collected through negative
impact indicators at the end  2024, published  by the
management companies  under  the SFDR Regulation.
This  data  is not restated  by the  data  provider, but is
instead entered directly by  the asset management
companies. [E1_6_29]
Use of primary data: For the entire calculation of operational
Scope 3 GHG emissions for La Banque Postale Group, the
percentage  of emissions calculated using primary data  is
2%. The categories concerned are fuel- and energy-related
activities, waste generated in operations and business travel.
Concerning  financed emissions (Scope 3  Cat. 15), data from
different data providers is used. Details of the databases used
are indicated  above.  [E1_6_25]
Biogenic  emissions  included  in Scope 1, 2 
and 3 GHG emissions
For the 2024 financial year, La  Banque  Postale Group is

the combustion or biodegradation of biomass included in
Scopes  1, 2 and  3. [E1_6_17]  [E1_6_24]  [E1_6_28]2.2.1.8 GHG phase-out  and mitigation

title: Value chain projects
heading: 2.2.1.8.1 Value chain projects
start_phrase: La Banque Postale does not support carbon absorption projects in its value chain or own operations.
summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document detailing CSR environmental information and sustainable performance.
- Portfolio carbon footprint methodologies:
  - Sovereign bonds: Uses UNFCCC national emissions and World Bank GDP (PPP); applies to all sovereign holdings; methodology aligned with NZAOA and PCAF, allocating national emissions by the investment’s share of GDP (PPP).
  - Real estate: Scope 1 and 2 estimated prioritizing actual consumption, EPC, location, and asset type; estimates follow PCAF when needed.
- Financed emissions data and coverage:
  - LBP AM: MSCI data; LFDE: Carbon4Finance; asset coverage for calculations is 74% (LBP AM) and 92% (LFDE); carbon intensity and footprint calculated for Scopes 1–3; data as of 31/12/2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Direct securities via Sustainalytics (primarily company-reported data, estimates if missing); UCITS via SFDR negative impact indicators provided directly by asset managers without restatement.
- Primary data use: 2% of operational Scope 3 emissions calculated with primary data (fuel- and energy-related activities, waste, business travel). Financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15) rely on external providers.
- Biogenic emissions: Not quantified for Scopes 1–3 in FY2024.
- GHG mitigation and carbon credit-related initiatives:
  - Within value chain: No support for absorption projects; supports internal reduction projects through the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund (building energy efficiency and mobility).
  - CNP Assurances forestry: Monitors annual absorption; 483,653 tCO2 gross absorbed in 2024; forests managed for services/timber, not offsets.
  - Outside value chain: “Climate + Regions” program (since 2015) with La Poste Group supports sequestration and adaptation projects in France; contributed to France’s Low Carbon Label with CNPF; 25 certified projects supported as of 01/06/2024, mainly forestry.
    - At La Banque Postale level: 20-project portfolio, 10 certified (two have generated verified credits/reductions); non-certified items include methodology development (hedges recognized; Aleppo pine silviculture not recognized).
    - Estimated lifetime sequestration: 11,455 tCO2e; average cost €29/t; portfolio contains no carbon reduction projects.
text:
2.1.8.1
Value chain projects
La  Banque  Postale does not support carbon absorption
projects 
in its value chain or own operations. It only
supports 
reduction projects via its internal call for projects
known as the "Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund".
It 
enables employees to submit projects to reduce greenhouse
gas emissions in their entities or  business lines. Real estate
projects (optimising the energy efficiency of buildings)
and  mobility projects are  specific targets.
CNP   Assurances has significant woodland assets, and
monitors  the annual carbon absorption of its forests: the
principle is to estimate the organic growth of the
woodland during the year and then convert this growth in
biomass 
into absorbed CO2. In 2024, the gross annual CO2
absorbed by CNP Assurances’ woodland assets amounted
to 483,653 metric  tonnes of CO2. CNP Assurances does not
use woodland for the purpose of carbon offsetting, but
rather for the  value of services and timber.  [E1_7_01]

title: Projects outside the value chain
heading: 2.2.1.8.2 Projects outside the value chain
start_phrase: Since 2015, La Banque Postale has voluntarily built a “Climate + Regions” programme with two other entities of La Poste Group (the Mail Services, Parcels and Digital Services business units).
summary:
- Overview of La Banque Postale Group’s GHG accounting and environmental performance, including financed and operational emissions, data sources, and carbon credit projects and governance.
- Financed emissions methodologies:
  - Sovereign portfolio: Calculated per NZAOA/PCAF using UNFCCC domestic emissions and World Bank GDP (PPP); covers all sovereign bonds (direct and indirect).
  - Real estate portfolio: Scope 1–2 estimated from actual energy use/EPC/location/asset type, prioritizing primary data; estimates aligned with PCAF when needed.
  - Listed assets: LBP AM uses MSCI; La Financière de l’Échiquier uses Carbon4Finance; calculation coverage 74% (LBP AM) and 92% (LFDE); Scope 1–3 intensity/footprint calculated; data as of 31 Dec 2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Direct securities data from Sustainalytics (reported or estimated); UCITS data from SFDR negative impact indicators provided by management companies without restatement.
- Data quality and scope:
  - Operational Scope 3 primary data share is 2% (fuel- and energy-related activities, waste, business travel).
  - Financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15) rely on multiple external data providers.
  - Biogenic CO2 emissions for Scopes 1–3 not quantified for 2024.
- Value-chain climate actions:
  - LBP does not support absorption projects in its own value chain; funds internal reduction projects via the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund (e.g., building energy efficiency, mobility).
  - CNP Assurances’ woodland assets absorbed 483,653 tCO2 in 2024; tracked for value, not used for offsetting.
- Outside value-chain carbon contributions:
  - Since 2015, “Climate + Regions” program (with La Poste Group) supports French sequestration/adaptation projects and helped catalyze the Low Carbon Label; La Poste Group leads in supporting low-carbon certified projects.
  - LBP portfolio: 20 projects, 10 certified; two have already generated credits; also supported methodology development (“Hedges” recognized; “Sylviculture du Pin d’Alep” not recognized). Estimated sequestration 11,455 tCO2e over project lifetimes at ~€29/t; portfolio comprises absorption (no reduction) projects.
  - CNP Assurances’ VCS-certified Serragem project (Brazil): replaces Amazonian firewood with biomass waste for ceramics; 9,469 tCO2e contributed in 2024; 585,959 tCO2e avoided over 11 years with 309,408 tCO2e expected over the next nine; delivers environmental and social co-benefits; not used to meet LBP’s own GHG reduction targets.
- Project selection and standards:
  - ESG panel across La Poste Group reviews projects with specialized partners (EcoAct, CNPF, Société Forestière, Carbone Farmers, CDC Biodiversité).
  - Assessment criteria include sequestration potential/certification (Low Carbon Label, Gold Standard), biodiversity and socio-economic co-benefits, carbon price, and value split.
- Credit issuance/cancellation:
  - Low Carbon Label credits are ex-post and cancelled upon DGEC recognition after N+5 external audits.
  - In 2024, LBP’s first Low Carbon Label forestry projects (1,334 tCO2e) received recognition; Serragem reduces 9,469 tCO2e per year.
- Net-zero pathway:
  - Alignment with La Poste Group’s NZE 2040 strategy; scenarios under analysis; conclusions expected Q1 2025 with a 2025 decision.
- Carbon credits summary:
  - Cancelled in 2024: 10,803 tCO2e total; 12.35% absorption, 87.65% reduction; 12.35% Low Carbon Label, 87.65% VCS; 12.35% in EU; 12.35% aligned with Paris Agreement Article 6 expectations; 2023 data not available.
  - Expected cancellations until 2026: 10,121 tCO2e.
text:
2.1.8.2 Projects outside the  value chain
Since  2015, La  Banque  Postale has voluntarily built a
“Climate + Regions” programme with two other entities of
La  Poste Group (the Mail Services, Parcels and Digital
Services 
business units). It aims to support carbon
sequestration and regional adaptation projects in France.
This project, whose launch was supported by I4CE, led to
the emergence of the Low  Carbon Label, the first carbon
offsetting benchmark recognised  in France , with the
partner CNPF (National  Forest Ownership Centre).
Through this programme,  La  Poste Group is now the
leading contributor of low-carbon certified  projects.  On 1
June 2024, 25 low-carbon certified projects were supported,
mainly in forestry methodologies.
At 
La  Banque  Postale level, the portfolio consists of
20 
projects, including 10 low-carbon certified projects
(certification 
decisions received from the Ministry). Of these
10 projects, two have already generated carbon credits
and  reduced  emissions (verification  decisions received),
these projects having been supported during the structuring
phase of the certification Label in 2015.
Non-certified projects are those supporting the drafting of
new AML methodologies (“Hedges”, which have since been
recognised, 
as well as the  “Sylviculture du Pin d'Alep'”
method (not recognised  by the Ministry).
This portfolio currently corresponds to an estimated carbon
sequestration  of 11,455 tCO₂e over the life of the projects,
with an average  cost  of €29 per tonne. The  portfolio does
not include any carbon reduction  projects.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1432Sustainable performance
Environmental information
CNP 
Assurances launched the  Serragem project in 2007. In
2024, it  made  a voluntary  contribution of  9,469 tCO₂e  to
mitigate  the effects of climate  change. The project fights
deforestation by replacing firewood with biomass waste to
supply two  ceramic  factories  in the city  of São Miguel  do
Guamá,  in the  Brazilian state of  Pará. Before  its launch, the
factories consumed 45,000 metric tonnes of Amazonian
firewood each year to  fuel their kilns.  Today, these plants
use the biomass of  acai kernels and sawdust, which were
previously a major waste problem in the region. This project
has already  avoided emissions of 585,959 tCO2 e over
11 years and will avoid another 309,408 tCO2e over the
following 
nine years. In addition to reducing GHG emissions
and  pressure on the Amazon rainforest, this initiative
supports  the local economy by  creating jobs and new
markets  for local biomass  suppliers. Serragem also
implements environmental actions to  reduce the impact
of the ceramics industry and supports vulnerable groups
through a number  of social initiatives.
The purpose of this voluntary contribution is not to enable
La  Banque  Postale to achieve its targets for reducing
direct or indirect  greenhouse  gas emissions.  [E1_7_02]
2.

title: Project qualification
heading: 2.2.1.8.3 Project qualification
start_phrase: Each project selected in La Banque Postale's portfolio must be presented to a selection panel bringing together the ESG experts from each contributing La Poste Group entity.
summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale’s sustainable performance and environmental actions, with emphasis on carbon credits, project governance, and internal carbon pricing.
- Highlights CNP Assurances’ Serragem project (launched 2007) that replaces Amazonian firewood with biomass waste (açaí kernels, sawdust) for ceramic kilns in Pará, Brazil; 2024 voluntary contribution of 9,469 tCO2e; 585,959 tCO2e avoided over 11 years and a further 309,408 tCO2e expected over the next nine years; delivers local jobs, markets, environmental actions, and social initiatives; not counted toward La Banque Postale’s GHG reduction targets; certified under the Verified Carbon Standard.
- Describes project selection by an ESG panel across La Poste Group entities, with partner presentations (EcoAct, CNPF, Société Forestière, Carbone Farmers, CDC Biodiversité) and multi-criteria assessment (carbon potential/certifications, biodiversity benefits, socio-economic co-benefits, price per tonne, revenue split).
- Explains absorption projects (natural CO2 sequestration such as afforestation, post-dieback reforestation, Arboreal City) and Low Carbon Label rules: ex-post credit cancellation upon DGEC-issued Emissions Reductions after N+5 third-party audits.
- 2024 base year milestones: first Low Carbon Label pilot forestry projects in France recognized for 1,334 tCO2e; Serragem delivers 9,469 tCO2e/year reductions; future cancellations tied to pending N+5 audits for absorption projects.
- Carbon credits canceled in 2024: total 10,803 tCO2e; 12.35% absorption vs. 87.65% reduction; 12.35% Low Carbon Label; 87.65% Verified Carbon Standard; 12.35% in the EU; 12.35% aligned with Article 6 expectations. Expected cancellations until 2026: 10,121 tCO2e.
- Net zero alignment: La Banque Postale follows La Poste Group’s NZE strategy, with scenario analysis underway toward NZE by 2040; represented on the NZE Steering Committee; conclusions due Q1 2025 with a 2025 decision.
- Internal carbon pricing mechanism (since 2015) aims to anticipate market carbon price dynamics and drive decarbonization; scope refresh planned in 2025 to fully cover the operational footprint.
- Framework built around the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund; CNP Assurances established a similar carbon and biodiversity fund in 2022.
- Dual funding dimensions: internal (building renovations/energy optimization, internal calls for projects, KPI tracking for avoided tCO2e, cost savings, ROI) and external (carbon sequestration and biodiversity projects in France and abroad, tracking tCO2e sequestered, species saved, area preserved; annual reporting to the Executive Committee).
- Results and funding: over €3 million allocated across ten editions; 103 internal projects funded avoiding over 7,529 tCO2e (e.g., energy retrofits, awareness campaigns, e-bikes/scooters, solar thermal/PV, green roofs, carpooling hub); external partnerships with CDC Biodiversité and WWF to develop national carbon sinks.
- Internal carbon price set at €60/tCO2e, informed by CDP, Institut Montaigne, and the Blanchard-Tirole Commission (≈€65/tCO2e benchmark); annual fund budgets calculated as GHG emissions multiplied by the internal price.
- Budget inputs: banking scope uses year N-2 emissions (Scopes 1 and 2: 5,278 and 1,876 tCO2e; Scope 3 operational: 31,819 tCO2e) due to project lead times; insurance scope uses year N emissions (Scopes 1 and 2: 1,495 and 276 tCO2e; Scope 3 travel/commuting: 6,525 tCO2e).
text:
2.1.8.3 Project qualification
Each  project  selected  in La   Banque  Postale's portfolio
must  be presented  to a selection panel bringing together
the ESG experts  from each contributing La  Poste Group
entity . The projects are presented by partners specialised
in supporting carbon contribution projects in France
(EcoAct,  CNPF, Société Forestière,  Carbone Farmers, CDC
Biodiversité) and are subject to a multi-criteria assessment,
including:  carbon  sequestration  potential  (Low  Carbon
Label certification, Gold Standard, etc.), biodiversity benefits
(biodiversity index associated  with  the project), socio-
economic  joint  benefits,  price per tonne  of carbon,
dividing the project amount between the partner and the
forest owner/farmer.
CNP   Assurances ’ Serragem  reduction project complies
with the Verified Carbon Standard international certification
standard.  [E1_7_12]
These  absorption  projects are  based  on  the  natural
sequestration of CO₂ through the  creation or reinforcement
of biogenic  sinks  (afforestation  of wasteland,  post-dieback
reforestation,  the Arboreal  City project,  etc.). [E1_7_15]Under  the Low Carbon Label, carbon credits are cancelled
based 
on receipt of letters recognising Emissions Reductions
(ER) issued by the French Directorate General for Energy
and Climate  (DGEC), which are linked  to the projects since
they  are they are ex-post projects. Recognition only takes

external third party.
For this base year of  2024,  La  Banque   Postale ’s first Low
Carbon Label pilot forestry projects in France, representing
1,334 tCO₂e, are the  first to be recognised and to have
enforceable credits. With regard to  CNP   Assurances, the
Verified Carbon Standard-certified Serragem project, carried
out in Brazil, achieved a reduction of 9,469 tCO₂e per year.
The carbon credits  that will  be cancelled in  the  future are
related to the various Low-Carbon Label absorption projects
for 
which year N+5 audits have not yet taken place, whereby
carbon credits are cancelled by recognising Emissions
Reductions.
With 
regard to achieving the net zero emissions (NZE) target,
La Banque Postale is aligned with La Poste Group’s strategy.
Work 
is currently being carried out to analyse the various

La  Banque  Postale is represented on the NZE Steering

to monitor the progress of the work. The conclusions

title: Internal carbon price
heading: 2.2.1.9 Internal carbon price
start_phrase: Since 2015, La Banque Postale has structured an internal carbon pricing mechanism with a dual ambition:
summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale’s internal carbon pricing mechanism, launched in 2015, designed to both anticipate market carbon price impacts for climate risk management and drive decarbonization targets, with scope expansion work planned for 2025.
- Central role of the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund (and CNP Assurances’ analogous fund since 2022) to monetize the Group’s carbon footprint and finance:
  - Internal projects: building renovation/energy optimization and internal calls for projects, with annual monitoring of environmental/economic gains and ROI (tCO2e avoided, euros saved).
  - External projects: carbon sequestration in France and abroad and biodiversity conservation, tracking tCO2e sequestered, species saved, and area preserved; results reported annually to the Executive Committee.
- Outcomes and resourcing:
  - Over €3 million allocated across the first ten editions; 103 internal projects financed, avoiding more than 7,529 tCO2e; examples include energy retrofits, awareness campaigns, e-mobility fleets, solar installations, green roofs, and carpooling hubs.
  - External partnerships with CDC Biodiversité and WWF to develop innovative national carbon sinks.
- Internal carbon price set at €60/tCO2e, aligned with recommendations (CDP, Institut Montaigne, Blanchard‑Tirole Commission ~€65/tCO2e for EU finance).
- Annual fund budgets derived from GHG emissions × internal carbon price:
  - Banking scope uses year N‑2 emissions: SBTi Scope 1 = 5,278 tCO2e; Scope 2 = 1,876 tCO2e; operational Scope 3 = 31,819 tCO2e.
  - Insurance scope uses year N: Scope 1 = 1,495 tCO2e; Scope 2 = 276 tCO2e; Scope 3 (business travel and commuting) = 6,525 tCO2e.
- Coverage via internal carbon pricing: 100% of Scope 1 and Scope 2; 35% of partial operational Scope 3.
- Anticipated financial effects of climate-related risks: reporting timing determined; detailed metrics disclosed under Pillar III elsewhere in the document (exposures to acute/chronic physical risks and real estate energy efficiency distribution).
- Operational GHG management indicators and trends:
  - Buildings CO2 (tCO2e): 18,421 (2022), 13,821 (2023), 13,071 (2024) – continuing decrease.
  - Vehicle emissions: 6,158 (2022), 5,540 (2023), 6,338 (2024) – +14% from 2023 to 2024 due to phased vehicle policy rollout and improved fleet estimation.
  - IT and data centers: 10,544 (2022), 9,651 (2023), 9,069 (2024) – 6% decrease from 2023 to 2024 via data center optimization, equipment life extension/reuse, responsible purchasing (EPEAT), and employee awareness/training.
  - Transition to the “Aguaro” measurement tool in 2024 improved precision, reliability, and traceability of carbon data.
- Alignment with SBTi and mission-led commitments:
  - Monitoring of low‑carbon pathway indicators within the operational scope supports climate action, stakeholder accountability, and credibility.
  - SBTi Scope 1 & 2 emissions: 6,389 tCO2e (2023), 6,260 tCO2e (2024), with a 2030 target of 3,823 tCO2e.
- Governance: annual indicator reviews and impact reporting to the Executive Committee to assess system relevance and progress toward reduction targets.

2.1.9
Internal  carbon price
Since 2015, La  Banque  Postale has structured an internal
carbon  pricing  mechanism with  a dual  ambition:
•anticipate  changes in  the market price that could be
incorporated into climate risk  management;
•contribute to the achievement  of the Company’s
decarbonisation  targets.
New  work  on the  scope  will be carried out in  2025 in order
to comprehensively  cover  La Banque  Postale ’s operational
footprint.
The internal carbon pricing is organised around the Climate
and Biodiversity Impact Fund, a voluntary and  unprecedented
internal 
system for monetising La Banque Postale's carbon
footprint.
Drawing  inspiration from this system, CNP Assurances set
up the carbon and biodiversity fund mechanism based on
an internal carbon price for the first time in 2022.
The process  includes:
•an internal dimension enabling financing of renovation/
energy  optimisation work on buildings as well as an
internal 
call for  projects at all institutions. For these two
systems, 
monitoring indicators are managed in order to
estimate the  associated economic and environmental
gains . The return  on investment  of the projects  is also
analysed, which gives an annual view of the tonnes of
CO₂  equivalent avoided and the euros saved thanks to
the implementation of the  projects;
•an external dimension enabling the financing of carbon
sequestration  projects in France and abroad, as well as
biodiversity  conservation projects.  Here  too,  monitoring
indicators are managed to measure the tonnes of CO₂
equivalent sequestered per project, the species saved or
the square metres preserved. These various indicators
are monitored annually and presented to the Executive
Committee  to justify the  relevance of the system and its
contribution  to achieving  the reduction  targets.
For the  first  ten  editions,  a total  financial budget  of more
than €3 million  was used  to finance:
•internal  projects  to reduce greenhouse gas  emissions:
Since  the launch of the Climate and Biodiversity ImpactFund, 
La Banque Postale has financed 103 internal projects
aimed 
at reducing greenhouse gas emissions, thus avoiding
more than  7,529 tCO₂e. These  projects include energy
efficiency renovation, sustainable development
awareness  campaigns, creating fleets of electric bicycles
and scooters, the installation of solar water heaters and
solar panels, the greening of  roofs and the creation  of a
carpooling hub for employee commuting;
•external projects (national and international) to sequestrate
and  offset residual emissions as well as biodiversity
conservation 
projects. Partnerships  with players such as
CDC  Biodiversité and WWF were supported in order to
structure 
innovative approaches to the creation of
national carbon sinks.  [E1_8_01]
The internal carbon  price corresponds to a fictitious price
associated with one tCO₂e. [E1_8_02]

around €65 per  tCO₂e in the European financial sector.

heading: 2.2.1.11.1 GHG emissions management indicators
start_phrase: To manage its low-carbon pathway in its operational scope, La Banque Postale specifically monitors emissions related to buildings, vehicles and digital technology.
summary:

text:
2.1.11.1 GHG  emissions management  indicators
To manage its low-carbon pathway in its operational scope, La  Banque  Postale specifically monitors emissions related to
buildings, vehicles  and  digital  technology.
Emissions  related to the vehicle  fleet increased  by 14%
between 2023  and  2024. This  change is  due  to the  gradual
implementation of the vehicle policy, which is not yet in
full effect, as well as a better estimate in 2024 of the
vehicle  fleet  taken  into  account.
Between  2023 and 2024, greenhouse  gas (GHG) emissions
related to La   Banque  Postale’s IT infrastructure and data
centres 
decreased by 6%. This decrease is due to a number
of initiatives  implemented by La Banque  Postale Group:
•optimisation  of data centres: lockdown of cooling areas,
regulation of temperatures and optimised management
of volumes and  allocated spaces;
•extending  the  life of  equipment: reusing computer
equipment,  primarily through donations to social and
solidarity-based economy (SSE) players;•responsible  purchasing: using CSR  criteria for computer
equipment purchases, favouring EPEAT-certified equipment;
•awareness and training: training and awareness programmes
for employees on responsible digital  technology.
In addition, the transition from the “Green Argile” to the
“Aguaro” measurement tool in 2024 has enabled more
precise and detailed measurements to be taken, contributing
to better reliability and traceability of carbon footprint data.
As 
part of its status as a mission-led company,
La Banque Postale monitors low-carbon pathway indicators
which 
reflect SBTi commitments within its operating
scope. Crucially,  ensuring that its own operations comply
with these pathways  helps it to contribute  to combating
climate change, to strengthen its responsibility towards its
stakeholders  and to establish its  credibility as a mission-
led company.

title: Management indicators related to impact financing
heading: 2.2.1.11.2 Management indicators related to impact financing
start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group’s commitments and actions to finance environmental solutions are reflected in indicators monitored as part of La Banque Postale’s status as a mission-led company, and in CNP’s company purpose.
summary:
- Climate-related risk disclosure: Key data (exposures to physical risk, location of high-risk assets, and real estate energy efficiency) is reported under Pillar III and referenced to specific sections of the Universal Registration Document.
- Operational GHG management focus: Buildings, vehicle fleet, and digital (IT/data centers).
- 2023–2024 emissions trends: Vehicle emissions up 14% (policy rollout and better fleet estimation); IT/data center emissions down 6% (data center optimization, equipment life extension/donations, responsible purchasing favoring EPEAT, staff training).
- Measurement enhancement: Migration from Green Argile to Aguaro tool in 2024 improved carbon data precision, reliability, and traceability.
- SBTi-aligned pathway and mission-led status: Scope 1 & 2 emissions at 6,260 tCO2e in 2024 vs 3,823 tCO2e target for 2030; operational emissions in 2024—buildings 13,071 tCO2e, vehicles 6,338 tCO2e, IT 9,069 tCO2e.
- Renewable energy financing: Target €5.6bn in commitments by 2025; 2024 annual production lower due to strong market competition; strategic diversification into batteries, hydrogen, and grid balancing with strict selectivity.
- Impact measurement: Proprietary Impact Weighting Factor (IWF) covered 73% of activities in 2024; target ≥87% by end-2025.
- CNP Assurances investments: Impact investments reached €1.7bn by end-2024 (exceeding 2025 pledge of €1bn); green investments €29.4bn (CNP SA and subsidiaries), tracking to ≥€30bn by end-2025.
- Green loans to local authorities: EU Taxonomy-aligned since 2022; outstanding €1.5bn as of 31 Dec 2024, already beyond the 2025 target.
- Key impact finance metrics: Renewables deployed production €5,039m (2024; target €5,600m in 2025); annual production €453m (2024); renewables commitments €2,621m (2024); green loan annual production €1,563m (2024).
- Biodiversity materiality: Not material for own operations; material via financed activities in sectors exerting significant pressure on nature (e.g., soil degradation/deforestation, pollution, ecosystem pressures, GHGs).
- Biodiversity transition approach: Integrating climate–nature linkages; supporting sector transformations (agriculture, chemicals, mining); participation in “Roquelaure Entreprises et Biodiversité”; initial qualitative TNFD-based scenario analysis for 2030/2050; 2024 Climate & Nature report focused on Corporate & Investment Banking; plan to adopt a combined climate–nature transition plan by 2028.
- Policy alignment: Roadmap guided by the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and a double materiality lens (financial dependence on natural capital and corporate impacts on nature).
