3.1.2.5 Diversity and inclusion policies 
and commitments
The policies presented in this paragraph respond to the
positive 
and negative impacts and risks related to diversity
and  inclusion.
Policies applicable  to diversity  and inclusion
The Diversity  and Inclusion policy is redefined every three
years 
in the related social agreement. It is implemented by
the Human Resources Department and applies to the
entire scope and to employees of La  Banque Postale UES.
The Diversity and Inclusion policy is based  on the  five
pillars of  Diversity:
•Disability: recruitment of people with RQTH (disabled
worker) 
status with equal skills, and obtaining recognition
of disabled  worker status  for our current employees;
•Generations: keeping older people in employment, bringing
young people into the job market, intergenerational diversity;
•Parity: 
gender equality, gender balance, combating everyday
sexism,  equal  treatment, parity of governing bodies;
•LGBT+: develop a respectful and inclusive working
environment for  LGBT+ people, with specific actions to
improve their well-being and inclusion;
•Social/Ethnic  origins: creating an inclusive collective
experience to ensure fairness at all stages of employee
life with the Company.
The diversity policy is built with experts, charities, the Human
Resources 
Department and employees. It is distributed
internally (on the intranet) and externally (on the website).
[S1_1_10]
La  Banque   Postale UES’ Diversity and Inclusion policy
covers all the grounds for discrimination identified by law
(26 listed by the legislator to date), including sex, gender,
age and  disability . [S1_1_11]170 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
As part of this Diversity and Inclusion policy, the Disability
policy  of La Banque  Postale UES  is implemented by the
Human  Resources Department and defined under the
sixth  social  agreement of 27 March 2023, based on the
disability  laws  applicable  in France.  It introduces the
systematic recruitment  of RQTH (Recognition of the status
of disabled worker) profiles, both internally and externally,
with  equal skills; as well as an RQTH declaration incentive
programme  for Company employees. The Disability policy
covers 
the entire scope and all employees of La Banque Postale
UES, 
as well as all banking functions. It is built with experts,
external associations (in particular the AFMD: Association
Française  des Managers de la Diversité, Entreprise pour
la Cité ) and  the Human Resources Department.
In order to combat all types of discrimination, and to promote
inclusion and equal opportunities, La Banque Postale UES
has demonstrated its commitment through  two major
social  agreements  signed  unanimously  by the Bank’s
social  bodies: the Disability agreement and the Diversity
and Professional Equality agreement . Each of these
agreements  – signed for  a period  of three years  and for
the sixth consecutive time – demonstrates the consistency
of the Group’s  commitment.
CNP  Assurances has its own QWLWC agreement, which
aims  to guarantee everyone equal treatment based on
skills and performance. Similarly, in its code of conduct,
CNP  Assurances mentions best  practices to be adopted
in  terms of preventing discrimination and harassment.
CNP  Assurances has also been a signatory of the Diversity
Charter  since 2006, and this long-term commitment is
now  part  of its company purpose to take action  for an
inclusive and sustainable society. Since 2021, an Inclusion
Committee 
has been set up to lead and drive the Company’s
overall 
approach in this area. It monitors and verifies the
progress of the action plans and guarantees overall
consistency . CNP   Assurances also  ensures  compliance
with its obligations in terms of combating discrimination,
harassment  and  sexist  behaviour through complaints
mechanisms.
Louvre  Banque Privée  also has a company agreement on
professional equality  and  quality  of life at work. [S1_1_10]
La  Banque  Postale SA has made commitments to the
inclusion  of vulnerable groups,  based on:
•Two basic agreements, including a Diversity and Professional
Equality  agreement and an agreement on people with
disabilities,  which  are renewed  every three years;
•The implementation  of a  mission-led  company gender
parity  indicator;
•Commitments in partnership with charities through charters
and  projects;
•A Diversity strategy shared with the  Group’s Executive
Committee.
Strategic principles for inclusion
To implement all of these commitments, every year,
La  Banque  Postale Group  proposes a comprehensive
action  plan to combat all forms of  discrimination andstrengthen the inclusion of  all people likely to be discriminated
against. Some of the flagship measures include:
•Gender parity: webinar on professional equality, conference
on violence against  women;
•Salary streamlining with a new remuneration package;
•Disability: Health and Disability Week (Spring) and European
Disability 
Employment Week (November), which are
two annual highlights to encourage managers and raise
awareness among staff. In addition, throughout the
year, 
ten disability officers support people with disabilities
with various processes and adjusting their workstations,
as 
well as an awareness-raising web series with a common
topic each  year (chronic  illness/mental health/disabling
diseases,  etc.);
•Diversity: webinars on various topics, support for managers
with 
inclusion situations (e.g. employee in transition;
appearance of a disability, etc.), mentoring (intergenerational,
female mentoring, etc.), inclusion survey and measurement
(everyday sexism survey, LGBT+ survey, focus groups, etc.),
sponsorship 
and speeches by executives on the various
diversity pillars. [S1_1_12]
In addition, La Banque Postale SA offers more than 30 events,
workshops, webinars and conferences per year to support
the cultural transformation  that inclusion represents.
It runs five training courses on diversity and inclusion in
conjunction 
with La Poste Group, one of which is mandatory,
and which are available to all its employees.
Finally, La Banque Postale Group has set up reporting and
whistleblowing channels for victims  or witnesses of
discrimination. More information on the processing of reports
is available in Section 2.3.1.2.6 “Human rights policies and
measures”. The whistleblowing system is also described in
paragraph 2.4.1.3.5 “Independence and  accessibility of the
whistleblowing  system”.  [S1_1_13]

text:
3.1.2.6 Human rights policies and measures
Policies regarding Human rights
The Group’s human rights policies aim to prevent and
minimise the  negative impacts and risks identified in
this area.
La 
Banque Postale Group’s commitments to respect Human
Rights are part of  La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy,
and apply in particular to its own workforce. This policy
reiterates 
the adherence of La Poste Group and
La Banque Postale to the United Nations Global Compact,
and 
indicates that the Group takes as a reference framework
several international agreements and commitments,
including:
•the Universal  Declaration  of Human Rights;
•the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights;
•the Declaration and Fundamental Conventions of the
International Labour Organization;
•the OECD  Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises;
•the UN Global Compact.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1712Sustainable performance
Social information
La Banque  Postale Group  is therefore committed to:
•preventing all forms of human rights violations and ensuring
that it is not complicit  in human rights violations;
•prohibiting  all forms of moral or physical violence, and
more  generally all  forms of inhuman, cruel or degrading
treatment;
•prohibiting 
all forms of forced or compulsory labour, child
labour and  human  trafficking;
•prohibiting all forms of discrimination; in particular according
to gender, age, state of health or disability, pregnancy,
sexual 
orientation, nationality, social background, belonging
to a particular community, political, trade union or religious
beliefs;
•defending 
freedom of association and the right to
collective bargaining;
•defending the  right  to adequate  remuneration;
•opposing  all forms  of invasion  of personal  privacy.
La  Banque  Postale Group conducts its activities in
compliance  with the labo ur laws of the countries in which
it operates. While local provisions are likely to limit the
protection 
of human rights within the meaning of international
standards, the Group seeks the best solutions to  come as
close as possible to this level of protection for its employees.
[S1_1_03] [S1_1_04]
When  developing its policies, La  Banque  Postale Group
complies  with  international  frameworks and instruments
(see Section  2.3.1.5.3 “Contribution to the Sustainable
Development  Goals (SDGs)” for the contribution to the
United  Nations  Sustainable Development  Goals  (SDGs) ).
[S1_1_07]
The Group is also committed to combating human trafficking,
forced labour  and child labour. These matters are specifically
addressed  in La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy,
which  also  applies  to La Banque  Postale Group.  [S1_1_08]Human rights impact  remediation process
Since  La  Banque  Postale SA and most of its subsidiaries
are 
located  in France, they do not have a great deal of
exposure to major human rights  risks. However, they may
face risks of discrimination and harassment requiring due
diligence to ensure  a good  working environment.
The processing of reports from the whistleblowing system
is 
described in Section 2.4.1.3.5 “Independence and accessibility
of the whistleblowing system”.
The Group has also set  up  a system  for dealing with
distressing situations at work. This system and the
procedure 
for processing reports are described in  Section
2.3.1.4 “Reporting and remediation process”. [S1_1_05] [S1_1_06]

start_phrase: The Human Resources Director is responsible for the human resources policies implemented by the Human Resources Department.
summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) detailing employee dialogue, representation, surveys, and reporting/remediation mechanisms, including CNP Assurances.

- Governance and responsibility:
  - Human Resources Department leads HR policy and ensures effective dialogue with employees and their representatives.
  - Strong emphasis on stakeholder representation in governance to reinforce the social dimension of ESG.

- Direct employee dialogue and listening:
  - Multi‑year listening framework with an annual Group‑wide engagement survey (~50 questions on strategy, customers, well‑being, teamwork, management); departments act on results.
  - 2024 special surveys: hybrid work (2,207 respondents; 59% participation) and CLDB transformation follow‑up.
  - Listening workshops on transformation and employee experience; monitoring of Glassdoor ratings.
  - Diversity focus groups collect feedback to inform and adjust inclusion policies.

- Employee representation and social dialogue structures:
  - Five employee representatives sit on La Banque Postale’s Supervisory Board.
  - Group Committee (parent and subsidiaries with SECs) meets regularly on strategic topics and consolidated financials.
  - For La Banque Postale UES:
    - Operates under several agreements (employee representation, social dialogue/right to organize, career paths/skills for office holders), aligned with French Labour Code and sectoral banking agreements; all published on intranet.
    - The Social and Economic Committee (SEC) ensures collective expression and is informed/consulted on workforce changes, structural changes, employment and working conditions (incl. hours, training), new technologies, H&S/working conditions, and environmental impacts.
    - 2024 activity: 15 SEC meetings (11 ordinary, 4 extraordinary), 15 SEC commission meetings (diversity/equality, employment, training, sustainability), 10 HSWCC meetings; monthly meetings with union reps; work on remote tools for exercising the right to organize.
    - Strategic guidelines consultation every three years with annual intermediate updates; early re‑consultation if strategy changes; local/regional representation maintained via alternate SEC members.
    - Discussion workshops with SEC/HSWCC support collaborative, calm transformation.
    - Sustainability Commission established by the SEC, meeting twice yearly; includes four Mission Committee representatives and four SEC representatives.

- CNP Assurances:
  - Two agreements enabling “constructive and effective” social dialogue and governing the SEC.
  - QWLWC survey on engagement and well‑being.
  - “Parlons ambition” dialogue between employees and the Executive Committee.
  - 2024 agreements signed on diversity and professional equality.

- Reporting and remediation of distressing situations at work:
  - Confidential, impartial process respecting presumption of innocence; multiple reporting channels (manager, HR, occupational health, employee reps, harassment officers, social worker, ethics officer/whistleblowing platform).
  - Coverage includes moral/sexual harassment, sexist behavior, broader distress/burnout.
  - Employee awareness via intranet, Internal Rules, and code of conduct; training/communication reinforced; Confirmodoc tool verifies distribution of the code to employees and relevant third parties.
  - Processing:
    - Reports logged; listening phase within 15 days assesses need for occupational health referral and temporary protective measures.
    - If needed, investigation phase led by a joint steering committee (two HR reps, SEC secretary, HSWCC rapporteur); interviews clarify facts and remedies.
    - Outcomes may include support (medical/psychological), disciplinary actions up to dismissal for gross misconduct, and organizational/process changes; HR monitors effectiveness.
text:
3.1.3 Dialogue  process  with employees and their representatives
The Human Resources Director is responsible for the human
resources  policies implemented by  the Human Resources
Department . It is also responsible for the  proper dialogue
with employees, whether direct or through representatives.
[S1_2_04]
Direct  dialogue  with employees
For La Banque Postale Group, daily communication with
managers and Human Resources managers, as well as
employee  representative bodies, play an important role in
ensuring  that  the employee's voice  is heard.
The expression of employees in their daily work is also
facilitated by the employee experience policy  deployed by
the Human  Resources  Department. The whistleblowing
system (system  for dealing  with distressing situations at
work  and compliance reporting system) is also a means of
expression  for employees taking  into account their
individual  and  collective interests.  [S1_2_02]
The Group has introduced a multi-year listening framework
that aims to place the needs and expectations of employees
at the heart of its strategy. This  has led to a large-scale
annual engagement survey, managed by La Poste Group,
and 
which covers all La Banque Postale Group employees.
The survey asks employees approximately 50 questions
about  aspects of Strategy, Customers, Well-being at Work,
Teamwork  and Management. The results are taken into
account  by each department,  which undertakes actions
accordingly.At the same time, multi-year listening sessions are conducted
as needed. In 2024,  a survey  on hybrid work was launched,
with more than 2,207 respondents (representing a
participation rate of 59%) and specific surveys on request,
including a survey conducted among  CLDB employees to
measure how well  they had adjusted to the ongoing
transformation.
Employees 
are also asked  to participate  in dedicated
listening workshops  on the transformation  plan  and the
topic of the employee experience. Willing employees who
take part in these workshops are invited to share their
points of view on internal operations, their needs, as well as
their ideas for improvement.
In addition, the Glassdoor rating , an external tool allowing
employees  to express their experience, is monitored by
the Human Resources teams and partly feeds into the
employee  experience  strategy.
As the effectiveness  of the interaction channels  is difficult
to quantify, La  Banque  Postale has indirect feedback on
them 
in its interactions with the Social and Economic
Committee (SEC) and employee  representatives.  [S1_2_06]
In addition to the traditional survey formats, La Banque Postale
SA sets up focus groups on all the emerging pillars of
Diversity in order to collect  opinions, facts and impressions
of the relevant or related people. These focus groups are a
means of formalising assessments of the current situation,
and proposing  or adjusting the related inclusion policies.
[S1_2_07]

Employee  representation at Group level
La Banque  Postale Group  attaches particular  importance
to social dialogue and employee representation.  This is
reflected in the presence of employee representatives at
all levels  of the organisation, including the highest levels.
Therefore, La Banque Postale’s Supervisory Board includes
five employee representatives, providing a wide range of
viewpoints and  improving the quality of discussions.
Their   presence sheds an internal light on social and
operational  realities,  contributing to a strategy aligned
with  the long-term corporate interest. This participation
also  strengthens the social dimension  of ESG  by ensuring
stakeholder representation  within  governance.
In addition, a Group Committee, made up of employee
representatives  of La  Banque   Postale’s parent company
and all subsidiaries with a Social and Economic Committee,
meets  regularly to discuss topics of strategic importance
and  the Group's  consolidated  financial statements.  [S1_2_03]
Social  dialogue  within La Banque  Postale UES
La  Banque  Postale UES does not have a specific global
framework 
agreement, but it  relies on several agreements(1)
in order  to consider  its employees’  viewpoints:
•A collective agreement on the organisation of employee
representation within  La Banque  Postale  UES;
•An agreement on social dialogue and the exercising of
the right  to organise;
•An agreement on managing career paths and improving
the skills  of office  holders.
These  agreements set out the framework for employee
representation within the Company as well as the framework
for exercising  this  representation,  allowing  for employee
interests  to be taken into account. These provisions are in
line with the legal and regulatory framework laid down in
particular  by the  French Labour  Code, as  well as by  any
regulations applicable to the business segment, via the
French 
National Collective Agreement on Banking for
La  Banque  Postale and  other branch agreements.
They are published on the intranet, making them accessible
to all employees.
For La  Banque   Postale UES, the Social and Economic
Committee 
(SEC) guarantees the  collective  expression of
employees  and ensures that their interests are  taken into
account, in particular in decisions relating to the  management
and 
economic and financial development of the Company,
and to the  organisation of work, professional training and
production techniques. It is informed and consulted on
issues  relating  to:
•measures  likely to  affect the volume or structure of
the workforce;
•a change  in its economic  or legal structure;
•employment and working conditions, in particular working
hours,  and  professional  training;
•the introduction of new technologies or any major changes
in health  and  safety  or working  conditions.It is also  informed and consulted on the environmental
consequences 
of these measures. In total, 15 SEC meetings
(11 
ordinary, 4 extraordinary) and 10 HSWCC meetings were
held in 2024. In addition, there were 15 meetings of the
SEC commissions dedicated to specific topics such  as
diversity  and professional equality, employment, training
and  sustainability. In addition, work has been undertaken
on ways of exercising the right to organise, and in
particular 
on the use of remote communications tools.
A  monthly meeting is also scheduled with union
representatives to discuss issues of collective concern or
current affairs concerning employees, and on the functioning
of social dialogue. 
[S1_2_01]
For certain types of projects, the  SEC is consulted before
the project is implemented by La Banque Postale.
In addition, pursuant to the law  and the agreement on
employee representation  entered into  within the  Group,
the consultation  of the SEC on the strategic guidelines of
La Banque Postale UES covers these guidelines as defined
by the body responsible for monitoring, and the consequences
of 
these guidelines within La  Banque  Postale UES.
This  consultation takes place every three years. However,
in 
order  to keep the members of the SEC informed of
strategic decisions, an intermediate information point not
covered by the consultation procedure  is held each year.
In the event of significant changes in the La Banque Postale
UES  strategy in the intervening period between these
three years, a new consultation is set up by management.
If a consultation takes place before the end of  the three-
year period, a new three-year cycle begins  from that  date.
La  Banque  Postale also wished to maintain local and
regional staff representation based on an agreement to
appoint local representatives (alternate SEC members)
throughout the country.
The deployment  of discussion workshops with elected
members of the SEC and the HSWCC has enabled everyone
to 
work together, share information and discuss certain
issues. This methodology, deployed upstream from talks
with the SEC/HSWCC or downstream as part of the tracking
process, 
has helped to foster a collaborative relationship,
enabling 
La Banque Postale to pursue its transformation
in a calm and  peaceful manner.
La  Banque   Postale  and  the SEC wanted to  set up  a
Sustainability Commission. The SEC has therefore created
a Sustainability Commission, which meets twice a year.
It is made up  of:
•four Mission Committee representatives, whose role is
to share the Committee’s progress and gather feedback
from SEC representatives, particularly as part of its work
to prepare the Mission  Committee’s annual report;
•four La Banque Postale Social and Economic Committee
representatives appointed  by the SEC (including its

Mission 
Committee and provide insight into the Group’s

title: Reporting and remediation process
heading: 2.3.1.4 Reporting and remediation process
start_phrase: For La Banque Postale UES, the procedure set up by the system for dealing with distressing situations at work is conducted in compliance with the principle of the presumption of innocence, with complete impartiality and with the discretion necessary to protect each person's dignity and privacy.
summary:
- Focus on social dialogue and employee engagement at CNP Assurances, including two agreements (constructive/effective dialogue and SEC), a QWLWC survey on engagement and well-being, and the “Let’s talk ambition” forum with the Executive Committee.
- 2024 social agreements advancing respect for human rights, notably on diversity and professional equality.
- Comprehensive processes at La Banque Postale UES for reporting and remediating distressing situations at work, grounded in presumption of innocence, impartiality, and confidentiality; covers moral/sexual harassment, sexist behavior, and broader well-being concerns.
- Multiple reporting channels (managers, HR, occupational health, employee reps, harassment officers, ethics officer/whistleblowing, social assistance), with employee awareness via intranet, code of conduct, training, and the 2024 Confirmodoc tool ensuring code of conduct distribution.
- Structured case handling: swift HR intake and registry, a 15-day listening phase, precautionary protections, conditional investigation with a joint steering committee (HR reps, SEC secretary, HSWC rapporteur), and outcomes ranging from support (medical/psychological) to disciplinary actions up to dismissal and organizational/process adjustments with effectiveness monitoring.
- Governance and oversight: Employee Relations Department interfaces with employee bodies and coordinates channels; HR monitors deployment and case management. Group whistleblowing platform accessible to all employees, with whistleblower protection, Compliance/Ethics oversight, and anonymized annual reporting to the Supervisory Board.
- Subsidiary mechanisms at CNP Assurances: Integrity Line whistleblowing (managed by Ethics), Internal Social Mediation (encrypted), and access via managers/HR; systems available across subsidiaries.
- Employee action plans and resources to prevent negative impacts on health and well-being: HR legal support and Life at Work division with health services; 2024 initiatives on traffic accident prevention, visual/hearing fatigue, sedentary lifestyle, workstation adjustments, and guidance on tool use and information overload.
- Hybrid/home-working framework: renewed three-year home-working agreement (2024), manager support planned for 2025, right-to-disconnect awareness, annual leave reminders, and planned 2025 measures for employee carers and a mental health prevention program.
- QWLWC agreement (signed September 2023 for three years) guiding action plan rollout over 2023–2026.
text:
3.1.4 Reporting and  remediation process
Reporting  distressing  situations  at work
For La Banque  Postale UES,  the procedure  set up by the
system for dealing with distressing situations at work is
conducted 
in compliance with the  principle of the presumption
of innocence, with complete impartiality and with the discretion
necessary to protect each person's dignity and privacy.
No information is disclosed beyond the circle of stakeholders.
Any employee who considers  themself to be a victim of
harassment  at work, or who is in a distressing  situation
that could harm their physical or mental health, has the
option 
of reporting this to their manager, the occupational
health 
service, employee representatives, harassment officers
or the ethics officer  (via the whistleblowing system  or the
social assistance  service).
Distressing situations at work that may be reported include
moral  harassment, sexual harassment,  sexist behaviour,
but also  any  problem  that  causes  a situation of  unease, or
even professional  burnout.
Employees  have several specific channels to raise their
concerns.  The Company has set up these channels, which
are partially implemented by experts (S EC, contact with
employee representatives, whistleblowing system,  system
for dealing with distressing situations at work).
​Reports  from employees can be received by the manager,
the various HR stakeholders (human resources manager,
occupational health department), employee representatives,
harassment  officers, the social worker or by the ethics
officer  (directly  or via the  whistleblowing platform). [S1_3_02]
La  Banque  Postale UES ensures that its employees are
informed  of the existence of this whistleblowing system
and  how it is used, via the Group's intranet. As part of the
recruitment process, all new Group employees receive a
paperless 
copy  of the  Internal Rules, to which  the  code of
conduct is attached. The latter contains detailed information
on the whistleblowing  channels  available to them.
All information concerning whistleblowing channels is also
available on the intranet site. In addition to this information,
the intranet also provides details of other mechanisms
such 
as the contacts of employee representatives and ways
of reporting distressing situations at work. To increase
awareness and  ensure that  employees  can have full
confidence in these mechanisms, training and communication
actions are regularly organised. Since 2024, a  tool called
Confirmodoc has been set up to verify the distribution of
the code of c onduct  to all employees and third parties
acting  for the Group.  [S1_3_06]  [S1_3_08]Processing reports
Reports are processed as quickly as possible by the Group’s
Human Resources Department, and recorded  in a dedicated
register.
Upon 
receipt of the report, the Human Resources Department
sets 
up a listening phase within 15 days. The purpose of
this first phase is to identify,  analyse and guide the alert in
order to verify whether the system is adapted to the
situation  of the employee  concerned.
The precautionary principle requires Human  Resources
managers in charge  of listening to  assess:
•whether the distressing situation of the person(s) requires
a referral to occupational health;
•whether 
there is a need for any temporary measures to
ensure the protection and safety of the employees involved.
At the  end  of the listening phase:
•if the information gathered at this stage allows the Human
Resources 
Department to make a decision, the investigation
phase as detailed below is not opened;
•if the information gathered at this stage does not allow
the Human Resources Department to make a decision,
the investigation phase is  opened.
During the investigation phase, a joint steering committee
is set up,  composed of two  representatives of the Human
Resources 
Department, the secretary of the Social and
Economic 
Committee (SEC) and the rapporteur of the
Health, Safety and Working Conditions Commission of the
SEC. This phase allows the two specialised HR contacts to
investigate 
any witnesses or persons who can  shed light
on the  situation, in  order  to identify  the  actions to be
taken to remedy it.
In the interests of combating moral harassment,  sexual
harassment and sexist behaviour, the  SEC and Human
Resources Department contacts are  responsible for
guiding, informing and supporting the employees who
contact them. Employees are informed of the regulations
in 
force through information, prevention and awareness-
raising actions.
At the end of any investigation phase, the Human Resources
Department 
decides on the actions to be implemented.
For example, these may include support measures provided
by the Company and intended to provide  medical and
psychological support  to the  victim.
The Human Resources  Department may  implement a
number of corrective measures:
•Disciplinary measures: employees are required to comply
with 
the internal rules and the code of conduct, which
specify the sanctions incurred in the event of moral or
sexual 
harassment, and sexist or violent acts. These sanctions
may  go as far as  dismissal for  gross  misconduct;
•Measures on work organisation and processes: if the
investigation 
reveals problems inherent in the work
organisation 
and processes implemented within the
team,  the Human Resources Department shall work
with 
the relevant department to take any measures that
it 
deems fit to resolve  the issue.  The effectiveness  of the
implemented  measures is monitored by the Human
Resources Department. 
[S1_3_05] [S1_4_02]Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1752Sustainable performance
Social information
The Employee Relations Department, which is affiliated to
the 
Human Resources Department, represents the Company
and  brings its policy before the employee representative
bodies (Social and  Economic  Committee,  employee
representatives as a whole), and ensures the monitoring
and  coordination  of these  channels.
The system for dealing with  distressing situations at work
is monitored by the Human Resources Department, which
records reports and ensures that the system is effectively
deployed and that individual situations are dealt with. [S1_3_07]
Process  for distressing situations at work 
in the subsidiaries
In its agreements, CNP Assurances describes its commitments
to remedy the negative impacts on its employees, and
exercises  constant due diligence to prevent any risk of
discrimination.
It has various specific reporting channels to collect and
process 
any report or alert submitted by a CNP Assurances
Group employee:
•Integrity  Line  whistleblowing system (online intranet
platform): reports are collected and processed by the
Group’s Ethics Officer and the Head of the Ethics Division;
•Internal 
Social Mediation (by email or telephone): reports
are processed  by the Mediator via an encrypted file.
CNP   Assurances ensures that its employees have access
to whistleblowing  and  report  processing  systems.
In addition, throughout the Group  reports can  be made
through line managers or human resources teams. The Group
whistleblowing system is also available to all employees of
the subsidiaries.  [S1_3_01]
Whistleblowing  system
A system for collecting and processing ethics reports is also
available  to all La  Banque Postale Group employees via a
specific platform. This system is described in Section 2.4.1.3.5
“Independence and accessibility of the whistleblowing system”.
Information 
on the system is provided to employees, notably
through the code  of conduct.  [S1_3_05]  [S1_4_02]
Whistleblower protection is also in place, in accordance
with  the rules.  [S1_3_09]
The whistleblowing system is monitored by the Compliance
Department through the Ethics teams. A report on the
monitoring  of this system and the situations reported
(anonymised)  is presented  to the Supervisory Board on an
annual basis.  [S1_3_07]2.3.1.5 Employee action plans and resources

title: Actions implemented and resources allocated
heading: 2.3.1.5.1 Actions implemented and resources allocated
start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group implements various actions to prevent or mitigate its potential negative impacts on its employees.
summary:
- Scope and governance: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) detailing HR governance, with the Employee Relations Department and HR overseeing employee dialogue and handling distressing work situations; Compliance/Ethics teams monitor whistleblowing; Supervisory Board and its committees review social and remuneration indicators.

- Whistleblowing and protections: Multiple reporting channels across La Banque Postale and CNP Assurances (Integrity Line platform, internal social mediation, HR/line managers, La Poste Group platform), anonymous options, employee communications via code of conduct, and explicit whistleblower protection; annual anonymized reporting to the Supervisory Board.

- Preventing negative impacts on employees:
  - Working conditions and health: Measures addressing stress, burnout, MSDs, traffic accidents, visual/hearing fatigue, sedentary risks; workstation adjustments; guidance on digital tool use and preventing information overload; renewed three‑year home‑working agreement (2024) with right‑to‑disconnect awareness and annual leave reminders; hybrid work and meeting practices to be manager‑supported in 2025; negotiations for caregiver measures and a mental health prevention program slated for 2025.
  - Resources: Dedicated prevention/health/safety budget, 2024 hybrid work survey, budget for workstation adjustments, €250 equipment loan every five years for home working. CNP offers LYFE (health services, counseling, remote consults) and Ulteam (stress/concentration education) platforms.
  - Remuneration and purchasing power: Annual market benchmarks, manager training on fair treatment, guaranteed salary increase after maternity/adoption leave, annual gender equality index monitoring (all entities ≥92/100 in 2024), €600k/year budget since 2022 to close unexplained wage gaps; local social dialogue at CNP in countries without centrally governed increases to safeguard purchasing power.
  - Anti‑discrimination and harassment: Disability and Diversity/Professional Equality agreements with targets and action plans (role models, ERGs, working groups, awareness activities); executive sponsorship, dedicated D&I team, partnerships and charters (Diversity & Equal Opportunities, L’Autre Cercle for LGBT+, STOPE against sexism); clear alert, prevention, and sanction policy; participation in PAQTE with targets to host 200 youths (2022–2025).

- Promoting positive impacts:
  - Inclusion, development, and fair conditions: Internal training via École de la Banque et du Réseau for business and personal development; La Poste Group data and AI training pathways; gender equality initiatives (mentoring, representation targets, corrective hiring where imbalanced); social fund to support employees facing severe medical or accident‑related hardship.

- HR risk mitigation: Regular medical visit tracking with occupational health partners; occupational health policy with SIAMT (Île‑de‑France); cultural transformation program; comprehensive QWLWC initiative covering work content/organization, health and prevention, work‑life balance, information overload, and a structured, indicator‑driven, multi‑stakeholder prevention approach with continuous improvement.

- Monitoring and decision‑making: Effectiveness tracked via engagement survey, ad‑hoc surveys (e.g., hybrid work 2024), remuneration indicators, social protection scheme reviews, OHS indicators, disability agreement metrics, incidents from whistleblowing, and medical visit completion; HR Management Committee proposes measures, approved by Executive Committee and aligned with strategic/financial planning.

- Business practices and data: Sales practices unlikely to amplify social risks due to regulation; purchasing specifications integrate employee health and safety criteria; strong safeguards for employee data privacy.

- Contribution to SDGs: Primary impacts on SDG3 (Good health and well‑being), SDG8 (Decent work), and SDG10 (Reduced inequalities), with additional links to SDG13 (Climate action) via employee volunteering; SDG‑aligned employee savings fund; leave donation mechanisms (Mathys law) and encouragement to donate time savings; annual public SDG contribution report.
text:
3.1.5.1 Actions implemented 
and resources allocated
Avoidance of  negative impacts
La  Banque  Postale Group implements various actions to
prevent  or mitigate its potential negative impacts on its
employees.
Working 
conditions affecting the physical or mental health
of employees (
e.g. stress, burnout, musculoskeletal disorders)
To remedy the impacts related to working conditions, an
employment 
law division supports local HR players to take
charge of all collective or individual files  on all aspects of
employee relations. The Life at Work division works in
conjunction 
with the health service to identify and implement
solutions adap ted to the observed impacts.
The specific actions carried out in 2024 to avoid the negative
impacts of working  conditions include:
•Preventing traffic accidents;
•Preventing visual and  hearing  fatigue;
•Preventing a sedentary lifestyle.
Workstation  adjustments were also made to prevent or
mitigate  musculoskeletal disorders.
The use of work  tools  and  preventing  information
overload  are also concerns for La Banque Postale UES. In
this respect, the practices for using work tools and the
information  overload prevention system are available on
the intranet.
These issues are particularly topical due to the increased
popularity  of hybrid working methods, and particularly
working from home.
Work and meeting organisation practices,  particularly in
hybrid mode, are also reiterated in the new home-working
agreement (renewed  for three years  in 2024). They will be
specifically supported by managers in 2025.
As part of the roll-out of the new home-working agreement,
an 
employee awareness campaign on the right to disconnect
is 
scheduled, and annual reminder campaigns on taking
leave are  carried  out each  year.
The Group is also particularly attentive to the specific
circumstances 
of employees who are carers and the
mental 
health of employees. The opening of negotiations
on measures for employees who are carers is scheduled
for the beginning of  2025, and a mental  health prevention
programme is also being looked into for 2025.
These various actions are intended for all employees of
La  Banque  Postale UES. As the QWLWC agreement was
signed 
in September 2023 for a period of  three years, the
associated action plans will be rolled out over the same
period.176 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
La  Banque  Postale UES has allocated  the following
specific resources  to these topics:
•There  is a  dedicated budget for prevention, health and
safety 
at work. This recurring budget may be supplemented,
if necessary, by any resources  required to implement
the annual  action  plan (seeking service  providers  with
expertise  in health  or occupational risk prevention);
•A survey on  hybrid  working was also  carried out in 2024
among all employees, to draw up an assessment of the
home-working agreement;
•There is  a special  budget for  workstation  adjustments;
•An equipment loan (€250 every five years) is also supported
by the home-working agreement, to improve working
conditions at home.
Finally, to promote a culture of prevention and well-being
at work, CNP  Assurances has set  up two platforms:
•The LYFE platform, which gives its employees quick access
to personalised health services and content (psychological
listening  service,  remote consultations, personalised
programmes based on formal questionnaires,  etc.);
•The Ulteam  platform, which provides educational content
on stress  management,  concentration and other health-
related  topics.
These tools offer comprehensive and personalised support.
Deterioration 
in remuneration levels, the number of jobs
or the type of contract leading to a decrease in the
purchasing  power of employees
La  Banque  Postale Group acts  to prevent the negative
impact  of a potential deterioration in remuneration levels,
and to ensure fair remuneration for work, based on expertise,
length of service  and  professional  experience.
To this end,  La  Banque  Postale Group prepares internal
benchmarks and market references each year for all
employees, provided by a firm specialising in the financial
services market.
In addition, to prevent unequal remuneration, the Group
trains  its managers in  providing fair treatment at all key
moments in Company life, in order to prevent discriminatory
decisions or behaviours.
La Banque Postale UES also guarantees a minimum salary
increase beyond what is legally required to employees
who have been on  maternity or adoption  leave during the
year . This amount  is determined based on  the individual
increase budgeted for  in the salary policy.
Each  Group entity monitors the gender equality index
annually to address any remuneration  gaps. If the gender
equality  index score  is below  85/100, progress targets for
each  indicator will be calculated  and disclosed. For the
2024  financial year, all La   Banque  Postale Group entities
have  an equality  index  greater  than  or equal to 92/100.Since  2022, La  Banque  Postale has allocated an overall
budget
 of €600,000 per year to reducing  wage gaps. If a
gap of more than 5% is identified, an in-depth individual
analysis 
is carried out by the manager and the HR Department.
If the gap  cannot be explained by  target criteria such as
the level of training, responsibility, experience and length
of 
service, skills  and performance, La  Banque  Postale is
committed to a salary review within the limit of the budget
set each year as part of the mandatory annual negotiations.
CNP 
Assurances, which has a presence outside Europe, is
particularly attentive to this issue. In particular, in
countries 
in which salary increases are not governed by
the administration of the country (State, region, etc.) or
the contractual branch, CNP  Assurances brings together
employee  representatives  and management at a local
level  to discuss the  Company’s economic and  financial
situation, the official inflation levels and the impact on the
purchasing power of employees. The purpose of these
discussions  is to determine the best way to maintain the
purchasing power of employees while protecting the
Company’s economic interests.
Cases  of discrimination, inequality or harassment with
negative consequences for employees and non-compliance
with other work-related rights  (covered by European
regulations)
La  Banque  Postale UES is committed to preventing all
types of discrimination and promoting inclusion and equal
opportunities, through two  major  social agreements: the
Disability  agreement and the Diversity and Professional
Equality agreement. Each year, these agreements give
rise to a comprehensive  action  plan that includes:
•Quantitative targets (disability, gender equality, generations);
•Concrete  actions, such as:
•Creating role models;
•Creating think  tank  and  working groups ;
•Setting  up the Employee Resources Group;
•Awareness-raising and acculturation actions, joint creation
workshops, webinars, etc.
To carry out these action plans, La Banque Postale relies on:
•a dedicated  Diversity and Inclusion  team;
•the empowerment of executives and managers through
regular 
reporting,  sponsorship actions at the  Executive
Committee level  and  identifying role  models;
•entering into partnerships with leading charities on the
theme of diversity  in business;
•charities for resources and discussions with other companies
(AFMD, Entreprises pour la  Cité);
•associations that audit and certify actions and commitments:
Diversity and Equal Opportunities Charter, signed in 2013
(Entreprises pour la Cité), L'Autre Cercle Charter for
LGBT+ employees, signed in 2024, STOPE initiative (AFMD)
to fight against everyday sexism, signed in 2022.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1772Sustainable performance
Social information
Finally, 
these measures and commitments are accompanied
by a prevention, alert and sanction policy. The whistleblowing
channels  are clearly signposted for all La Banque Postale
Group 
employees (practical guides, intranet, HR and managers).
The 
Group uses a shared La Poste Group platform to submit
reports, whether anonymously or not. All of  these components
comprise a policy which endeavours  to provide the most
fair and inclusive working environment possible, which is
against  any form  of discrimination or harassment.
In addition, CNP Assurances, as part of its commitment to
equal 
opportunities, has joined the PAQTE initiative (Pacte
avec les Quartiers pour Tous les Entreprises – Pact with
the districts for all  companies) launched in  2018 by the
French State. For this reason, CNP  Assurances has set
itself  the  target  of taking on  at least  200  young  work-
study students or interns from  priority districts or who
have  dropped out of school between 2022 and 2025.
[S1_4_01]  [S1_4_09]  [S1_MDR_A_01_12]
Actions  to promote  positive impacts
In addition to actions to limit the identified negative impacts
or to remedy  them, La Banque Postale has implemented
actions  to promote  its positive impacts on its employees.
Actions to promote inclusion, protection, equal opportunities,
skills  development and  professional  development of
employees
All of the actions  presented above and aimed at avoiding
negative impacts in the event of harassment, discrimination
or inequality are also intended to generate positive impacts
on inclusion, protection and equal opportunities for employees.
In addition, to promote employee skills development, the
Group  is committed to rolling out its skills development
plan . In order to do so, La   Banque  Postale relies on an
internal training organisation (École de la Banque et du
Réseau) 
to manage the business line training programmes,
led 
by internal resources (trainers) or, failing that, by external
service providers.
Running  training in-house gives La  Banque  Postale the
ability to roll out ambitious skills development plans,
which  include  training that meets  employee expectations.
The École de la Banque et du Réseau also offers a wide
range of group  and individual training offers to support
personal 
development, and therefore actively helps to develop
the 
employability of its employees within La Banque Postale
but also  on the market.
Favourable working conditions for the Group’s own workers
(working 
hours, social dialogue, fair remuneration system,
social protection,  collective  agreements, etc.)
To supplement the actions carried out on remuneration,
there are initiatives in place for gender equality (mentoring
programme  for women, targets  for  representation of
women  in management  positions, hiring of people of the
underrepresented gender with comparable  skills and
qualifications when the profession  or department has
an imbalance).
Finally,  to provide financial  support for employees in
difficult situations following a medical procedure or a life-
threatening  accident, in addition to the social protection
scheme,  a social fund is planned, which will be open to all
employees  of La Banque  Postale UES.  [S1_4_03]HR risk mitigation actions
HR risk relating to the failure of the Group’s employment
and employee health  and safety  practices.
To mitigate this risk, the Group is implementing the following
actions:
•Medical 
visits are monitored on a regular basis, in
collaboration with the occupational health service.
An update of the Company’s files by the partner health
services in the regions is to  be put in place;
•An occupational health policy has been set up with the
Île-de-France (Paris region) occupational  health  service
(SIAMT), based on the support and management services
offered.
As 
part of the Company’s transformation plan, there is a
dedicated cultural transformation project which supports
managers and employees in their work-related practices.
In 
addition, La  Banque  Postale has launched a QWLWC
project which aims to implement measures relating to:
•defining and  implementing a  comprehensive QWLWC
approach shared  by all stakeholders in  the  Company,
designating and grouping the following  components:
•work content: streamlining work organisation and working
methods, promoting workload regulation, thus enabling
high-quality work;
•prevention and  health at work: protecting the physical
and mental  health of  employees;
•work relations: facilitating work-life  balance;
•tackling  information  overload  (infobesity);
•creating a  multi-disciplinary  approach to the primary
prevention of occupational risks, in order to protect
the physical and  mental health and safety of employees
and, more generally, contribute to their well-being at
work, broken down into various phases:
•analyse  and objectify situations by  relying specifically
on indicators;
•build the approach by involving the various stakeholders;
•involve all stakeholders in the Company in QWLWC issues;
•use trial and  error and implement gradual steps as
part of a continuous improvement approach;
•monitor the actions implemented and progress made;
•promote  good  work relationships at every stage of
employees’ professional lives  by making integration a
driver  of alignment with the Company's values and
culture, 
and by ensuring a work-life balance throughout
their career. 
[S1_4_06]178 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
Actions  to develop  HR opportunities
Development  of the skills of the Company’s employees
promoting  innovation  and  the creation  of new  products
and services
In order to  address this opportunity at CNP  Assurances,
the 
Company offers various career paths and training courses
to strengthen business expertise,  develop versatile skills
and respond to priority projects. Support is based on adapted
offers, professionalising systems, certifying training courses
and attention to cross-functional skills (autonomy, innovation,
agility).  Initiatives on strategic  issues (ecology, artificial
intelligence, QWLWC ) and  individual  support  (mobility,
coaching, mentoring)  promote  continuous learning, with
employees involved in their  development supported by
trained  managers.
In addition, a  Data and Artificial  Intelligence training (AI)
programme is  offered  by La  Poste and  is available  to all
Group  employees.  Several  training  courses  are available
(Data  Academy, Objectif AI, etc.) and aim to support the
development  of skills in this area. These training courses
also aim to promote the emergence of innovative data- or
AI-based projects.  [S1_4_07]

title: Monitoring the effectiveness of actions
heading: 2.3.1.5.2 Monitoring the effectiveness of actions
start_phrase: To assess the effectiveness of the actions implemented, La Banque Postale Group relies on several categories of indicators:
summary:
- Focus on sustainable performance and social information within La Banque Postale Group, emphasizing HR development, skills building, and innovation.
- Employee development at CNP Assurances through diverse career paths, professional and certifying trainings, and cross‑functional skills (autonomy, innovation, agility), with initiatives on ecology, AI, and quality of life at work, plus individual support (mobility, coaching, mentoring).
- Group-wide Data and AI upskilling via La Poste’s programs (e.g., Data Academy, Objectif AI) to build competencies and foster data/AI-driven projects.
- Robust monitoring of HR actions using multiple indicators: annual engagement/QWL survey, ad‑hoc internal surveys (e.g., hybrid work), remuneration tracking, annual review of social protection schemes, OHS/HSWCC reporting, disability agreement indicators, whistleblowing on discrimination/harassment/sexist behavior, and medical visit compliance.
- Governance and oversight by the Supervisory Board through its Appointments & Governance and Remunerations Committees; annual review of key social indicators including gender parity.
- Decision-making on preventing/mitigating negative workforce impacts led by HR Management Committee and approved by the Executive Committee within strategic and annual target setting.
- Risk management: sales practices pose low amplification of negative impacts due to regulation; purchasing practices incorporate health and safety criteria; strong attention to employee data privacy and responsible data use.
- Contribution to SDGs: primary impacts on SDG3 (Good health and well‑being), SDG8 (Decent work), SDG10 (Reduced inequalities), with additional actions supporting SDG13 (Climate action) via the “Tous Engagés” volunteer program.
- Employee savings options aligned with the UN SDGs and leave‑donation schemes (per Mathys law and its extension) to support carers and families, reinforcing SDG3.
- Annual public reporting of SDG contributions and related indicators.
text:
3.1.5.2 Monitoring the effectiveness of actions
To assess the effectiveness of the actions implemented,
La  Banque  Postale Group relies on several  categories of
indicators:
•the annual engagement survey (quality of life at work
indicator);
•ad-hoc 
internal surveys (for example on hybrid work in 2024);
•indicators which monitor  remuneration;
•annual monitoring of the social protection scheme, carried
out to ensure the financial  balance of the scheme and
the relevance of  its coverage  for employees.  If necessary,
decisions to add or modify them may be made, in particular
to ensure  the regulatory compliance of the plan;
•OHS report indicators, presented quarterly to the HSWCC;
•indicators for the  social agreement on disability, as well
as the gap  in relation to the  statutory  indicator;
•incidents of discrimination, harassment or sexist behaviour
reported  through  whistleblowing channels;
•the rate  of completion of  medical  visits  for all employees
(compliance).
These  indicators  form  part of the  social  report.
The Supervisory  Board  oversees these  matters through
its  Appointments and Governance Committee and its
Remunerations Committee. In particular, it adopts and
regularly reviews the remuneration practices and processes
and the Group’s remuneration policy, and monitors its
implementation,  in collaboration  with  the  Remuneration
Committee. In addition,  the main  social indicators, such as
the results of the  social survey or gender parity indicators,
are presented  annually  to the Supervisory Board. [S1_4_04]La  Banque  Postale UES decides which measures are
necessary 
and appropriate to deal with an actual or potential
negative impact on its own  workforce,  through  strategic
decisions  taken by the Human Resources Department's
Management  Committee. These decisions are approved
by the Group’s  Executive Committee as part of the setting
of annual targets and the strategic plan. Financial items
are arbitrated as part of the financial  years. [S1_4_05]
The material negative impacts identified are not likely to
be amplified by La Banque Postale Group’s sales practices,
due 
to the highly regulated nature of the banking services
sector. On the other hand, purchasing practices can affect
the safety and physical health of employees, based on the
working 
environment  made available to employees.
La Banque Postale is attentive to the health of its employees,
and  ensures that in its  purchasing practices and the
specifications  of the relevant purchasing categories take
into account relevant criteria to meet health and safety issues.
In 
addition, as  an employer that respects the privacy of its
employees, La Banque Postale is careful not to cause any
impact on its employees through the use of their data.
The 
Group’s practices in terms of data management and
use reflect these considerations.  [S1_4_08]
2.

title: Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
heading: 2.3.1.5.3 Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
start_phrase: Through its actions, La Banque Postale Group also has positive impacts on other Sustainable Development Goals.
summary:
- Focus on employee development and innovation:
  - Multiple career paths and professional training to build business expertise and versatile, cross-functional skills (autonomy, innovation, agility).
  - Strategic upskilling on ecology, artificial intelligence, quality of work life, with individual support (mobility, coaching, mentoring).
  - Group-wide Data and AI training programs (e.g., Data Academy, Objectif AI) to foster AI/data capabilities and innovative projects.

- Monitoring effectiveness and governance:
  - Use of diverse indicators: annual engagement survey (QWL), ad-hoc surveys (e.g., hybrid work), remuneration monitoring, social protection scheme reviews, OHS indicators, disability agreement metrics, whistleblowing reports on discrimination/harassment/sexist behavior, and completion of medical visits.
  - Supervisory Board oversight via Appointments & Governance and Remunerations Committees; annual review of social indicators (e.g., gender parity).
  - HR decisions on managing negative impacts approved by the Executive Committee; financial arbitration aligned with fiscal years.
  - Attention to employee health and safety in purchasing specifications; strong employee data privacy practices.

- Contribution to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
  - Core impacts on SDG3 (Good health and well-being), SDG8 (Decent work), and SDG10 (Reduced inequalities).
  - “Tous Engagés” volunteering program supporting SDG13 (Climate action) and SDG10.
  - Employee savings offering SDG-aligned investment funds.
  - Leave donation scheme for carers under Mathys law (SDG3) and encouragement to donate time-savings days.
  - Annual public booklet detailing SDG contributions and indicators.

- Environmental transition and employees:
  - No significant negative impact from the green transition on banking/insurance roles.
  - Extensive “Just Transition Programme” training:
    - Basic track: climate risk regulation, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresco, eco-behavior modules (climate, responsible digital, sustainable consumption), and responsible finance.
    - Specialized tracks by business line: integrating just transition into practices (commercial tools, ESG financing analysis, responsible communication, supplier relations/responsible purchasing, biodiversity in finance).
  - ESG targets embedded in remuneration to reinforce engagement.

- Target setting and review process:
  - Targets derived from policies, ambitions, legal obligations; negotiated with employee representatives where applicable.
  - HR roadmap governed by quarterly committee meetings and annual reviews; agreement-based targets monitored by dedicated commissions.
  - Targets and roadmap communicated to all employees via intranet.
  - Subsidiaries set aligned targets; CNP Assurances includes HR targets within corporate agreements and purpose.

- Current targets:
  - Promote favorable working conditions (working hours, social dialogue, fair pay, social protection, collective agreements).
  - Quality of Work Life (QWL) measured via annual engagement survey across the UES; resources and communications (e.g., leave, right to disconnect) available on intranet.
  - QWL target set at a score greater than 7 for La Banque Postale SA and La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring (UES).
text:
3.1.5.3 Contribution  to the Sustainable 
Development Goals (SDGs)
Through its actions, La  Banque  Postale Group also has
positive impacts on  other  Sustainable Development G oals.
By design, the actions  carried  out under S1 have an  impact
on good health and well-being (SDG3), reduced inequalities
within 
the Company (SDG10),  and  decent  work (SDG8).
The actions implemented by La Banque Postale on specific
themes  may also have positive impacts under other SDGs
selected by  La Banque Postale.
For example,  as part of the "All Engaged"  (“Tous Engagés”)
programme, La  Banque  Postale offers its employees the
opportunity  to volunteer with charities committed to
serving  the  environment (SDG13:  Climate action) or  to
reducing inequalities within the French economy (SDG10:
Reduced  inequalities).
Through its remuneration policy, and more specifically in
respect 
of employee savings, La  Banque  Postale allows
employees to invest in a fund covering a large investment
universe (around 25 funds), all in connection with the United
Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
Lastly, under the French Mathys law (2014) on the donation
of leave by employees to parents of seriously ill children
and 
its extension to carers on 15 February 2018,
La  Banque  Postale employees can now donate days of
leave 
to one of their colleagues who is a carer (SDG3: Good
health and well-being). In addition, La  Banque  Postale
encourages  holders of a time savings account to donate
days of leave, to support a community initiative by making a
one-off donation  in the form of monetised  rest days.
Each  year, La  Banque  Postale publishes a booklet  on its
institutional website, detailing its contribution to each of
the SDGs as well as the related indicators. [S1_4_18]Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1792Sustainable performance

title: Impact of the environmental transition on employees
heading: 2.3.1.5.4 Impact of the environmental transition on employees
start_phrase: As La Banque Postale Group operates in the banking and insurance sector, the activities of its employees are not impacted by a significant negative impact due to the transition to a greener and climate neutral economy.
summary:
- Assesses the impact of the environmental transition on employees, noting no significant negative effects for a banking/insurance workforce but emphasizing proactive support and awareness-raising.
- Details the “Just Transition Programme” training delivered via the École de la Banque et du Réseau:
  - Basic course for all employees (since 2022): mandatory climate risk training, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresco workshops, and learning cycles on eco-friendly behaviors (climate, responsible digital, sustainable consumption) and responsible finance.
  - Specialized courses by business line: practical integration of just transition into roles, including commercial tools and speaking, ESG analysis of financing, responsible communication, supplier relations and responsible purchasing, and biodiversity in finance.
- Embeds ESG competencies long term and links ESG objectives to all employees’ remuneration, monitored through a mission-led company indicator to boost awareness and engagement.
- Explains the employee target-setting process:
  - Targets aligned with group policies, ambitions, and legal requirements; negotiated with employee representatives under an Executive Committee framework by HR.
  - HR roadmap governed by the HR Management Committee with quarterly monitoring and annual reviews; agreement-based targets tracked by monitoring commissions.
  - Targets and roadmap shared on the intranet; results analyzed annually and adjusted as needed; subsidiaries (including CNP Assurances) align their own HR targets.
- Presents specific employee targets on working conditions and quality of life at work (QWL):
  - QWL measured via the annual engagement survey covering La Banque Postale UES employees; resources and policies (e.g., leave, right to disconnect) communicated on the intranet.
  - QWL score target set at greater than 7, covering employees of La Banque Postale SA and La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring.
text:
3.1.5.4
Impact  of the environmental  transition 
on employees
As La Banque Postale Group operates in the banking and
insurance  sector, the activities of its employees  are not
impacted  by a  significant negative impact due to the
transition to  a greener  and  climate  neutral  economy.
However,  La Banque Postale  SA has implemented several
types of actions with its employees to raise their awareness
and support  them  on these issues.
Firstly,  it organises training sessions for its employees, to
enable  them to better understand the impacts associated
with  this transition  on their activities or their customers.
The Bank relies on the École de  la Banque et  du Réseau to
train and raise awareness among its employees on ESG-
related 
topics. This training programme, known as the “Just
Transition Programme ”, is divided into  two main courses:
•The “basic”  training course:
This  course aims  to raise awareness of climate, societal
and environmental issues, and has been available to all
employees  since 2022. It  includes mandatory regulatory
training  on climate risks, an e-learning course dedicated
to sustainability,  participatory activities (Climate  Fresco)
and two topical sustainability learning cycles on eco-friendly
behaviours (three topics:  climate, responsible digital
technology and sustainable consumption) as well as
responsible finance (two topics: concept, behind the scenes);
•Specialised  courses for  each business  line:
These courses are designed to incorporate the challenges
of 
the just transition into the professional practices specific
to each business  line. They  enable employees to take
concrete action by adapting their practices, offers  and
processes. They  include  proficiency  in commercial tools
and  speaking, ESG analysis of business or public sector
financing files, the basics  of responsible communication,
a deep dive into supplier relations and responsible
purchasing  as well as a course on biodiversity in the
financial sector.
This  structured programme aims to embed ESG skills over
the long term, therefore strengthening the commitment
of all La Banque  Postale  employees.
In addition, all employees have ESG targets integrated
into  their  remuneration  packages (additional  information
is available in paragraph 2.1.2.5 “Alignment of remuneration
with La   Banque  Postale's sustainability  targets”).
This  commitment, monitored  by mission-led company
indicator 1.2, also  serves to raise employee  awareness and
ensure that employees engage with sustainability issues.
[S1_4_19]2.3.1.6

title: Target setting process
heading: 2.3.1.6.1 Target setting process
start_phrase: Targets are set in light of La Banque Postale Group’s policies and ambitions, and its legal obligations.
summary:

- Impact of environmental transition on employees:

text:
3.1.6.1 Target setting process
Targets 
are set in light of La Banque Postale Group’s policies
and  ambitions, and its legal obligations. When targets are
set in agreements signed  with employee representatives,
they  are discussed and approved for the duration  of the
agreement  with them. The negotiation framework (for the
remuneration 
policy or the diversity agreement, for example)
is set by the Executive Committee and negotiated by the
Human 
Resources Department and employee representatives.
[S1_5_01]
The La Banque Postale UES Human Resources Department
roadmap, 
which sets out its targets and monitors their
achievement, 
is managed through dedicated  meetings of
the Human Resources Department Management Committee.
These meetings take place quarterly, with an annual review.
The targets set within the  framework of agreements are
monitored by monitoring commissions throughout the
duration of the  agreements.
The targets and the roadmap are shared with all employees
via
 the intranet. [S1_5_02]
During the annual  review of the Human Resources Department
roadmap, 
and the setting of targets for the year Y+1, the
HRD 
Management Committee analyses the results for the

The 
targets set within the framework of the agreements

Group subsidiaries also set targets in line with their
