title: Targets set
heading: 2.3.1.6.2 Targets set
start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has set targets with regard to the identified impacts, risks and opportunities.
summary:
- Scope and context: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) detailing how the Group manages employee-related impacts, targets, and indicators, including governance of target-setting and reporting scope.

- Environmental transition and employees:
  - Minimal direct negative impact on banking/insurance roles.
  - Extensive ESG awareness and capability-building via the Just Transition Programme:
    - Basic course (mandatory climate risk training, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresk, learning cycles on eco-behaviors and responsible finance).
    - Specialized, business-line courses (adapting practices/offers, ESG analysis of financing, responsible communication, supplier relations, responsible purchasing, biodiversity in finance).
  - ESG targets integrated into all employees’ remuneration; monitored as a mission-led company indicator.

- Target-setting governance:
  - Targets aligned with Group policies, ambitions, legal obligations; negotiated with employee representatives where applicable.
  - HR Department roadmap overseen by the HR Management Committee (quarterly reviews, annual validation/adjustment).
  - Agreement-based targets monitored by dedicated commissions; roadmap shared on intranet.
  - Subsidiaries align targets with their remuneration policy/strategy; CNP Assurances also sets HR targets.

- Key targets, actions, and performance:
  - Working conditions and quality of life at work (QWL):
    - Target: QWL indicator >7; 2024 score 7.2/10 (up 0.1).
    - Broad internal communication of survey results and provisions (right to disconnect, leave, etc.).
  - Health and psychosocial risk (PSR) prevention:
    - Target: 100% of managers trained on PSR; achieved 85% as of 31/12/2024 (ongoing due to managerial turnover).
    - Occupational H&S plan on intranet; coordinated HR/manager actions to prevent absenteeism.
  - Inclusion, equal opportunity, and skills:
    - Disability employment: aim to meet/exceed 6% statutory rate; quarterly/biannual monitoring and regular awareness actions.
    - Training: target 100% completion of regulatory training; monthly tracking and reminders; monitoring of training hours/days and six‑year legal review; quarterly oversight of the Skills Development Plan; Supervisory Board monitors training as a risk metric.
    - Gender diversity: mission target >43% women among strategic managers and senior executives; 40.5% at 31/12/2024.
    - Harassment: zero-tolerance stance with an action-focused approach; cases monitored quarterly; no numeric reduction target to avoid under-reporting.
  - HR risk focus (2024): health and harassment.
    - Medical visit compliance: target full compliance for all employees/types of visits; regional outsourcing to PrestaMed launched to strengthen scheduling/monitoring; ongoing communications and intranet info.
  - Remuneration and purchasing power:
    - Objective of 100% adequate wages; most employees covered by favorable collective agreements; annual wage negotiations.
    - No numeric targets for gender/executive pay gaps; aim for objective, role-based pay fairness.
  - Social dialogue and work-life balance:
    - Robust representative bodies and annual monitoring commissions; quality of dialogue assessed via surveys/relations rather than a numeric target.
    - Professional elections held Nov 2023; next in 2027.
    - New home‑working agreement signed 14 Nov 2024; work‑life balance tracked via QWL and hybrid work surveys.
    - Comprehensive social protection; social fund to cover low-coverage benefits; justified exemptions to healthcare plan.

- Opportunities:
  - Skills development fosters innovation; no separate target beyond existing training/skills objectives.

- Workforce indicators and reporting scope:
  - Coverage: La Banque Postale SA and all financially consolidated subsidiaries; includes permanent, fixed-term, and other contracts (apprentices, professionalization; excludes interns).
  - CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (created 31/12/2024) included for specific indicators (employee characteristics except departures/turnover, collective bargaining coverage, age breakdown, adequate wages, disability, H&S policy).
  - Unless stated otherwise, indicators calculated as of 31 December 2024.
text:
3.1.6.2 Targets  set
La  Banque  Postale Group has set targets with regard to
the identified impacts, risks  and opportunities.
Favourable  working conditions for La  Banque  Postale
Group employees (working hours, social dialogue, fair
remuneration  system, social protection, collective
agreements , etc.) (positive  impact)
Quality of life at work is measured using the QWL indicator
from 
the annual engagement survey. All employees of
La  Banque  Postale UES are covered. The provisions on
quality  of life at work are published on the intranet,
and  therefore  available  to all employees. Communication
campaigns are run on different topics such as leave  and
the right to disconnect.
Satisfaction with working  environment and conditions is
measured by the QWL indicator from the annual engagement
survey, and is one of the cornerstones of La Banque Postale’s
HR policy.
The 
expected target for this QWL indicator is more than 7
The index includes all employees of La Banque Postale SA
and 
La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring (La Banque Postale
UES).180 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
The score for the 2024 annual survey was 7.2/10, up 0.1 point
since 2023.
In addition to the engagement indicator, the overall
results  of the survey are proactively communicated by
the  Communications  Department, the operational HR
stakeholders and by managers.
Working  conditions affecting the  physical or mental
health of employees (e.g. stress, burnout, musculoskeletal
disorders)  (negative  impact)
Indeed, protecting physical and mental health is an employer's
obligation to all  its employees. At La   Banque  Postale,
managers receive mandatory training on the prevention
of psychosocial  risks (PSR). The  target to be achieved is:
100% of managers must have completed the PSR
prevention  training. It covers employees with managerial
responsibilities in 2024.
The occupational health and safety plan is available  on the
intranet.  In addition, communication actions  are regularly
implemented  with managers to raise their awareness of
these  issues. They are supplemented by a system for
coordinating  HR  and managerial teams  on occupational
health  and  preventing  absenteeism.
The rate  of training  of managers  in the  prevention of  PSR
was 85%  as of 31  December 2024. Over the  calendar year,
the 100% coverage rate is difficult to achieve in view of the
continuous 
flow of arrivals and departures in management
roles. Nevertheless, La Banque Postale wishes to maintain
this ambitious target, which it communicates regularly to
its managers.
Actions to promote inclusion, protection, equal opportunities,
skills  development and  professional  development of
employees (positive  impact)
For diversity and inclusion, La   Banque  Postale has set  a
target for the employment of people with disabilities
and aims  to reach or exceed the  statutory rate of 6%.
The targets of the diversity and inclusion policy cover all
French 
employees of La Banque Postale (UES), and cover
the 
implementation of the commitments of the regulations,
the 
Company’s social agreements and the Diversity division
action plan. The indicators  are monitored quarterly for
disability and biannually for diversity, during the monitoring
committee meeting  for the  related  social agreement.
The measurement period  is that of the  social agreement,
i.e. three years. The expectations and  indicators relating to
the Disability and Diversity policy are regularly reported on
the Company’s intranet. This  information is  accompanied
by awareness-raising,  workshops  and  recurring actions on
diversity and disability for all employees. Specific initiatives
and  events are  carried out for managers and the HR
department.
Disability indicators are available in Section 2.3.1.7.5 “Disability
situations”.
In terms of skills development, La Banque Postale has set
itself  the target of ensuring that 100% of its employees
comply  with regulatory training . To guarantee this
commitment, monthly reports are prepared and reminders
are sent to employees who have not yet completed their
training. 
In addition, each year, La Banque Postale assesses
the number of employees trained (monitoring carried out
in number of hours per employee). This ambition is also
monitored  on a monthly basis by the Supervisory Board as
part  of the Group’s  risk management.Monthly monitoring is also carried out on all training sessions
(number of training days and number of employees
trained), with the aim of  achieving the highest possible
level  of training hours  per employee  each year.
As part of the “six-year review”, the École de la Banque et
du 
Réseau provides the HR Department with an annual
follow-up of employees who could be impacted by a lack
of 
training, within the meaning of French law no. 2014-288
of 
5 March 2014 on professional training, employment
and social  democracy.
In addition, the Skills Development Plan is monitored
quarterly by the departments of La  Banque   Postale and
Human Resources. The results are presented each year in
the SEC, including  the balance sheet for the previous year
and the current  skills development plan. Since 2020, these
aspects have also been included  in the sustainability
reporting produced by La Banque Postale’s departments.
In terms of diversity, as part of its mission-led company
status, La Banque Postale  has set itself the goal of exceeding
the 
threshold of  43% women among strategic managers
and 
senior executives (target 3.1 of the mission-led company).
This 
target covers employees of La  Poste SA (Financial
Services and Banking Advice Line), La Banque Postale SA
and the six main  subsidiaries and is monitored by the
Supervisory Board.
Unlike the  management bodies at the top of the pyramid,
strategic managers and senior executives are not subject
to regulatory measures.
At 31 December 2024, 40.5% of the Group’s strategic managers
and senior executives  were women.
Finally, no target  has been set concerning dealing with
harassment or distressing situations at work, except for
a 
limitation or reduction in the  number of cases processed
each year. Indeed, the declaration of a target  to limit this
number could have a negative effect on the declarations
of cases. Th e number of  these cases and  their reasons are
monitored on a quarterly basis.
HR risk relating to any failure of the Group’s employment,
health, safety, diversity  or inclusion practices  (Risk)
While regularly monitoring the risks identified,
La  Banque  Postale  has chosen to focus its management
efforts in 2024  on two  topics:  health and harassment.
The identified target under the heading of health, is the
compliance rate for medical visits. While medical visits
are an obligation for all employees, the compliance rate
for medical visits ensures compliance with legal obligations
in terms  of health  and safety at  work, thus  preventing the
risk of sanctions and litigation. It also contributes to the
protection of employees’ health while promoting inclusion
and  adjustment of  working  conditions to meet the
specific  needs of each employee. La Banque Postale aims
for compliance for all staff and all types of visits for all
employees of La  Banque  Postale UES. The compliance
rate 
for medical visits is improving. In 2024, an outsourcing
project 
concerning the organisation and monitoring of
medical visits for La Banque Postale UES employees in the
regions was carried out (implementation scheduled for
December 2024). This project  aims to ensure more
rigorous  management of  medical visits in  the regions.
The policy is implemented and made available through
the organisation of medical visits by the health service
(Île‑de-France) or PrestaMed  (regions), sending emails or
postal  notifications and information on medical visits on
the Company’s intranet. A communication was also launched
at the start of  the PrestaMed service  in the regions.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1812Sustainable performance
Social information
La Banque Postale Group has not set a quantitative target
in 
addition to that concerning zero tolerance on harassment.
The choice was made to set an action target rather than a
numerical 
target. This target is estimated to be achieved
in 2024  in view  of the many  actions  implemented on  this
subject.  [S1_MDR_T_01_13]
Deterioration 
in remuneration levels, the number of
jobs  or the type of contract leading to a decrease in the
purchasing  power of employees (Negative impact)
100%  of employees  receive an adequate wage, and the
majority are covered by a collective agreement setting
salary  scales which are more  favourable than  the statutory
minimum wage. In addition, as part of its social dialogue,
La Banque Postale opens negotiations on wage measures
each year.
Regarding remuneration inequalities (women/men, executive
salaries),  no target  has been  set to date.  However, all the
measures taken aim to ensure that remuneration gaps
between  men and women are based on target
components (level of responsibility, skills, length of service,
performance,  etc.).
Favourable  working conditions for La  Banque  Postale
Group  employees (working  hours,  social dialogue,
fair  remuneration system, social  protection, collective
agreements,  etc.) (Positive impact)
All La  Banque   Postale employees have a voice through
the implementation of  these regulatory  provisions for
social  dialogue. To date, no quantified target has been set
for the quality of social dialogue. Indeed,  the quality of
social dialogue  is difficult  to quantify . It is measured in the
various  surveys  and  through ongoing relationships  with
employee representatives. In addition, collective agreement
monitoring commissions are organis ed once a year
for  each agreement. They monitor and manage the
implementation and expected  effectiveness  of the  actions
undertaken . The meetings of the SEC, the HSWCC and
the DSN  allow  employees'  voices to be heard.
Regarding the implementation of employee representation
mechanisms , professional elections  took place in
November  2023. As  the term of office of employee
representatives  is set for a period of  four  years,  the  next
elections will take  place in 2027.
Regarding the adoption of a flexible work pattern contributing
to a better work-life balance and well-being of employees,
a new  home-working  agreement was signed  on
14 November  2024,  in accordance with the  target  set.
Satisfaction with work-life balance can be monitored through
various survey-based  indicators.  Work-life balance  and
well-being  at work are monitored through the survey’s
QWL  indicator, as well as occasional internal surveys, such
as the one on hybrid  work  in 2024.
In order to guarantee a  safe environment for employees
and  to offer social benefits  for employees, including social
protection, all employees are covered, within the framework
of public schemes or services offered by the Company, by
social protection against loss of income due to illness,
unemployment, work-related accidents, parental leave
and  retirement.As part of the annual monitoring of the social protection
plan, 
a social fund has been  set up  to compensate for
benefits with no  or little coverage  under the plan.  It should
be noted that all exemptions from enrolment in the
healthcare  plan must  be duly justified by the employee's
enrolment in another plan.
Development of the skills of the Company’s employees
promoting innovation and the creation of new  products
and services  (Opportunity)
No target has been set for this  opportunity, as actions and
targets have already been put in place for employee training
and skills. The targets corresponding to these topics are
described 
in the paragraph above concerning  the positive
impacts on skills development and professional development
of employees. [S1_MDR_T_14_19]
2.

start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has 14,512 employees, the majority of whom are women (55%), permanent contracts (94%) and full-time employees (94%).
summary:
- Scope: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) covering workforce characteristics, social dialogue, and diversity.
- Workforce profile (31 Dec 2024): 14,512 employees; 55% women; 94% on permanent contracts; 94% full-time. Work-study students at LBP SA up 37% in 2024 due to employer brand efforts.
- Organizational changes: Headcount growth mainly from integrating La Mutuelle Générale into CNP Assurances (forming CNP Assurances Protection Sociale). Wind-down of Ma French Bank had minimal impact thanks to redeployment offers.
- Geography: Operations largely in France; exceptions are La Financière de l’Échiquier (6% of its staff outside France) and CNP Assurances (27% of its staff outside France). Brazil accounts for over 10% of Group headcount. Main country totals: France 12,204 (6,781 women; 5,423 men); Brazil 1,530 (787 women; 743 men).
- Contracts and working time: Breakdown includes permanent, fixed-term, and work-study contracts; no contracts with non-guaranteed hours. Work-study students counted as full-time for reporting.
- Turnover: 9.4% staff rotation (considered moderate). 1,173 permanent employees left; includes movements to La Poste Group and Caisse des Dépôts (72 from LBP SA).
- Data and methodology: Workforce reported as active natural persons at year-end; breakdowns by gender, contract, working time, age, and socio-professional category. Departures counted for permanent contracts (voluntary, dismissal, retirement, death). Data collected by subsidiaries and consolidated with consistency checks. Note on differing scopes: CNP Assurances Protection Sociale included in the sustainability report but not yet in the financial statements.
- Regional working time split: France 11,375 full-time/829 part-time; Europe 641/29; Rest of world 1,621/17.
- Social dialogue: Near-universal coverage by collective agreements in France; some entities also have company-level agreements. For CNP employees outside France, 92% covered by collective agreements. All France-based employees have workplace representation. European Works Council applicability began after the 2023 merger with CNP; HR is adapting representative bodies accordingly. Reported coverage indicators show very high collective bargaining and representation levels in France and strong coverage in Latin America.
- Diversity and leadership: Commitment to balanced gender representation among senior executives; senior management split is 54.5% men (24) and 45.5% women (20). Definition of “general management” provided (top strategic roles).
- Age diversity: Balanced demographic structure with a strong 30–50 cohort, ongoing hiring of under-30 talent, and retention of over-50 expertise.

title: Social dialogue
heading: 2.3.1.7.2 Social dialogue
start_phrase: All La Banque Postale Group employees based in France are covered by a collective agreement.
summary:
- Scope: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document covering social dialogue, diversity, and workforce demographics.
- Social dialogue and collective bargaining:
  - All La Banque Postale Group employees in France are covered by collective agreements; subsidiaries apply sectoral mandatory or voluntary agreements, with some company-level accords.
  - 92% of CNP Assurances employees outside France are covered by collective agreements.
  - All employees in France are represented by employee representatives.
  - Following the 11 April 2023 merger with CNP Assurances, European Works Council provisions now apply; HR is adapting representative bodies to integrate transnational social dialogue.
  - Reported coverage rates: 98.77% of employees covered by collective agreements overall; in France, collective agreement coverage is 100% and workplace representation 99.97%; Latin America shows high coverage (98.89%).
- Diversity in general management:
  - Strong emphasis on ensuring women’s representation in senior executive appointments with equal skills.
  - Definition of “general management” includes roles shaping Group strategy, first/second in command to Executive Committee members, MDs of major subsidiaries, and positions of highest strategic complexity/impact.
  - Senior executives by gender: 54.5% men (24) and 45.5% women (20).
- Workforce age structure:
  - Balanced demographics with a strong 30–50 cohort central to operations and strategy.
  - Notable presence of under-30 employees reflecting talent attraction efforts.
  - Significant over-50 population demonstrating retention of experience and expertise.

3.1.7.2 Social  dialogue
All La Banque Postale Group employees based in France

summary:

text:
3.1.7.5 Disability situations
La Banque Postale Group pays  particular attention to the
integration of employees with disabilities, while promoting
the ability of existing employees to declare a disability should
they need to do so. However, the percentage of employees
with  disabilities  remains  lower  than the  statutory  rate.
In addition to recruitment, La  Banque  Postale Group
ensures  good working conditions for its employees with
disabilities  and takes specific measures to support them
according  to their individual needs. Such measures may
include  adapting the workstation,  adapting working time
or funding  commuting (taxis).Calculation methodology and background information
For 
employees in France, the data are aggregated from
the payroll file on which  the  recognition of  the status of
disabled worker (RQTH) is declared. RQTH is a French
administrative statute. The RQTH gives access to employment
support schemes and strengthens workers’ rights.
Employees not working in France are subject to the legal
definition 
of the notion of people with disabilities in their
respective countries.  [S1_12_03]
2.

- Disability inclusion:

- Training and careers:

  - Strong internal communication on appraisals; continuous training emphasized; work‑study academic training excluded from figures.

3.1.7.6 Training  and careers
Annual  employee  appraisals play an essential role in
career development, offering an opportunity to recognise
performance, 
identify skills to be improved and map out
career  development prospects. They are a strategic driver
of 
talent and enable employees to align their personal
targets with those of  the organisation.
In France, professional appraisals are a legal obligation,
which is not the case in all Group countries. This regulatory
difference may explain the variations observed in appraisal
completion  rates  internationally.
The Group also provides strong communication on the
importance 
of the appraisal to supporting the development
of skills and careers.
In addition, the Group supports its employees beyond the
annual 
appraisal. Training, in particular, is an essential driver
of employee career development, enabling employees to
acquire new skills, adapt to changes in the business  lines
and strengthen their expertise.  By investing  in continuous
training,  the  Group stimulates motivation, promotes
commitment and supports the  professional development
of its talented individuals.  The  training  figures  below
exclude academic training for work-study students.

start_phrase: Almost all of La Banque Postale Group’s workforce is covered by a health and safety policy.
summary:
- Focus area: Sustainable performance – Social information from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, covering health and safety, work-life balance, and remuneration equality.
- Health and safety:
  - 99.66% of employees covered by a health and safety policy.
  - Indicators monitored monthly; accident rates remain below the French average.
  - 0 deaths due to occupational accidents or illnesses; 54 workplace accidents with lost time.
  - 2.32 lost-time accidents per million hours worked; 0 recordable cases of ill health.
  - 1,760 days lost due to workplace accidents and related causes.
  - High participation in performance and career reviews; average training around 22 hours per employee, with similar levels across genders.
- Work-life balance and family leave:
  - 100% of employees entitled to a wide range of family leaves (maternity/adoption, paternity, parental, breastfeeding, co-parent, birth/adoption, disability support, etc.).
  - 2024 usage: 5.6% of total workforce took family leave (3.8% men; 6.7% women).
  - Among eligible employees: 11.91% took leave (10.73% men; 12.88% women), indicating persistent gender imbalance in caregiving responsibilities.
- Remuneration gap and pay equity:
  - Overall gender remuneration gap: 16.7%, mainly driven by job/grade structure (more women at lower grades, reverse at higher levels).
  - Actions under the 2024 “Diversity and professional equality” agreement: targeted recruitment of under-represented gender, partnerships to de-segment “gendered” roles, career development for women (e.g., Girlz in the Bank), and anti-sexism initiatives.
  - €600,000 annual budget dedicated to reducing unjustified pay gaps.
  - Pay ratio: highest to median remuneration is 10.4.
- Methodology highlights:
  - Gender pay gap based on gross hourly remuneration (fixed, bonuses, annual and long-term variable; excludes profit-sharing/matching).
  - Pay ratio includes profit-sharing and matching; covers employees with at least three months’ service.
  - Work-study contracts excluded due to statutory pay grid; indicators aggregated across Group entities proportionate to workforce; small number of non-France employees excluded where data unavailable.

title: Work-life balance
heading: 2.3.1.7.8 Work-life balance
start_phrase: Group employees are entitled to family leave:
summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR/Social information) covering work-life balance and gender remuneration topics, with methodology notes.
- Work-life balance and family leave:
  - 100% of employees are entitled to family leave based on intrinsic eligibility, regardless of whether a triggering event occurs.
  - Types of leave offered include: maternity/adoption, paternity, parental, breastfeeding leave, conventional maternity top-ups (100% and 50%), co-parent leave (LBP SA), birth/adoption leave, and ASA leave supporting people with disabilities (LBP SA).
  - In 2024, 5.6% of the total workforce took family-related leave: 3.8% of men and 6.7% of women.
  - Among employees eligible for such leave, uptake was higher, with women using it more than men, highlighting a persistent imbalance in parental and family responsibility sharing.
- Gender remuneration gap:
  - Overall 2024 gender pay gap: 16.7%, largely explained by job structure (more women in lower grades, more men in higher grades).
  - Actions under the 2024 “Diversity and professional equality” agreement: targeted recruitment to improve gender mix in business lines, partnerships with schools/charities to attract under-represented genders to “gendered” professions, career support for women (e.g., Girlz in the Bank), and prevention of everyday sexism.
  - €600,000 annual budget dedicated to reducing unjustified pay gaps.
  - Highest-to-median remuneration ratio: 10.4, presented as reflecting moderation and alignment with inclusion and social responsibility values.
- Methodology and perimeter:
  - Gender pay gap compares gross hourly remuneration (annualized fixed pay, bonuses, benefits, annual and long-term variable), excluding profit-sharing and matching contributions.
  - Highest-to-median ratio uses total annual remuneration including profit-sharing and matching.
  - Population: employees on permanent or temporary contracts with at least three months’ service in the year; work-study students excluded due to statutory pay grids.
  - Indicators aggregate CNP Assurances with the rest of La Banque Postale Group weighted by workforce; 10 La Financière de l’Échiquier employees outside France excluded.
text:
3.1.7.8
Work-life balance Group employees are entitled to  family leave:
•Conventional maternity (100%);
•Maternity/Adoption;
•Paternity;
•Parental leave;
•Breastfeeding  leave;
•Conventional maternity (50%);
•Co-parent leave (for La Banque  Postale  SA);
•Birth/adoption leave;
•ASA leave  helping people with disabilities  
(for La Banque Postale  SA).
The rate of "eligible" employees  is calculated taking into
account 
the intrinsic entitlement and not the  existence or
absence of the triggering event. Therefore, all employees
are entitled to family leave  if they  become eligible. [S1_15_04]
La Banque Postale Group strives to support its employees
in the balance between professional and personal life, by
offering  a framework  conducive to the use of leave for
family reasons. In  2024, 5.6% of the Group’s total workforce
took leave for family reasons, with a significant breakdown
by gender:  3.8% for  men  and  6.7%  for women.
For eligible employees  only, this  rate  is 11.91%, of which
10.73%  are men and 12.88% are women. These figures
reveal  an over-representation of women in the use of such
leave, reflecting a persistent imbalance in the distribution
of parental  and  family responsibilities.

title: Remuneration gap
heading: 2.3.1.7.9 Remuneration gap
start_phrase: In 2024, the overall remuneration gap between women and men was 16.7%.
summary:
- Scope and context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR/Social information), covering work-life balance, gender remuneration, and human rights performance and metrics.

- Work-life balance and family leave
  - Broad family leave entitlements (100% of employees eligible): conventional maternity (100% and 50%), maternity/adoption, paternity, parental, breastfeeding leave, co‑parent leave (LBP SA), birth/adoption leave, and ASA leave to support people with disabilities (LBP SA).
  - 2024 usage: 5.6% of total workforce took family leave (3.8% men; 6.7% women).
  - Among eligible employees: 11.91% took leave (10.73% men; 12.88% women), indicating higher uptake by women and a persistent imbalance in caregiving responsibilities.
  - Eligibility rate is based on intrinsic entitlement, not occurrence of a triggering event.

- Gender remuneration gap and pay ratio
  - 2024 overall gender remuneration gap: 16.7%, primarily due to job structure (women overrepresented in lower grades; reverse at higher levels).
  - Actions under the 2024 “Diversity and professional equality” agreement: increase gender diversity in roles (targeted recruitment with equal skills), partnerships with schools/NGOs to attract underrepresented genders to “gendered” jobs, women’s career development initiatives (e.g., Girlz in the Bank), and prevention of everyday sexism.
  - Dedicated annual budget of €600,000 to reduce unjustified pay gaps.
  - Pay ratio: highest total remuneration to median is 10.4, reflecting moderation aligned with inclusion and social responsibility values.
  - Methodology highlights: gender gap based on gross hourly pay (fixed pay, bonuses, benefits, annual and long‑term variable pay; excludes profit-sharing/matching). Pay ratio includes profit-sharing and matching. Includes employees (permanent/temporary) with ≥3 months’ service; excludes work‑study contracts; aggregates CNP Assurances with the rest of the Group proportionally; excludes 10 La Financière de l’Échiquier employees outside France.

- Human rights, discrimination, and complaints
  - Commitments aligned with La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy: prevent violations and complicity; prohibit violence, inhuman/degrading treatment, forced/child labor and trafficking; ban discrimination (gender, age, health/disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, nationality, social background, community, political/union/religious beliefs); uphold freedom of association and collective bargaining; ensure adequate remuneration; protect privacy; ensure GDPR compliance; comply with labor laws in operating countries.
  - 2024 outcomes: no proven severe human rights incidents; no fines, penalties, or compensation related to human rights incidents.
  - Discrimination/harassment and complaints metrics: 5 incidents recorded; 76 complaints received via communication channels; 0 complaints to national contact points; €0 in fines/penalties/compensation.
  - Severe human rights issues and employee-related incidents (including UNGP/OECD non-compliance): 0; associated fines/penalties/compensation: 0.
text:
3.1.7.9 Remuneration gap
In 2024, the overall remuneration gap between women
and men was 16.7%. The remuneration gap between
women and men is mainly related to the job structure:
women  are more represented than men at lower grade
levels,  while  this trend is  reversed  at higher levels.
Motivated by the “Diversity and professional equality”
agreement  of 2024, La Banque  Postale has implemented
substantial actions to remedy this, such as ensuring gender
diversity in  the  business lines  (under-represented gender
recruitment  with  equal skills, developing  partnerships
with schools and  charities to develop the attractiveness of
so-called "gendered" professions, and boosting the careers
of women through  community events (Girlz in the Bank,
etc.) as well  as preventing  everyday  sexism.
In addition to these actions, La  Banque   Postale allocates
an overall budget of €600,000  per year to reducing
unjustified  remuneration  gaps.
The ratio between the highest salary and  the median
salary is 10.4, reflecting a moderation of the remuneration gap
within  the  Group,  in line  with the values  of inclusion  and
social responsibility that drive us.Calculation methodology and background information
The gender remuneration  gap compares the  gross hourly
remuneration paid to women during the financial year to
that 
paid to  men. Th is hourly remuneration includes, on
an annual basis, fixed remuneration, bonuses and benefits
paid, annual and long-term variable remuneration paid,
excluding profit-sharing and matching contributions.
The ratio between the highest remuneration and the median
remuneration compares the total annual remuneration
(remuneration components mentioned above, also including
profit-sharing bonuses paid as well as  any matching
contributions) of the person receiving the highest remuneration
to the total annual median remuneration of all other
employees. 
The employees taken into account are those
with permanent or temporary employment  contracts,
working with La  Banque  Postale Group for at least three
months of the financial year.
Work-study students were excluded from these calculations
given that the work-study (“alternant”)  status is  specific to
France, and that work-study contracts are governed by a
statutory  remuneration grid and are not subject to a
discretionary wage. As a result, including work-study students
would mean that  the analysis  could not be refined.
These indicators are calculated by aggregating the indicators
of CNP Assurances and those of the rest of La Banque Postale
Group, in proportion to th e workforce of each scope.
The number of La Financière de l’Échiquier employees outside
France 
(10) could not be included in the calculations for
these  indicators.  [S1_16_03]

title: Severe human rights incidents
heading: 2.3.1.7.10 Severe human rights incidents
start_phrase: As part of La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy, La Banque Postale Group is committed to:
summary:
- Human rights commitments: prevention of violations; prohibition of violence, forced or compulsory labour, child labour and trafficking; ban on all discrimination (e.g., gender, age, health/disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, nationality, social background, community, political/trade union/religious beliefs); defense of freedom of association and collective bargaining; right to adequate remuneration; opposition to invasion of privacy. Strong GDPR and national labor law compliance.
- 2024 outcomes and metrics:
  - Proven severe human rights incidents: 0
  - Non-compliance with UNGP/OECD Guidelines: 0
  - Incidents of discrimination and harassment: 5
  - Complaints received via communication channels: 76
  - Complaints to national contact points: 0
  - Fines/penalties/compensation for discrimination/harassment: €0
  - Fines/penalties/compensation for severe human rights issues: €0
  - No additional background information beyond reported figures.
- Workers in the value chain (La Poste employees and civil servants working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale):
  - Scope: Significant share of the value chain; roles in branches, remote customer relations, IT, and head-office support; report to La Poste or La Banque Postale; work on La Banque Postale or La Poste sites; not part of La Banque Postale’s direct workforce.
  - Risk profile: Activities in France in banking services; no specific risks of forced or child labour; no particularly vulnerable sub-groups identified; no subgroup more exposed to harm.
  - Material IRO: Potential negative impact from poor working conditions or forced/child labour in the value chain identified as material but not widespread/systemic; no specific positive impact identified for these workers.
  - Dependency: Functional dependency on La Poste due to scale and services, not monitored as a risk since La Poste is the parent company.
- Policies and governance:
  - Covered by La Poste’s Human Rights policy; HR policies provided by La Poste and aligned with La Banque Postale’s culture.
  - Two agreements between La Banque Postale and La Poste:
    - Health and safety for seconded workers hosted on La Banque Postale sites.
    - Workforce, recruitment, and regulatory/mandatory training.
    - Regular monitoring; no specific action plan implemented to date.
  - Human rights protections equivalent to La Banque Postale employees; La Banque Postale’s code of conduct applies to all workers in the value chain.

title: Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
heading: 2.3.2.1.1 Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
start_phrase: Among the workers in the value chain, the workforce working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale, with a re-invoicing system by La Banque Postale for the use of La Poste’s employees, is affected by the (positive or negative) impacts identified (see list of IROs in Section 2.1.3.2 “Description of material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs)”).
summary:
- Focus on ensuring favorable working conditions for workers in La Banque Postale’s value chain, specifically La Poste employees working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale.
- Scope covers a significant workforce of La Poste Group employees and civil servants assigned to La Banque Postale activities (banking advice, post offices, remote customer relations, IT, and head-office support), included in ESRS 2 reporting.
- These workers operate on La Banque Postale or La Poste sites, may report to managers from either entity, and are not counted in La Banque Postale’s own workforce; costs are re-invoiced.
- No vulnerable categories or sub-groups with higher exposure to harm have been identified.
- No specific risk of forced or child labor, as activities are banking services conducted in France; workers are protected by La Poste’s Human Rights policy.
- A material negative impact is recognized: potential poor working conditions (e.g., unequal pay, safety issues) in the value chain; this impact is material but not widespread or systemic.
- No specific positive impacts identified; policies on working conditions and anti-discrimination are aligned with La Poste as the parent company, and La Banque Postale does not significantly influence La Poste’s policies.
- Functional dependency on La Poste due to workforce size and mission is acknowledged but not treated as a risk because La Poste is the parent company.
- Applicable policies: La Poste’s HR and Human Rights policies cover these workers; two inter-company agreements exist—one on health and safety for seconded workers hosted on La Banque Postale sites, and another on workforce, recruitment, and mandatory training; these are regularly monitored, with no specific action plan currently in place.
- Human rights protections mirror those for La Banque Postale employees, and La Banque Postale’s Code of Conduct applies to all value-chain workers.
text:
3.2.1.1 Material IROs and links with strategy 
and business  model
Scope
Among  the workers in the value chain, the workforce
working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale, with  a re-
invoicing system by La   Banque  Postale for the use of
La Poste ’s employees, is affected by the (positive or negative)
impacts identified (see list of IROs in  Section 2.1.3.2
“Description of material impacts,  risks and opportunities
(IROs)”).  Indeed, these workers represent a significant part
of La Banque  Postale  Group’s value chain.  As a  result, they
are included in the information published under ESRS 2.
[S2_SBM_3_01]
This  workforce consists of La Poste Group employees and
civil 
servants. They are part of La Poste Group and are attached
to the La  Poste – France Télécom joint agreement for
permanent, fixed-term or work-study contracts, and to the
civil service status for civil servants.
They may report to a La Poste or La Banque Postale manager.
These  workers  carry  out their  role  for and on behalf of
La  Banque  Postale, for the Banking Advice Line, in post
offices,  for remote customer relations centres,  but also
within the IT teams and other head office support
functions.  [S2_SBM_3_02]
These  workers  therefore work  on the sites of the Company
or its parent company, but are not part of the La Banque Postale
Group 
workforce. No specific category of worker particularly
vulnerable to a material negative impact on their working
conditions (due to their intrinsic characteristics or a
particular  context)  has been  identified. [S2_SBM_3_03]
Furthermore,  no specific sub-group has been identified as
being  more  likely  than others to  be exposed to risks of
harm.  [S2_SBM_3_08]
Risks  of forced  labour  and child labour
All activities are carried out in France for these employees,
and 
concern banking services. Therefore, there is no specific
risk regarding  forced labou r or child labour.
These  employees are also covered by La Poste Group’s
Human  Rights  policy,  as detailed in  Section 2.3.1.2.6
“Human  rights  policies  and  measures”.  [S2_SBM_3_04]
Material  impacts,  risks and opportunities
The material negative impact identified concerning workers
in the  value  chain is  as follows:  “Negative  impact in the
event of poor working  conditions (unequal remuneration,
safety, etc.), forced labour and/or child labour within companies
in the value chain of own operations and service activities”.This impact is considered material but is not widespread
or systemic in the context of La  Banque  Postale Group.
[S2_SBM_3_05]
There 
is no positive impact specifically identified  for these
workers. As La Poste is the parent company of La Banque Postale
Group, 
the policies and actions concerning, in particular,
the improvement of working conditions and combating
discrimination 
are aligned, and La  Banque  Postale does
not have a significant impact on the policies and actions
implemented  by La Poste. [S2_SBM_3_06]
In view  of the significant size of the workforce dependent
on La Poste Group in  La  Banque  Postale’s value chain,
and   the banking service missions that they provide,
La  Banque  Postale  has a functional dependency  on
La Poste. However, this dependency is not considered and
monitored as a risk given  that  La  Poste is the parent
company of  La Banque Postale. [S2_SBM_3_07]

title: Applicable policies
heading: 2.3.2.1.2 Applicable policies
start_phrase: La Poste workers working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale are, like La Banque Postale workers, covered by La Poste’s Human Rights policy.
summary:
- Scope and workforce: Focus on La Poste Group employees (including civil servants) who work for and on behalf of La Banque Postale (LBP) in post offices, remote customer relations, banking advice, IT, and HQ support. They may report to La Poste or LBP managers, work on La Poste/LBP sites, are not counted in LBP’s own workforce, and are covered under ESRS S2 disclosures.
- Risk profile: Activities occur in France and involve banking services; no specific risks of forced or child labor identified. No vulnerable sub-groups or sub-groups with higher exposure to harm identified. The potential material negative impact relates to poor working conditions (e.g., unequal pay, safety). Impact is material but not widespread/systemic. No specific positive impacts identified. LBP has a functional dependency on La Poste, but it is not treated as a risk since La Poste is the parent company.
- Policies and governance: Workers are covered by La Poste’s Human Rights and HR policies, aligned with LBP’s culture. Two intercompany agreements govern (1) health and safety for seconded workers on LBP sites and (2) workforce, recruitment, and mandatory training. LBP’s code of conduct applies to value-chain workers. No dedicated action plan tied to these agreements to date.
- Dialogue mechanisms: Feedback gathered through La Poste’s engagement survey and annual appraisals/interviews, with social dialogue managed by La Poste’s bodies. LBP’s HR Director (Executive Committee member) leads the interface with La Poste. Effectiveness of dialogue assessed via engagement survey outcomes, which inform operational management.
- Reporting and remediation: Concerns can be raised via the engagement survey, annual appraisals, direct manager dialogue (when managed by LBP), and the Group whistleblowing system (independent, accessible platform, managed by Compliance, with whistleblower protections). LBP HR accesses survey and appraisal results to monitor issues and act as needed. No significant negative impacts identified; remediation would follow due diligence if they occur.
- Actions and 2024 initiatives: Regular HR coordination between LBP and La Poste; joint work on variable remuneration and workforce matters; a co-led monitoring committee addressing workplace “niggling” issues; evolution of employee representative bodies with social dialogue overseen by LBP HR within La Poste’s rules. Effectiveness tracked through engagement survey results.
text:

title: Dialogue mechanisms
heading: 2.3.2.1.3 Dialogue mechanisms
start_phrase: The point of view of La Poste employees working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale is important for La Banque Postale in order to ensure the smooth running of these activities.
summary:
- Focus: Social information on workers employed by La Poste but working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale (LBP), within LBP’s CSR framework.
- Dialogue mechanisms: use of La Poste Group’s engagement survey and annual appraisals/professional interviews to capture expectations and concerns; information also flows via La Poste’s social bodies; both entities respect legal obligations on social dialogue.
- Governance/interface: the Human Resources Director of LBP Group (Executive Committee member) is the most senior point of contact with La Poste on these workforce issues.
- Effectiveness monitoring: dialogue effectiveness is assessed indirectly through results of the annual engagement survey, which inform operational management actions.
- Reporting channels: workers can raise concerns through the engagement survey, mandatory annual appraisals, and direct dialogue with LBP managers when applicable.
- Data access and follow-up: LBP’s HR Department accesses survey and appraisal results to monitor significant issues and implement measures as needed.
- Whistleblowing: a Group-wide, independent, confidential platform managed by the Compliance Department is available to all employees; communicated via the code of conduct and protects whistleblowers.
- Impacts and remediation: no significant negative impacts identified to date; therefore no specific remediation effectiveness procedure yet, but due diligence would apply if needed.
- Material risk identified: potential negative impacts linked to poor working conditions (including unequal pay and safety), and forced or child labor in the value chain related to own operations and services.
- Action plans (2024): joint HR work with La Poste on variable remuneration and workforce issues; a co-led monitoring committee addressing workplace “niggling issues”; adjustments to employee representative bodies with social dialogue managed by LBP HR under La Poste’s rules.
- Evaluation of actions: effectiveness measured via engagement survey outcomes.

  - 75.8% covered by collective agreements (La Poste–France Télécom agreement for permanent, fixed-term, and work-study contracts).

- Human rights, discrimination, and grievances:
  - No severe human rights issues reported for these workers; no related fines or penalties.

  - ESG risk ratings applied to suppliers to identify specific working conditions and tailor prevention/due diligence.
  - Risks vary by geography, segment, and contract (notably for CNP Assurances); mitigations include contractual clauses, targeted audits, and a whistleblowing system.
  - Impacts identified: positive (improving working conditions, protection, inclusion) and potential negative (poor conditions, unequal pay, safety issues, forced/child labor).
  - Responsible purchasing strategy supports improved conditions and contributes to LBP’s mission-led commitments and SDGs monitoring; no severe human rights incidents or related fines reported for La Poste workers.

title: Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
heading: 2.3.2.2.1 Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
start_phrase: Workers in the upstream value chain are key stakeholders for La Banque Postale.
summary:
- Scope and stakeholders: Focus on workers in the upstream value chain—non-payroll workers on La Banque Postale sites and supplier employees; downstream workers covered elsewhere.
- Risk exposure: Higher exposure in building, maintenance, and logistics; vulnerable groups (older workers, people with disabilities, ethnic minorities) face greater risks of discrimination and inequality.
- Supplier ESG assessment: ESG risk rating differentiates by activity (e.g., consulting vs. maintenance) and considers geography, business segment, and contract type to tailor prevention and due diligence.
- Mitigation tools: Contractual clauses, targeted audits, and a whistleblowing system to address social and safety risks, especially in sensitive regions.
- Impacts identified:
  - Positive: Responsible purchasing strategy improves working conditions and inclusion; aligns with mission-led status (since 2022) and supports selected SDGs with published indicators.
  - Negative (potential): Poor working conditions (unequal pay, safety lapses), discrimination, forced labour, and child labour within suppliers and subcontractors.
- Performance indicators: Reported zero severe human rights incidents and zero related fines, penalties, or compensation for La Poste workers operating for/on behalf of La Banque Postale.
- Operating context: Significant outsourcing primarily to French/European suppliers, limiting potential negative impacts due to EU labour standards and UN Global Compact alignment.
- Governance and certifications: Adoption of La Poste Group Purchasing Policy; “Responsible Purchasing Approach”; RFAR charter signed in 2022; RFAR certification obtained in 2023 for La Banque Postale SA and CNP Assurances; rollout to banking subsidiaries from 2025; promotion of responsible purchasing culture across the group.
- Material risks: Financial losses from inadequate partner assessment amid social transition and regulatory change; operational/financial impact from termination or slowdown of major suppliers; risks integrated into group risk mapping with emphasis on limiting supplier dependency.
- Forced and child labour: Overall low risk in main operating regions (France/Europe); continued vigilance, notably for CNP Assurances’ activities including Latin America.
- Policies and supplier obligations: Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter requires suppliers (and their subcontractors) to:
  - Ensure dignified management and working conditions, prevent psychosocial risks, and safeguard health and safety.
  - Comply with laws on working hours, remuneration, training, and trade union rights.
  - Adhere to the UN Global Compact, ILO core conventions, and ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work.
  - Cascade these requirements across their own supply chains, including in countries not signatory to ILO conventions.
text:
3.2.2.1
Material IROs and links with strategy 
and business  model
Scope
Workers in the  upstream value chain are key stakeholders
for La  Banque  Postale.  This  entire population is likely  to be
impacted by the Group. Two main types of workers are
concerned:
•Employees  working on one of La Banque Postale’s sites
(head office, subsidiaries, post offices) but who are not
part of the workforce;
•Workers working  for La Banque  Postale ’s suppliers.
The workers integrated into the Company's downstream
value  chain (workers of the financed companies) are dealt
with in Section 2.3.2.3 “Workers in the downstream value chain”.
Service 
providers in the building, maintenance and logistics
sectors  are more exposed  to the potential  impacts of any
failure  of safety  rules. In addition, workers belonging to
vulnerable groups (older employees, people with disabilities,
ethnic minorities) are more exposed to the potential impacts
of discrimination  and inequality.  [S2_SBM_3_01] [S2_SBM_3_02]
[S2_SBM_3_03]
In order to identify these specific groups, an ESG risk  rating
is carried out to assess third-party suppliers. It incorporates
the specific working conditions applicable to the different
types  of workers within the value chain, for example  by
differentiating between consulting services where risks
are 
mainly related to mental load, and maintenance activities,
which are more exposed to physical risks or precarious
working  conditions.  This  differentiation makes  it possible
to identify particularly exposed groups more precisely and
to adapt  prevention and  due  diligence  measures
accordingly.  [S2_SBM_3_08]La  Banque  Postale recognises that social factors in the
value 
chain do not affect all workers in the same way.
These 
risks may vary depending on the geographical
location 
of the suppliers (for CNP Assurances in particular),
the 
business segment and the contract type. For example,
workers 
operating in sensitive regions may face social or
safety 
risks at work. To mitigate these risks, La Banque Postale
adopts specific clauses in contracts, targeted audits and
implements a whistleblowing  system.  [S2_SBM_3_09]
Identified impacts, risks and opportunities
The identified material impacts on workers in the upstream
value chain  are as follows:
•Actual positive impacts by  contributing to improving
working conditions, and the protection and inclusion of
workers 
in the value chain of own operations and
service activities;
•Potential negative impacts in the  event of poor working
conditions 
(unequal  remuneration, safety,  etc.),  forced
labour or child labour within companies in the value chain
of own operations (suppliers, etc.) and service activities.
La  Banque  Postale ’s responsible purchasing strategy
generates positive impacts on workers in the value chain,
as it helps to improve the working conditions of employees
in 
its value chain. In 2022, La  Banque  Postale became  a
mission-led company, making its community foundations
the key  driver of  its performance in support of the  just
transition.  In this context, its business  model directly
interacts with six Sustainable Development  Goals (SDGs),
and  it publishes monitoring indicators in relation to these
Goals. 
The purchasing strategy, which takes into account
the identified impacts on workers in the value chain,
contributes to  the achievement of these SDGs.

In addition, as a subsidiary of La Poste, La Banque Postale’s
business 
model also contributes to developing the responsible
purchasing culture.  Through regular interactions between
La Banque Postale’s purchasing function and its subsidiaries,
it 
engages in a group dynamic to promote La Poste Group’s
Responsible Purchasing policy, as well  as the “Supplier
Relations and  Responsible Purchasing” certification from
La Banque  Postale.
These positive impacts cover all  workers in the value chain
(for more information, see Section 2.3.2.1.1 “Material IROs
and  links  with  strategy  and  business  model”).
The requirement  to comply with the principles of the  UN
Global Compact and the fundamental conventions of the
International
 Labour Organization (ILO), as well as the
introduction of CSR criteria in the selection of service
providers and suppliers, contribute to the improvement of
working  conditions. They promote a healthy, safe and
inclusive  work  environment. [S2_SBM_3_06]
The potential negative impacts identified on workers in
the value chain are the result of the  business model.
La  Banque  Postale is a tertiary sector company that
outsources 
or subcontracts a significant  portion of its own
operations.  Being positioned in France and operating its
activities mainly in France (excluding CNP  Assurances),
La Banque Postale mainly relies on French and European
suppliers for the outsourcing of its services and subcontracting.
In this context, the activity of  its leading subcontractors is
carried out in compliance with European labour law and
the 
standards of the United Nations Global Compact, thereby
limiting  the potential of the  negative  impacts  identified.
The management and monitoring  of the Responsible
Purchasing  Charter targets guide La  Banque  Postale’s
purchasing  strategy. For example, the environmental and
social  commitments made as part of La Banque Postale’s
mission-led company and strategic plan for 2030 led it to
approve  La Poste  Group’s Purchasing policy and to draft
its 
“Responsible Purchasing Approach”, as well as confirming
its 
commitment to the “Supplier Relations and Responsible
Purchasing (RFAR)” approach. This resulted in the signing
of the RFAR charter in September 2022, while the
La  Banque  Postale SA and CNP   Assurances entities
obtained the RFAR certification  in September 2023.
The RFAR certification process  for banking subsidiaries of
La Banque  Postale SA  will be launched from 2025.
The potential negative impacts identified are related to
the following  events:
•Poor  application of security  measures;
•Unequal  remuneration  (women/men, executive salaries)
due to  inadequate  remuneration policies  among
subcontractors;
•Acts of discrimination;
•Forced  labour  or child labour. [S2_SBM_3_05]
No material opportunities arising from the impacts on
workers  in the value  chain were  identified.
However,  two material  risks  stand  out:
•Risk  of financial  loss due to failures  in assessing
La Banque Postale’s partners (service providers, suppliers
or 
distributors) in an environment shaped by the transition
towards  a more equitable  and  inclusive society (with
more or less rapid regulatory changes in the face of social
injustice, changes in consumer behaviour and markets, etc.);
•Termination  or temporary decrease in the activity of a
major  service  provider,  supplier  or distributor resulting
in financial  losses.These risks are taken into account in La Poste Group’s
Purchasing Charter, one of the  main areas of which is  to
limit dependency on suppliers. This Charter applies to all
subsidiaries 
majority owned by La  Banque  Postale.
These  risks are therefore considered within the scope of
own 
operations for a majority of the  Group’s entities.
In 
addition, the ESG risks associated with products and
services are included in the Group’s overall risk mapping,
which feeds into its strategy.
These risks are gross risks, which can arise in the event of
poorly  managed dependency on suppliers. [S2_SBM_3_07]
Risks  of forced  labou r and child labour
La  Banque  Postale and most of its subsidiaries operate
mainly  in the tertiary sector in France,  a country in which
the risks of  forced labour,  compulsory labour  and child
labour are generally considered low.
CNP  Assurances operates in the tertiary sector in France,
Europe 
and Latin America. Although CNP Assurances’ activities
are 
concentrated in regions in which the risks of forced
labour and child labour are  low, the  Company remains
vigilant on these issues, in accordance with regulations
and international  initiatives in  force.  [S2_SBM_3_04]
