title: Applicable policies
heading: 2.3.2.2.2 Applicable policies
start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group is actively committed to the workers in its upstream value chain, in order to limit the negative impacts and develop the positive impacts that it may have on this group of people.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s responsible purchasing approach and management of social impacts on workers in its upstream value chain within La Poste Group’s CSR framework.
- Positive impacts: Embedding CSR criteria and requiring adherence to the UN Global Compact and ILO conventions improves health, safety, inclusion, and overall working conditions across the value chain.
- Operating model context: A tertiary-sector business largely outsourcing in France/Europe (except CNP Assurances with activities in Europe and Latin America), where forced/child labor risks are generally low; vigilance maintained.
- Governance and alignment: Adoption of La Poste Group’s Responsible Purchasing policy; participation in ObsAR; reference to ISO 20400 responsible purchasing standard.
- Certifications and milestones: Signing of the Supplier Relations and Responsible Purchasing (RFAR) charter in Sept 2022; RFAR certification for La Banque Postale SA and CNP Assurances in Sept 2023; certification rollout to banking subsidiaries from 2025.
- Core policy instruments: La Banque Postale Group’s Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter (approved by the Executive Committee), appended to all supplier contracts and managed by the Purchasing Department.
- Supplier obligations under the Charter: Respect human dignity and worker rights; prevent psychosocial risks; ensure safe work; comply with laws on hours, pay, training, and union rights; uphold UNGC and ILO fundamental conventions; extend these principles throughout their own supply chains, including in non‑ILO signatory countries.
- La Poste Group policy pillars: (1) Enforce/promote human rights in supply chains; (2) Reduce environmental impacts of purchases and encourage positives; (3) Promote social inclusion and regional economic/social development via purchasing; (4) Build responsible, ethical supplier relationships.
- Inclusion through purchasing: Seek suppliers engaged in integrating people far from employment; facilitate access to markets for inclusive structures; encourage positive regional inclusion impacts throughout subcontracting chains.
- Supplier assessment and due diligence: Pre‑contract and in‑contract assessments covering financial risk, anti‑corruption (Sapin II), documentary and ESG due diligence (French duty of vigilance); criteria include financial health, supplier dependency, environmental compliance, and human rights risks.
- Processes and tools: A Purchasing Manual (from 2025) detailing organization and multi‑criteria tender assessment to manage risks of financial loss from inadequate partner assessments; procedures and templates available on intranet.
- Identified potential negative impacts on value‑chain workers: Poor implementation of security measures; unequal remuneration (gender and executive pay) at subcontractors; discrimination; forced or child labor.
- Risks and mitigation: Material risks include financial loss from failures in partner assessment amid evolving social expectations/regulation, and disruption from key supplier/distributor failure; supplier dependency addressed via the Purchasing Charter and included in Group risk mapping; risks considered gross if dependency is poorly managed.
- No material opportunities identified related to impacts on value‑chain workers.
- Engagement mechanisms with suppliers: Establishment of a Supplier Relations Mediator (2023); creation of an SME Officer role (2024) to support SMEs; ongoing “supplier listening” with annual interviews, notably in intellectual services.
text:
3.2.2.2 Applicable policies
La  Banque  Postale Group is actively committed to the
workers in its upstream value chain, in order to  limit the
negative impacts and develop the positive impacts that it
may  have on this group of people. These commitments
include various  policies.
The Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter formalises
the commitments of La  Banque  Postale Group to its
customers,  employees, society, the regions and the planet,
with the aim of  it being  jointly imple mented by its
employees, suppliers  and  subcontractors. This charter
requires La  Banque  Postale Group’s service providers to
comply  with a certain number of principles, and to ensure
that the same applies to their  subcontractors.
The following commitments are defined by  the Charter
and enable La Banque Postale to contribute to establishing
good working conditions and respect for fundamental rights
throughout the value chain. Suppliers therefore undertake to:
•develop 
management and working conditions that respect
human dignity and the rights of workers, and in particular
comply with  the  National Interprofessional Agreement
of 2 July 2008 on stress  at work, in order to prevent
psychosocial risks;
•refrain from any  form  of work  that, due to the  conditions
in which it is carried out, may  be detrimental  to health
or safety;
•comply with legislation on the management of working
hours, remuneration, training and trade union rights;
•respect 
the principles of the Global Compact, the eight
fundamental 
conventions of the ILO (International Labour
Organization) and the ILO  Declaration on Fundamental
Principles  and Rights  at Work, aimed in particular at
combating forced labour, child labour and discrimination;
•implement 
all means necessary to comply with the
principles set  out by the Charter throughout their design,
supply and manufacturing chain of the  products or
services they offer to La   Banque  Postale,  including in
non-signatory countries of ILO conventions in which
they may be required to work.196 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
La Banque Postale Group’s Responsible Purchasing Charter is
appended to and systematically included in the product
and  service  contracts  signed between La Banque  Postale
and  its suppliers, and is accessible via a link in the General
Purchasing Conditions shown on the back of purchase orders.
The Responsible Purchasing  Charter  was  approved
by  La  Banque  Postale  Group’s Executive Committee.
Its implementation and monitoring are the responsibility
of the Purchasing  Department.
For several years, La Poste Group has forged close relationships
with stakeholders on the subject of responsible purchasing.
In particular, it is an active member of the Observatoire
des Achats Responsables (ObsAR). As a subsidiary of
La  Poste Group, La  Banque  Postale’s Responsible and
Ethical Purchasing Charter is a continuation of this approach.
La Poste Group’s Responsible Purchasing policy has been
adopted  as a reference document  by La  Banque  Postale.
It is based  on four pillars:
•Pillar  1: Enforce  and  promote  human rights throughout
supply chains;
•Pillar  2: Reduce  the negative impact of  purchases and
suppliers on the environment and encourage positive
impacts;
•Pillar 
3: Promote social inclusion and contribute, through
purchases, 
to the development of the regional economic
and social  fabric;
•Pillar 4: Consolidate responsible and ethical relationships
with  suppliers.
To promote inclusion through its purchases, La Poste Group
is looking for suppliers committed to the integration of
people 
who are isolated from employment and contributing
to the development of the regions in which they operate,
particularly  in vulnerable regions. The Group is committed
to facilitating access to its markets for the structures
involved,  and encourages its suppliers to have a positive
impact in terms of inclusion in their region, through their
subcontracting  chain.
La Poste Group ’s Responsible Purchasing policy is approved
by the Group’s Executive Committee. Its implementation
and  monitoring are the responsibility of the Group’s
Purchasing  Department. Within La  Banque  Postale , the
Purchasing  Department  is responsible  for implementing
this policy  and  ensuring that it is  operational.
According to the international standard ISO 204001, La Poste
Group  defines responsible  purchasing as  “a purchase with
the most positive environmental, social and economic
impacts  possible  over  the entire life cycle”.
The principles of this policy are reiterated and supplemented
in La  Banque   Postale Group’s body of documents and
contractual agreements with each stakeholder. In addition,
La Poste Group’s Responsible Purchasing policy is available
on its website.
La Poste Group ’s Respo nsible  Purchasing policy  and
La  Banque   Postale Group’s Responsible and Ethical
Purchasing  Charter apply to the entire value chain and to
all of La  Banque  Postale Group’s purchasing activities,
whether  in France or internationally.The supplier assessment procedure is intended to determine
the rules to be followed in order to  assess  the risks
associated with La Banque Postale Group’s suppliers, and
to decide on any action to be taken, whether before
entering 
into a contractual relationship or during the
performance  of the contract.  The Group’s suppliers  must
be assessed to cover the risks that the relationship with
them may bring  in terms of:
•Financial  risks;
•Risks of  corruption (French  Sapin II law);
•Documentary risk (French  Due  diligence  law);
•ESG risks  (French Due diligence law).
Criteria such as the supplier’s financial health, dependency
rate, 
environmental compliance and Human Rights risks
are assessed.
In addition, the Purchasing Manual is a document for use
by the Purchasing  Department which will be rolled out
within the Group’s Purchasing teams from 2025. It presents
the organisation and  describes the macro-processes to
be applied by Purchasing staff for La  Banque  Postale
Group purchases. In particular, it specifies the structure of
the tender assessment grid. This multi-criteria assessment
approach  manages the risk of financial loss related to a
failure 
in the  assessment of suppliers, service providers or
distributors, in a context of transition to a more equitable
and inclusive society.
All of the  documents applicable by La   Banque  Postale
Group’s Purchasing function can be consulted by all
employees of the Purchasing Department on the private
intranet. 
The purchasing procedure, operating methods
and models required by specifiers to apply the purchasing
process are available on the public intranet.  [S2_MDR_P_01_06]
2.

title: Commitments to workers in the upstream value chain
heading: 2.3.2.2.3 Commitments to workers in the upstream value chain
start_phrase: The relationship between La Banque Postale and its suppliers, who are employers of workers in the value chain, is framed by the Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter between La Banque Postale and its suppliers.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s responsible purchasing and human rights framework within the La Poste Group’s CSR strategy, governance, tools, and supplier expectations across the value chain in France and internationally.

- Governance and scope:
  - Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter appended to all contracts and linked via General Purchasing Conditions; approved by the Executive Committee; implemented and monitored by the Purchasing Department.
  - Alignment with La Poste Group’s Responsible Purchasing policy; active membership in ObsAR; policy published online; documents available on intranet.
  - ISO 20400 definition adopted: maximizing positive environmental, social, and economic impacts over the life cycle.

- Responsible purchasing pillars:
  1) Enforce and promote human rights across supply chains.
  2) Reduce negative environmental impacts and foster positive ones.
  3) Promote social inclusion and regional socio-economic development through purchasing.
  4) Build responsible and ethical supplier relationships.

- Inclusion through purchasing:
  - Preference for suppliers integrating people distant from employment and contributing to vulnerable regions; encouragement to drive inclusion through subcontracting chains; facilitated market access for inclusive structures.

- Supplier risk assessment and tools:
  - Formal supplier assessment pre- and in-contract covering financial risks, anti-corruption (Sapin II), documentary due diligence, and ESG risks.
  - Criteria include financial health, dependency, environmental compliance, and human rights risks.
  - Purchasing Manual (from 2025) standardizes organization, macro-processes, and tender multi-criteria assessment to manage loss and transition risks.
  - Procedures and templates accessible on intranet.

- Commitments to workers in the upstream value chain:
  - Supplier Relations Mediator (2023) to handle disputes, including worker well-being issues.
  - SME Officer (2024) to support SMEs whose workers face higher risks (role being finalized).
  - “Supplier listening” system with annual interviews in intellectual services categories.
  - Confidential whistleblowing website for suppliers and their employees to report serious fundamental rights infringements; suppliers must inform employees and cooperate on investigations.
  - CNP Assurances provides additional concern-raising channels (whistleblowing and mediation).

- Human rights framework and initiatives:
  - La Poste Group Human Rights policy covering operations and value chain; regular social agreements with unions.
  - References to ILO core conventions and UN Global Compact principles.
  - Responsible Purchasing policy validated January 2023; directly supports SDGs 3, 5, 8, and 10.
  - Diversity and inclusion commitments: AFMD StOpE initiative (2023) against everyday sexism; L’Autre Cercle LGBT+ Charter (2024).

- Supplier obligations via the Charter:
  - Ensure decent working conditions and prevent psychosocial risks.
  - Prohibit discrimination and promote equal treatment.
  - Comply with anti-corruption laws and standards.
  - Cascade Charter requirements to subcontractors and suppliers.
  - Accept external audits and implement corrective actions (process effective since Q4 2024).
  - Take appropriate measures following human rights incident reports at postal sites.
  - Reinforces buyer conduct: adherence to Code of Ethics, fair treatment, transparency, and independence.
text:
3.2.2.3 Commitments to workers 
in the upstream value  chain
The relationship between La Banque Postale and its suppliers,
who are employers of workers in the value chain, is framed
by the Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter between
La Banque Postale and its suppliers.
Through Pillar 4 of the Responsible Purchasing policy,
La  Banque  Postale is committed to building responsible
and  ethical relationships with its suppliers. In this context,
La Banque Postale has therefore set up:
•a “supplier relations” Mediator in 2023, who can intervene
in 
any disputes, including when they concern situations
affecting the well-being of suppliers’  workers;
•an SME Officer in 2024, whose target  is to support  SMEs
whose workers are particularly exposed to negative
impacts  concerning their working conditions, and
whose  job description is still being developed.
The Purchasing Department is also working to  integrate
these  points relating  to the working conditions of workers
in the value chain, in a more informal manner, as part of
the “supplier listening” system which has been set up.
In 
this respect, questions will be addressed during
the  annual interviews held, with the firms listed by
La Banque Postale in the intellectual services purchasing
categories.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1972Sustainable performance
Social information
La 
Banque  Postale provides a website  to enable the supplier
and  its employees to confidentially report any serious
infringement of fundamental rights. Through the contracts
and General Purchasing Conditions, the supplier undertakes:
•to take note of this procedure and to inform its employees
of the existence of this whistleblowing system to thereby
report  any  serious  infringements of  fundamental  rights
of which  it is personally  aware;
•to work with La Banque Postale in the event that a report
made 
by one of its employees reveals that a serious
violation of fundamental rights may have occurred at
the service provider’s premises.  CNP  Assurances has
also  set up channels enabling workers in the upstream
value chain to raise their concerns, and  in particular to
report  negative  impacts  (through  the  whistleblowing
system and  mediation system  for suppliers). [S2_1_03]
2.

title: Human rights
heading: 2.3.2.2.4 Human rights
start_phrase: La Poste Group has adopted a Human Rights policy that embodies its commitments to the protection, respect and promotion of human rights in all of its activities, in its value chain, both in France and internationally.
summary:
- Scope and context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance/Social information) detailing human rights, responsible purchasing, supplier oversight, and grievance mechanisms across the upstream value chain, including CNP Assurances.

- Human rights and policy framework:
  - La Poste Group Human Rights policy applied across activities and value chains, in France and internationally.
  - Alignment with ILO core conventions, UN Global Compact principles, and UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights.
  - La Banque Postale’s Responsible Purchasing policy (validated Jan 2023) built on four pillars; Pillar 1 commits to enforcing and promoting fundamental rights in supply chains and contributes to SDGs 3, 5, 8, and 10.
  - Diversity and inclusion commitments, including AFMD’s StOpE initiative (2023) and L’Autre Cercle LGBT+ charter (2024).
  - Explicit references to ILO Conventions 29 (forced labor) and 182 (child labor), and UNGC principles 4 and 5.

- Supplier obligations and charters:
  - Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter sets reciprocal commitments on human rights, labor law, environment, and anti-corruption; flow-down to subcontractors; acceptance of external audits (rolled out from Q4 2024); cooperation in case of reported human rights issues.
  - Contractual “due diligence” clauses require risk identification and mitigation of fundamental rights infringements.
  - Group code of conduct (zero tolerance on corruption) annexed to contracts and published online; aligned with ILO standards.
  - CNP Assurances policies mirror UN human rights guidelines; Responsible Supplier Charter deployed Dec 2024 and rolled out/translated in foreign subsidiaries from Jan 2025; suppliers sign upon onboarding from Jan 2025.

- Supplier risk assessment and monitoring:
  - Pre-onboarding and annual assessment for all suppliers (with thresholds noted), covering financial risk, corruption/AML-CFT (Sapin II), documentary due diligence, and CSR risks (including human rights).
  - Use of AFNOR risk mapping (segment exposure rated 1–4), translated into high/medium/low CSR risk levels; supplier CSR ratings integrated in mapping.
  - Deployment of La Poste Group’s e-compliance with EcoVadis ratings and a CSR maturity questionnaire; potential escalation to documentary or on-site audits.
  - “Due diligence” clauses mandate corrective actions where risks are identified.
  - No upstream value chain non-compliance reported to date.

- Dialogue and grievance mechanisms:
  - Ongoing dialogue with suppliers through compliance analyses, mediation, listening systems, and whistleblowing channels; consultations report high satisfaction and no significant issues thus far.
  - Independent Supplier Mediator (shared with La Poste Group), accessible online, participates in the Responsible Purchasing Committee (ARCOM), publishes annual reports; usage monitored monthly with no cases recorded to date.
  - Supplier listening system for intellectual services (PM/PMO/consulting) via questionnaires, annual meetings, and KPIs; since Oct/Nov 2024 includes questions on working conditions and internal whistleblowing; informs action plans where needed.
  - Confirmation of purchasing function’s responsibility for responsible purchasing and supplier compliance; “Supplier Relations and Responsible Purchasing” certification achieved Sep 2023, follow-up audit Jun 2024.

- Reporting and remediation:
  - Whistleblowing platform covers all upstream workers (suppliers and their employees), accessible via La Banque Postale’s website; suppliers must inform their employees and provide access.
  - Workers can also access the Supplier Mediator; channels rely on availability of digital equipment.
  - Processes allow for investigation, corrective actions, and continuous improvement based on findings and audits.
text:
3.2.2.4 Human  rights
Applicable  framework  agreements
La Poste Group has adopted a Human Rights policy that
embodies its commitments to the protection, respect and
promotion  of human rights in all of its activities, in
its  value chain, both in France and internationally.
Through the responsible purchasing charters of its entities,
La Poste Group acts as a responsible and ethical customer,
in a shared  progress approach with its suppliers and
partners.  La  Poste and its French subsidiaries regularly
sign  social agreements that promote human rights with
representative  trade  unions.
As indicated in  Pillar 1 of the Responsible Purchasing
Policy, La Banque  Postale, like its parent company, makes
strong  commitments to diversity and inclusion. As such,
for several years it has been working closely and sharing
information  with  non-governmental  organisations and
charities.  It has signed  several inter-professional charters
on this subject,  including:
•AFMD’s (French Association of Diversity Managers) StOpE
initiative 
in 2023, which commits La Banque  Postale to
act against  everyday  sexism;
•the L'Autre Cercle association's LGBT+ charter in 2024,
which commits La Banque Postale Group to promoting
the diversity of gender identities and sexual orientations.
Policies regarding Human  rights
La Poste Group’s Responsible  Purchasing policy  and
La  Banque  Postale’s Responsible and Ethical Purchasing
Charter refer to the eight fundamental conventions of the
ILO and the ten principles of the United  Nations Global
Compact relating  to business and  human rights.La Poste Group’s Responsible Purchasing policy, validated
by La Banque Postale’s Executive Committee in January 2023,
is based on four pillars, the first of  which  formalises
La Banque Postale’s commitment to “enforce and promote
fundamental rights throughout supply  chains”.
As such,  this pillar covers  the following  SDGs:
•SDG 3: Ensure  healthy lives and promote well-being for
all at all ages;
•SDG 5: Achieve gender equality and empower all women
and  girls;
•SDG 8:  Promote  sustained,  inclusive  and sustainable
economic  growth, full and productive  employment and
decent  work  for all;
•SDG 10: reduce inequalities between countries. [S2_1_05]
In addition, La Banque Postale’s commitments in terms of
its suppliers’ respect for human rights are included in its
Responsible  and Ethical Purchasing Charter, which is
published on the  institutional  website. The reciprocal
commitments set out in this Charter are based in particular
on the  fundamental principles of the United Nations
Global Compact and ILO conventions in the areas of
human rights, labour  law, respect for the  environment
and  anti-corruption.
Through the Charter, La   Banque   Postale  reiterates the
role of its buyers  in terms of compliance with the Code  of
Ethics and the application of the principles of fair treatment,
transparency and independence  for suppliers.
Beyond the commitments relating to human rights and
compliance with  international standards presented  in
paragraph 2.3.2.2.2 “Applicable policies”, this Charter requires
suppliers  to:
•Promote working conditions within  the company that
respect workers’ rights, in particular to prevent psychosocial
risks;
•Not practise any form of discrimination and promote
equal  professional treatment;
•Comply with all anti-corruption  laws, regulations and
international  standards;
•Make  this charter enforceable against their own
subcontractors and suppliers;
•Receive  external auditors responsible for verifying
compliance with these principles and implement corrective
actions in the event of identified shortcomings. This process
has been in  place since  the fourth quarter of 2024.
•Take appropriate measures, in consultation with the
company concerned, in the event of a report of a situation
contrary 
to respect for Human  Rights on  a postal site,
against a  member of staff or that of an external
company. [S2_1_01] [S2_1_02]198 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
In its appendix,  the Charter cites  Convention no. 29 on  the
fight against forced labour and Convention no. 182 on the
fight  against child labour, as well as the United Nations
Global  Compact principles no. 4  (the elimination of all
forms  of forced or compulsory  labour)  and  no. 5  (the
effective  abolition  of child labour).
The human rights  commitments of suppliers are  also set
out in La  Banque  Postale’s contractual documents and
purchase  orders, which include a “due diligence” clause.
[S2_1_05]  [S2_1_08]
CNP  Assurances’ policies are also aligned with the United
Nations 
guidelines on Human Rights. Through its Responsible
Purchasing policy, CNP  Assurances (SA and its French
subsidiaries)  considers respect  for fundamental rights and
their  promotion throughout supply chains as one of its
priority  issues. The Company is committed to working
with suppliers who comply with these principles, including:
•guaranteeing  decent working conditions  that  respect
human rights;
•ensuring transparent  management  of remuneration
and working  hours;
•encouraging access  to training;
•respecting the right to organise and freedom of association.
At the same time, CNP  Assurances SA strives to prevent
and  mitigate the risks of human rights violations. It is
committed to promoting professional equality and combating
all forms  of discrimination.
All of these principles are included in a Responsible Supplier
Charter,  intended for  suppliers  since  December 2024.
In  January 2025, the Responsible Purchasing policy and
the Responsible Supplier Charter were translated and rolled
out in CNP  Assurances ’ foreign subsidiaries. [S2_1_01] [S2_1_02]
Supplier  assessment
In order to cover the risks that La  Banque Postale incurs in
the context of relations with its “prospective” suppliers
and  its “stock” suppliers, it assesses these based on the
following aspects:
•Financial risk (obligation of the French Commercial Code
with  regard to  the abuse of economic dependency as
well as the  risk of  supplier, service provider or distributor
default);  Risk of  corruption (French Sapin II law) and
AML-CFT;
•Documentary risk (French  Due diligence law);
•CSR  risk (French  Due  diligence  law).
The assessment of suppliers is carried out with respect to
prospects,  before entering into  any relationship with a
new supplier, and updated annually for all of La Banque Postale’s
suppliers (except for a few specific cases specified in the
“Supplier  assessment”  procedure). This  assessment is
carried out in  accordance with this procedure which the
Purchasing Department  has put  in place.The CSR compliance risk is monitored with two matters,
one of which is human rights. These matters are considered
in 
relation to the supplier’s main purchasing segment,
through the risk  levels  observed in  this segment.
These  indicators, in line with  the AFNOR framework and
rated  from 1 to 4 (4 being a highly exposed segment), are
transcribed 
into three  risk levels (high, medium and low) in
the supplier compliance portfolio.
CSR 
compliance is assessed using the AFNOR mapping
for the supplier’s main business segment. This is an
automatic 
transaction performed when  the supplier is
integrated  into the portfolio. The supplier’s CSR rating is
included in  the  supplier mapping.  If the supplier  is able to
present a CSR assessment or certification specific to its
organisation, this is included in the mapping, without
modifying  the initial  level  of CSR  risk.
To go further, La  Banque   Postale is currently deploying
the e-compliance solution  set up by La Poste Group,
which uses the Ecovadis CSR rating tool, supplemented
by a CSR  maturity questionnaire sent to suppliers under
contract, suppliers under purchase orders and direct
invoicing  suppliers.  Depending on the response to this
questionnaire, a documentary or on-site audit may be
launched with the supplier.
In addition, the “due diligence” clause in supplier contracts
and in the General Purchasing Conditions requires the
supplier 
to identify the risk of infringement of fundamental
rights. 
In the event that such a risk is proven, the supplier
undertakes 
to implement appropriate actions to mitigate it.
[S2_1_04]
No case  of non-compliance with these principles has
been  reported to date in the upstream value chain of
La Banque Postale Group. [S2_1_09]
Compliance  with  the Group’s  code of conduct
The Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter between
La  Banque  Postale and  its suppliers  also commits
La Banque Postale to building  an ethical and high-quality
relationship with its suppliers. La Banque Postale employees
are 
invited to consult the Group’s code of conduct, and
undertake to comply with it.
The Charter also formalises the anti-corruption commitments
expected from suppliers, in line with La Poste Group’s
“zero 
tolerance” policy. In terms of ethics, La Banque Postale’s
code of conduct, intended for all third parties with which
it does  business,  is available  on its website. This code of
conduct is included in the appendix of the contracts signed
between La Banque Postale an d its  suppliers.  [S2_1_06]
The provisions of the code of conduct are  in line with
applicable ILO standards.  [S2_1_07]
At CNP  Assurances, the CapEthic code of conduct sets
out 
the principles and ethical values  which apply to  its
senior executives, employees and stakeholders. It can be
consulted 
on the CNP   Assurances institutional  website,
and  serves as a shared reference throughout the Group.
From  January 2025, the Responsible Suppliers Charter is
signed by the supplier when entering into  a relationship
with CNP  Assurances . [S2_1_06]Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 1992Sustainable performance

title: Dialogue mechanisms
heading: 2.3.2.2.5 Dialogue mechanisms
start_phrase: As part of its ESG approach and its “Responsible Purchasing” policy, La Banque Postale ensures that the views of workers in its upstream value chain are incorporated into its decisions and activities.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s CSR governance of its upstream value chain, emphasizing supplier dialogue, responsible purchasing, and worker voice mechanisms.
- Ongoing supplier dialogue: Initiated pre-contract via compliance analysis and maintained throughout the relationship; annual compliance reviews for all suppliers invoicing ≥€10,000; existing channels include mediation, supplier listening, and whistleblowing.
- Mediation system: Independent supplier relations Mediator (shared with La Poste Group), accessible online, participates in the Responsible Purchasing Committee (ARCOM), issues annual reports, and proposes out-of-court solutions; usage is monitored monthly with no cases to date.
- Supplier listening program: Structured engagement with intellectual services suppliers (project management/assistance/consulting) via questionnaires, annual meetings, relationship committees, and KPI tracking; assesses CSR maturity and drives improvements. Since Oct 2024, includes questions on working conditions and internal whistleblowing systems. Results inform action plans where needed.
- 2024 updates: Nov 2024 questionnaire to verify suppliers’ own worker-voice systems; related questions integrated into third-party audit tools from Nov 2024; the listening program is conducted annually for the specified supplier panel.
- Governance and compliance: The purchasing function owns Responsible Purchasing and ensures contractual and GPC compliance; this was validated by “Supplier Relations and Responsible Purchasing” certification in Sep 2023 and confirmed in a Jun 2024 follow-up audit.
- Reporting and remediation: All workers in the upstream value chain can access the whistleblowing platform and supplier mediator via the corporate website; the whistleblowing system covers suppliers and their workers. Suppliers are contractually required to inform their employees about the platform and ensure access.
- Outcomes to date: Supplier consultations indicate high satisfaction and no significant issues regarding working conditions or impacts, so no decision changes have been needed, while maintaining vigilance and continuous dialogue.
text:
3.2.2.5
Dialogue  mechanisms
As 
part of its ESG approach and its “Responsible Purchasing”
policy,  La  Banque  Postale ensures that the views of
workers  in its upstream value chain are incorporated into
its decisions and activities. Regular consultations with
suppliers reveal a high level of satisfaction and the absence
of significant feedback on working conditions or potential
impacts.  As a result, no change in decisions or activities
has been necessary to date. However, La Banque Postale
remains  committed to maintaining an active dialogue
with  its suppliers to identify and address any future needs,
in line with  its commitments. [S2_2_01]
Dialogue  with suppliers  is initiated  before entering into a
relationship 
with a prospect, based on supplier compliance
analysis. This dialogue continues throughout the relationship
between La Banque Postale and its  suppliers,  through:
•a compliance analysis carried out annually on the entire
portfolio  of suppliers who invoiced at least €10,000 over
the previous  year;
•all the systems in place: mediation, supplier listening
and  whistleblowing system. [S2_2_03]
Mediation  system
In 2023, La  Banque  Postale set up a “supplier relations”
Mediator,  which can be consulted by suppliers when a real
or potential impact on  workers in the value chain is
identified.  [S2_2_01]
La Banque Postale’s supplier Mediator, who is also La Poste
Group ’s supplier Mediator, can be contacted by suppliers
at all times  via a  URL.  Th e Mediator takes part in
La  Banque   Postale’s Responsible Purchasing Committee
(ARCOM),  which  meets every  four  months. [S2_2_03]
La Banque Postale’s Mediator is fully independent. It analyses
disputes impartially,  proposes out-of-court  solutions  and
publishes an annual activity report detailing trends and
recommendations to 
prevent and resolve conflicts.
The “use of the Mediator” indicator is  monitored monthly
in the responsible purchasing dashboard, and no use has
been  identified  to date . [S2_2_04]
Supplier  listening  system
La  Banque  Postale interacts with workers in the value
chain through representatives appointed by the supplier’s
company  to represent it. With them, La  Banque Postale’s
Purchasing Department has set  up a “supplier listening”
system with project management and consulting intellectual
services firms.
This system promotes proactive collaboration with suppliers.
A pilot programme was launched to collect their feedback
in 2023 through questionnaires and annual meetings.
This 
project aimed to assess their CSR maturity and improve
practices 
through regular discussions, relationship committees
and monitoring  of key indicators  (KPIs).
Since  October 2024, this system has included questions
relating to the systems put in place by the supplier to enable
its employees  to benefit from  good  working  conditions,
as well as the implementation of a whistleblowing system.
[S2_2_02]Through 
these interviews, the Purchasing Department
collects 
supplier feedback on the positive aspects of
the  relationship, but also on areas for improvement.
This 
approach also enables  it to find out about  the
systems put in place by its stakeholders on various topics,
including  working conditions and, since October  2024, the
internal whistleblowing  system.
The analysis of the results of this system can, as far as
necessary, serve as the basis for an appropriate action plan
depending  on the nature of the identified areas for
improvement.  [S2_2_06]
The Purchasing  Department launched a questionnaire in
November 2024, in order to identify whether the same
type of system is in place at its suppliers of intellectual services
(project management/project management assistance/
consulting categories). The questions  relating to the
implementation  of such systems are  also included in the
third-party audit questionnaires, which have been in place
since  November 2024. [S2_3_03]
The “supplier listening” system is set up annually, with the
panel of intellectual services suppliers in the project
management/project management  assistance/consulting
categories. 
[S2_2_03]
As specified in the "Supplier Relations and Responsible
Purchasing Charter" signed by La  Banque Postale in 2022,
La Banque Postale’s purchasing function is responsible for
the Responsible Purchasing policy, and particularly for
suppliers’  compliance with the provisions set out in the
contracts and in the General Purchasing Conditions.
The 
auditor who carried out the audit for the award of the
“Supplier 
Relations and Responsible Purchasing” certification
to La  Banque   Postale in  September 2023 approved this
point,  and confirmed it during  the follow-up audit carried
out in June 2024.  [S2_2_02]
2.

title: Reporting and remediation process
heading: 2.3.2.2.6 Reporting and remediation process
start_phrase: In addition to the dialogue mechanisms with suppliers described above, workers in the upstream value chain also have access to the whistleblowing system set up by La Banque Postale.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s ESG/Responsible Purchasing approach to integrating upstream value chain workers’ perspectives, managing reporting and remediation, and maintaining targets.
- Supplier dialogue mechanisms:
  - Pre-engagement and ongoing compliance reviews, including annual analyses for suppliers billing ≥€10k.
  - Multiple channels: supplier mediation, supplier listening, and whistleblowing.
- Mediation system:
  - “Supplier relations” Mediator established in 2023, shared with La Poste Group, accessible online, independent, part of the Responsible Purchasing Committee (ARCOM), issues annual reports.
  - Usage monitored monthly; no cases to date.
- Supplier listening system:
  - Engagement via supplier representatives, with pilots among project management/consulting firms.
  - Questionnaires, annual meetings, relationship committees, and KPI monitoring assess CSR maturity and identify improvements.
  - Since Oct 2024, includes questions on working conditions and whistleblowing; results can trigger action plans.
  - Nov 2024: questionnaire and third‑party audits expanded to check such systems at intellectual services suppliers; process repeated annually on a defined panel.
- Governance and assurance:
  - Purchasing function accountable for Responsible Purchasing policy and supplier compliance (contracts and GPC).
  - Confirmed by “Supplier Relations and Responsible Purchasing” certification audit (Sept 2023) and follow‑up (June 2024).
- Reporting and whistleblowing:
  - Whistleblowing platform covers all upstream value chain workers; access via LBP website.
  - Suppliers must inform their employees and provide access per contracts/GPC.
  - Ethics Officer manages reports; Purchasing Director involved for supplier-related cases; protection against reprisals ensured.
  - LBP assesses risk to certain worker categories as limited; current system deemed sufficient.
- Remediation approach:
  - LBP will remediate if it caused or contributed to negative impacts on value chain workers.
  - No formal written remediation process yet due to no proven negative impacts; commits to implement appropriate, proportionate remedies with monitoring and stakeholder feedback if needed.
- Subsidiaries:
  - CNP Assurances: buyers trained to identify/report impacts; cases handled by Compliance/HR/Procurement/Legal; reporters informed; external mediation possible; focus on non‑recurrence.
  - LBP AM: procedure for non‑compliance; can terminate supplier relationships and notify relevant authorities (e.g., HALDE, CNIL).
- Targets and performance management:
  - Three‑year action plan with regularly monitored targets informed by supplier feedback and monitoring systems; reviewed by the Responsible Purchasing Committee.
  - Maintain established levels: 100% inclusion of CSR criteria in tenders and 100% worker coverage by a charter guaranteeing healthy and safe working conditions.
  - Effectiveness assessed via supplier listening questionnaires and analysis of providers’ CSR criteria.
text:
3.2.2.6 Reporting and remediation process
In addition to the dialogue mechanisms with suppliers
described 
above, workers in the upstream value chain also
have 
access to the whistleblowing system set up by
La  Banque  Postale. This system enables them to report
their concerns  directly to the  Group. [S2_3_02]
La Banque Postale provides access to all of these channels,
(whistleblowing 
and supplier mediator), to any worker in
the 
value chain, as  long as they can access digital equipment.
This access is in fact available  via the La  Banque  Postale
institutional website. [S2_3_03]
Whistleblowing system
The whistleblowing system set up by La Banque Postale is
designed  to cover all workers in the upstream value chain,
whether 
they are the Group’s suppliers or their workers.
This system is described in paragraph 2.4.1.3.5 “Independence
and accessibility of the whistleblowing system”. [S2_3_0 2]
Workers 
in the value chain are informed by their employer
of 
the existence of the whistleblowing reporting platform.
Through the contract signed with La  Banque  Postale or via
La 
Banque Postale’s General Purchasing Conditions, suppliers
commit 
to becoming familiar with La  Banque  Postale’s
whistleblowing procedure, informing their employees working
with La Banque Postale of the existence of this  platform,
and providing them with access to this whistleblowing
system.  [S2_3_05]200 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
Reports  are handled  by La Banque Postale’s Ethics Officer
who, in  the event of a report relating  to or originating
from a supplier or one of its  employees, contacts the
Purchasing  Director  to process the  report.  [S2_2_03]  [S2_3_04]
With regard to value chain workers or their representatives,
the 
operational processing of the report is the responsibility
of the Purchasing function  for which the highest role is
that  of the Purchasing Director. The  Purchasing Director
reports to the Managing Director  in charge  of Finance
and Strategy, who is  a member of  La  Banque  Postale's
Executive Board.  [S2_2_04]
In addition, whistleblowers are protected from reprisals in
accordance  with  regulations. [S2_3_06]
Given  the nature of La  Banque  Postale ’s activities, the
specific  risks associated with certain categories of workers
remain  limited. This assessment is based on the absence
of structural or operational factors  that would particularly
expose certain categories of workers, due to the  type  of
activity and the geographical location of the Group’s
activities.
Thus,  the current system is considered sufficient to meet
the needs of all  stakeholders. By offering a secure and
accessible  environment to all, this mechanism helps to
strengthen  collective  due diligence  and protect the
fundamental  rights of workers throughout  the  value
chain.  [S2_2_07]
Report  handling  process
If La  Banque   Postale is alerted by a third-party supplier
that it  has  caused  or contributed to a  negative  impact  on
one or more workers in the value chain, it will manage the
remediation  of this negative impact.
To date,  La Banque Postale  does not have a formal written
process or  specific  cases dealt  with  in the past  on the
subject of remedy mechanisms as part of the management
of human rights incidents, as the Group has identified no
proven  negative  impact,  only  potential  impacts.
However,  La Banque Postale is aware of the importance of
being  prepared to manage such incidents should they
occur, and undertakes, if necessary, to implement appropriate
and proportionate remedies. To do so, it will take into
account  best practices  in terms of managing impacts on
human rights and respecting the expectations of the
stakeholders 
concerned. Lastly, in order to guarantee their
effectiveness, they will be accompanied by assessment
mechanisms.  These would  include regular  monitoring
processes and feedback from the relevant stakeholders to
verify  that the  solutions provided fully meet the identified
needs and  contribute  effectively  to resolving  negative
impacts.  [S2_3_01]
Remediation of  negative impacts in the subsidiaries
At CNP Assurances,  all buyers are trained to identify negative
impacts and report them to their manager, who contacts
the appropriate person according to the topic  and severity
of the impact. These cases are then handled by Compliance,
Human Resources, Procurement or the Legal Department,
which determines the appropriate actions.When an impact is reported, the topic is analysed according
to 
the process  of the chosen channel. In all  cases, the
persons authorised to handle reports contact the third
party  that submitted the report to keep them informed of
the result of  the analysis. Depending on the type of
concern/dispute (compliance with human rights, harassment,
discrimination, pressure from  management,  etc.),  matters
are addressed internally with the relevant contacts.
Meetings with stakeholders are  held to  review the
situation and attempt  to remedy it. In certain cases,
CNP  Assurances  may use an external mediator. It will then
be necessary to  ensure that once remediation has been
carried  out, this type  of impact does  not occur again.
LBP  AM has put in place a  procedure to take the
necessary  actions in the event of non-compliance with its
Responsible  Purchasing policy, and reserves the right to
terminate relationships with suppliers who do not comply
with its Responsible and Ethical Purchasing Charter.
In the event  of a practice contrary to  this Responsible  and
Ethical Purchasing Charter and contrary to human rights,
respect for people or the  environment, LBP   AM reserves
the right to inform the HALDE (French Equal Opportunities
and Anti-Discrimination  Commission), the CNIL  (French
Data Protection Commission) and any other relevant
institution. 
[S2_3_01]
2.

title: Targets
heading: 2.3.2.2.7 Targets
start_phrase: La Banque Postale's Responsible Purchasing approach is based on targets that are regularly monitored.
summary:
- Governance of reports and ethics: La Banque Postale’s Ethics Officer oversees reports; supplier-related cases are processed with the Purchasing Director, who reports to the Managing Director (Finance & Strategy) on the Executive Board. Whistleblowers are protected from reprisals.
- Scope and risk profile: Given LBP’s business nature and locations, specific worker-category risks are considered limited; existing mechanisms are deemed sufficient and inclusive for value chain workers.
- Report handling and remediation: If alerted by a supplier of a negative impact on workers, LBP manages remediation. While no formal written remediation process exists due to no proven negative impacts to date, LBP commits to implement appropriate, proportionate remedies with best practices, stakeholder engagement, and monitoring if needed.
- Subsidiary practices:
  - CNP Assurances: Buyers trained to identify/report impacts; cases handled by Compliance/HR/Procurement/Legal; stakeholder meetings, possible external mediation; prevention of recurrence required.
  - LBP AM: Procedure for non-compliance with Responsible Purchasing policy; may terminate supplier relationships and inform relevant authorities (e.g., HALDE, CNIL) for breaches related to human rights or ethics.
- Targets and monitoring (Responsible Purchasing):
  - Maintain inclusion of CSR criteria in 100% of tenders.
  - Ensure 100% of supplier workers are covered by charters guaranteeing healthy, safe working conditions.
  - LBP AM supplier CSR adoption: ≥75% of eligible suppliers in 2024; ≥80% in 2025–2026.
  - Inclusion Market platform: increase buyer use; currently monitored via dashboards and stakeholder feedback; plan to formalize quantitative targets.
- Human rights safeguards in the value chain:
  - 100% of upstream workers covered by a charter aligned with UN Global Compact and ILO conventions.
  - Zero cases of forced or child labor in 2024; target is to maintain zero and full coverage.
- Supplier financial risk management:
  - Annual financial risk analysis for 100% of suppliers invoicing >€10k (N-1) and 100% of prospects.
  - Dependency threshold at 25% triggers an action plan; goal is to maintain full coverage and annual cadence.
- Action plans and resources:
  - A structured, three-year Responsible Purchasing action and improvement plan defines actions, targets, and deadlines.
  - Plan aligned with RFAR certification; initiated in 2022, validated by the Purchasing Director, independently audited, running through 2025; new 2026–2029 roadmap to be prepared in 2025.
- Supplier awareness and contractualization:
  - Systematic communication of the Responsible Purchasing Charter; reinforced via training and contractual clauses on worker rights and social standards.
- CSR integration in procurement:
  - Tenders include social/CSR criteria (e.g., ethics/anti-corruption training, CO2 data for hardware/software, equipment sustainability/compatibility).
  - CSR criteria carry significant weight (≥10%) in evaluations to drive responsible supplier practices.
text:
3.2.2.7 Targets
La Banque Postale's Responsible Purchasing approach is
based on targets that are regularly monitored. These targets
are 
set as part of a three-year action plan, taking  into
account the material  impacts identified as well as the
information collected from suppliers  and their  employees
through the dialogue  mechanisms in place.
Improvements resulting from the Company’s performance
are presented to the Responsible Purchasing Committee.
They  are recorded  and formalised  as part of the review of
the action plan,  in order to set the new targets for the
three-year plan. [S2_5_01] [S2_5_02] [S2_5_03]
The results of the various supplier monitoring  systems are
also taken into account when  setting these targets.
Contributing to the improvement of working conditions
and the protection and inclusion of workers in the value
chain  of own operations and service activities
La Banque Postale has previously set  measurable targets
and does not plan to set  new targets  for these actions,
because:
•CSR criteria are included in 100% of  calls for tenders;
•All supplier workers  are already covered by a charter
guaranteeing healthy and safe working conditions.
The effectiveness of policies related  to working conditions
is assessed through supplier listening questionnaires and
the analysis of service providers’ CSR criteria.
La  Banque  Postale’s targets is to maintain this level of
excellence by ensuring:
•100%  of workers continue to be covered by a charter
promoting healthy and safe working conditions.
•CSR criteria  continue  to be included  in 100%  of calls  for
tender.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 2012Sustainable performance
Social information
As part of its Purchasing policy, LBP AM has set itself the
following targets:
•2024: 
at least 75% of eligible suppliers(1)  have CSR approaches
that  promote  respect  for fundamental rights;
•2025-2026:  at least 80% of eligible suppliers have CSR
approaches that promote respect for fundamental rights.
[S2_MDR_T_01_13]
At present, La  Banque  Postale cannot set quantifiable
targets  for the use of the Marché de l’Inclusion (Inclusion
Market) platform,  as it has  only recently  been launched.
However,  it aims to increase its use by buyers. Monitoring
is already  in place:
•Occasional feedback from stakeholders is shared;
•A quantitative indicator on the use of the platform is regularly
monitored via the Purchasing Department’s dashboard,
presented at the meetings held every four months (ARCOM).
The target is to formalise precise quantitative monitoring
of the  rate  of use  of the  platform while  boosting the
promotion of the Inclusion Market to buyers. [S2_MDR_T_14_19]
Negative impact in the event of poor working conditions
(unequal remuneration, safety, etc.), forced labour and/
or child labour within companies in the value chain of
own operations  and service activities
Measurable targets  have  been  set:
•100%  of workers in the upstream value chain are
covered  by a  charter guaranteeing compliance with the
principles  of the United Nations Global Compact and
the ILO’s  fundamental conventions;
•No cases  of forced labour  or child  labour were  reported
in 2024.  The  Responsible Purchasing  Charter is signed
and third-party audits ensure the effectiveness of this policy.
The target  is to maintain  this level of ambition by:
•ensuring  100%  of workers continue to  be covered by a
charter  which respects the principles of the Global
Compact  and  the ILO  conventions;
•maintaining  the total absence of workers affected by
forced  labour  or child labour. [S2_MDR_T_01_13]
Management  of financial risks related to suppliers in
a context of transition to a more equitable and inclusive
society
La  Banque  Postale does not set additional measurable
targets  for these  actions, because:
•100%  of suppliers  invoicing more than €10,000 in year
N-1 and 100% of prospects are subject to an annual
financial  risk analysis.
These  risks, including the supplier dependency rate, are
rigorously  monitored. If the dependency threshold (25%) is
exceeded,  an action plan is systematically put in place.
The target  is to maintain  this level of rigo ur by:
•ensuring  that 100%  of suppliers remain covered by an
associated financial  risk analysis.
•guaranteeing that these assessments are carried out each
year. 
[S2_MDR_T_01_13]2.

title: Action plans and resources
heading: 2.3.2.2.8 Action plans and resources
start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group deploys a structured strategy to ensure that matters related to workers in the value chain are taken into account, based on a number of practical and coordinated actions.
summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s responsible purchasing and social performance regarding workers in its upstream value chain and financed activities, within the 2024 Universal Registration Document.
- Supplier CSR targets: LBP AM aims for at least 75% of eligible suppliers with CSR approaches promoting fundamental rights in 2024, rising to 80% in 2025–2026.
- Inclusion Market platform: recently launched tool to source inclusive suppliers; usage is being monitored via dashboards and ARCOM meetings every four months, with plans to formalize quantitative targets and increase buyer adoption.
- Human rights safeguards: targets to keep 100% of upstream value chain workers covered by a charter aligned with the UN Global Compact and ILO conventions; zero cases of forced or child labor in 2024 and goal to maintain this.
- Financial risk management of suppliers: 100% of suppliers invoicing >€10k and all prospects receive annual financial risk analyses; supplier dependency >25% triggers systematic action plans; objective is to sustain full coverage annually.
- Governance and action planning: Group Purchasing Department leads a structured, three-year responsible purchasing action plan under the RFAR certification; current plan runs 2022–2025 with a new roadmap planned for 2026–2029.
- Supplier engagement: widespread communication of the Responsible Purchasing Charter, use of training and contractual clauses to embed CSR expectations.
- CSR in tenders: social and environmental criteria integrated into RFPs (e.g., ethics/anti-corruption training, CO₂ data, product longevity/compatibility), weighted at least 10% of overall scoring.
- Audit regime: internal/external audits (Provigis, Indued) and third‑party audits (via La Poste–selected firms) on anti‑corruption and due diligence; annual third‑party audits from December 2024.
- Inclusion initiatives: systematic access to the Inclusion Market for buyers since 2024 and promotion of inclusive purchasing, including suppliers supporting social inclusion and disability employment.
- Internal awareness: ongoing ESG dissemination via Just Transition ambassadors and Sustainability; 2023–2024 awareness for specifiers on responsible purchasing criteria.
- SME access: creation of an SME Officer role planned for 2025 to facilitate SME engagement with purchasing.
- Incidents and remediation: no forced or child labor incidents or other human rights breaches reported in 2024; updated purchasing documentation includes due‑diligence clauses and whistleblowing links; no remediation required.
- Risk management tools: annual ExCo reviews of portfolio and risk map; specific risk sheets and corrective action plans for working-condition and compliance risks; responsible purchasing procedures and manual to be updated in 2025.
- Resources and budget: Supplier Mediator, Ethics Officer, Purchasing Department involved; external audit budget €20k (2024) and €100k (2025); ~0.5 FTE allocated in 2024–2025 for supplier assessment.
- Monitoring effectiveness: indicators tracked via a Responsible Purchasing dashboard; progress reviewed by a committee every four months; annual external RFAR audits with employee/representative consultations; RFAR label obtained in Sept 2023 (based on standard 20400).
- Safeguards and grievance: contractual clauses on worker rights and data protection; internal/external audits, risk mapping, and a confidential whistleblowing system in place; no severe human rights incidents reported.
- Financed activities scope: material impacts on workers in the value chain considered across financing by CNP Assurances, LBP AM, and Louvre Banque Privée; use of the Impact Weighting Factor and controversy management to assess issuers.
- Strategic linkage: human rights, climate, and biodiversity commitments inform risk controls and sector policies; while considered, these topics do not directly reshape the business model.
- Material risks: identified risk of financial loss from inadequate partner assessment during the transition to a fairer, more inclusive society due to multi‑sector, multi‑geography exposure.
- Forced/child labor exposure in portfolios: indirect risk via asset management; LBP AM mapped salient human rights risks in 2023 following OECD/UNGP guidance and disclosed methodology/results; most critical risk identified is violation of fundamental workers’ rights in the downstream value chain.
text:
3.2.2.8 Action plans  and resources
Actions implemented
Process of defining actions
La Banque Postale Group deploys a structured strategy to
ensure 
that matters  related to  workers  in the value chain
are taken into  account, based  on a number of practical
and  coordinated actions. Through this comprehensive
and consistent approach, La Banque Postale demonstrates
its commitment to integrating workers’ rights and conditions
into  its responsible purchasing  processes, by meeting
regulatory requirements while promoting exemplary social
practices.
The Group Purchasing Department is responsible for
defining this strategy. It is developed based on the
negative and positive impacts identified, but also on the
information collected  through  the dialogue mechanisms
presented  above. If necessary, the information  can be
traced back to the members of the La  Banque  Postale
Group Executive  Board.
As part of its Responsible Purchasing approach, the
Purchasing Department operates on a three-year  action
and  improvement plan, which can be reviewed  during the
third year.
Each action, broken down into stages, is associated with a
target 
and a deadline.  The Purchasing Department is
committed  to implementing the  action plan presented
under  the "Supplier Relations and Responsible Purchasing
(RFAR)" certification.
This plan, initiated in 2022, developed in  accordance with
the requirements of the responsible purchasing label, was
validated 
by the Purchasing Director and audited  by an
independent body as part of the certification process. It
runs 
until the end of 2025. A new roadmap will be prepared
in 2025 for the 2026-2029  period.  [S2_4_05] [S2_4_06] [S2_4_07]
Raising supplier  awareness  of CSR issues
In addition, La Banque Postale strives to raise its  suppliers’
awareness of CSR issues by systematically communicating
its Responsible Purchasing Charter, which contains specific
commitments 
on respect for workers’  rights and social
standards. This awareness-raising process continues through
training or specific contractual clauses. [S2_MDR_A_01_12] [S2_4_03]
[S2_4_01]
Establishing CSR criteria  in the selection of service 
providers and suppliers
Questionnaires included in calls for tender include social
criteria in the supplier assessment grids (hardware, software
and intellectual services). These criteria include, for example,
the training of consultants in ethics and anti-corruption,
details on the CO₂ consumption of hardware and software
and equipment compatibility to promote its sustainability.
These 
criteria have a significant weighting, i.e. at least 10%
of the overall score. This measure encourages suppliers to
adopt 
responsible practices in line with the Group’s
expectations. 
[S2_MDR_A_01_12] [S2_4_03]  [S2_4_01]
(1) Suppliers  selected as  part of a competition or call for tenders, excluding monopolies and semi-monopolies.202 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
Implementation  of supplier audits
A rigorous  control system  is also  in place to  assess the
compliance of  suppliers with social regulations and
commitments made.
Internal  and external audits are carried out, using tools
such as Provigis and Indued, to verify documentary
compliance , the management of social risks and the
implementation  of corrective actions when necessary.
These audits prevent non-compliance while strengthening
relationships of trust with upstream value  chain partners.
La  Banque  Postale uses audit firms selected by La  Poste
to carry out  third-party audits. These audits can be
documentary or  on-site and cover the themes of the fight
against  corruption and the  duty of vigilance. Above all, this
enables La  Banque  Postale to ensure compliance with
the commitments made by suppliers when the Responsible
and  Ethical Purchasing  Charter was signed.
The preparatory phase  of the third-party audit system on
anti-corruption and due diligence issues was completed
in November 2024.  From December  2024, audits  will be
carried out every  year. [S2_MDR_A_01_12]  [S2_4_01]
Creating an inclusive working  environment
Since  2024,  a system  has been  put  in place  to encourage
La Banque Postale buyers to consult the Inclusion Market
website  when sourcing.  The Inclusion Market is a tool
bringing together disability and  integration service
providers across  150 purchasing categories.
This  initiative applies to  supplier selection operations,
which  make up La Banque Postale’s upstream value chain
in France.
The deployment of the Inclusion Market access system
was both started and completed in 2024. [S2_MDR_A_01_12]
[S2_4_03]
Initiatives  to promote social inclusion
In a proactive  approach, La  Banque  Postale  is also
developing initiatives to promote social inclusion. For
example,  it actively promotes  inclusive purchasing  by
using  dedicated  platforms  such  as the  Inclusion Market,
which  promotes suppliers committed to social inclusion
or support for people with disabilities, for consultations
relating  to compatible  purchasing categories.
These  initiatives are part  of a desire  to maximise social
opportunities and meet the expectations of internal and
external stakeholders. Finally, dialogue  with suppliers is
central  to La   Banque  Postale’s strategy. [S2_MDR_A_01_12]
[S2_4_03]
Raising  awareness  among  Group employees
To disseminate ESG topics within the Group, regular
meetings  are held between Just Transition ambassadors
and  the Sustainability Department. In 2023 and 2024,
awareness-raising was carried out on the Responsible
Purchasing  approach, aimed at informing all specifiers of
the CSR criteria concerning workers in the upstream value
chain, in addition to the Purchasing Department.
[S2_MDR_A_01_12] [S2_4_03]
Introducing an SME Officer
La  Banque  Postale Group is also developing a project to
facilitate  SME  access  La  Banque   Postale’s Purchasing
contacts, with  an SME Officer  to boost its links with SMEs.
This position will be  filled in 2025, and the assignment
sheet  is being  finalis ed. [S2_MDR_A_01_12] [S2_4_03]Incidents  of forced labour or  child labour
The documentation  on responsible purchasing was
updated in  2022. In 2024, the General Purchasing
Conditions  included new clauses relating to due diligence.
Links  to the whistleblowing system and  the Responsible
Purchasing and Ethics Charter have also been included. In
addition, awareness-raising was  carried out among the
entire Purchasing Department.
This is a potential negative impact that did not require
solutions. No one was affected  by this impact in 2024.
[S2_MDR_A_01_12] [S2_4_01]
Remediation of actual material impacts
No 
actual negative impact was reported in 2024, including
no case of  practices which infringe upon human rights.
As a result, La Banque Postale did  not need  to implement
remedial action  plans. [S2_4_02]
Managing risks related to workers in the upstream 
value chain
La  Banque   Postale  plans to update its reference
documents  on the  management  of risks  related  to
responsible  purchasing in  2025. The procedure for
assessing third parties and the  Purchasing Manual will be
improved  and  distributed to  the relevant stakeholders.
At least once a year, the Purchasing Department meets its
Executive  Committee to present an analysis of the
purchasing portfolio as well as the risk map.
First 
of all, a risk  map was drawn  up, specifically identifying
the risks related to working conditions and supplier
compliance. This map  is accompanied by  specific risk
sheets, which are regularly  updated, which include
corrective action plans  and priorities defined according to
the criticality of the issues identified. These tools allow the
Purchasing 
Department to focus its efforts on the most
sensitive  issues, while guaranteeing  a proactive response
to social factors. [S2_MDR_A_01_12]  [S2_4_08]
Resources allocated
The 
internal functions of La  Banque  Postale that
contribute to managing impacts  are the Supplier
Mediator, the Ethics Officer and the Purchasing
Department.
La  Banque  Postale uses external firms to carry out third-
party  audits on the due diligence component. The budget
allocated to these audits is €20,000 for 2024 and the
provisional  budget  for 2025 is  €100,000.
The supplier  assessment  questionnaire requires the
Purchasing Department's existing internal resources,
estimated at half a FTE in 2024 and half a FTE in 2025.
[S2_MDR_A_01_12] [S2_4_12]
Monitoring  the effectiveness of actions
Responsible  purchasing  performance monitoring is based
on a structured framework that includes the participation
of 
upstream value chain workers or  their  legitimate
representatives.
Each  action in  the Responsible Purchasing action plan is
monitored using specific indicators, compiled  in a
Responsible  Purchasing dashboard. This dashboard
brings together progress  on key aspects such as working
conditions, 
respect for  human and social rights, and the
environmental practices of suppliers.
The 
results of the monitoring are presented to the
Responsible Purchasing Committee every  four months.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 2032Sustainable performance
Social information
In addition, each year, an external audit assesses the
implementation  of the planned actions, with direct
consultations  with  employees  or their representatives,
within the framework of the Responsible Supplier
Relations  and Purchasing (RFAR)  label.  In September
2023,  La  Banque  Postale obtained the RFAR label, based
on the 20400 standard. This recognition reflects its
commitment  to a continuous improvement approach in
terms  of responsible purchasing.
Employee  representatives  are  therefore  involved through
regular consultations  that  are  shared  within the
Purchasing  Committee.  These  discussions  help to adjust
priorities and ensure that concerns are addressed. In
addition,  the  Company promotes constructive dialogue
with workers and representatives through its mediation
system,  ensuring that  suppliers are fully heard and any
disputes are resolved. [S2_4_04] [S2_5_02]
Thanks  to its structured approach and practical measures,
La  Banque  Postale guarantees that its own  practices do
not cause or contribute to significant negative impacts.
Relations  with suppliers are governed by  contracts that
include specific clauses on  compliance with employee
rights,  working conditions and personal data protection.
These  clauses require suppliers to comply with the
regulations in force, specifying that La  Banque  Postale
undertakes  not to impose commercial or contractual
conditions  likely to have a negative impact on workers in
the upstream  value  chain.
Internal  and external audits as well as risk mapping are
implemented  as part of the continuous assessment of
suppliers.  These measures make it  possible to identify any
negative  impacts related to working conditions. The
whistleblowing  system is also available to report any
incident  or concern. This system is governed by strict
confidentiality  and  data  protection  guarantees.  [S2_4_10]
Severe  human  rights  incidents
No human rights issues or severe incidents related to its
upstream  value chain were reported by the workers in the
value  chain  or by  their  legitimate  representatives,
regardless  of the  channel made available to them by
La Banque  Postale. [S2_4_11]
