title: Financing of local authorities, associations and the local economic sector
heading: 2.3.3.3.1 Financing of local authorities, associations and the local economic sector
start_phrase: La Banque Postale, through the Corporate and Local Development Banking (CLDB), implements strategic initiatives and concrete actions aimed at maximising positive impacts for the affected communities and is committed to local authorities and associations.
summary:
- Focus on human rights integration by LBP AM (La Banque Postale Asset Management) in line with OECD Guidelines and UN Guiding Principles: requires portfolio companies to consult affected stakeholders, provide accessible whistleblowing/complaints channels, and demonstrate effective remediation, with heightened expectations in sensitive/conflict areas. Dedicated SRI Solutions team (10 experts, including a human rights lead) and tools/risk mapping guide investment decisions. No serious human rights incidents reported in 2024.

- Commitments to affected communities through financing and operations: Corporate and Local Development Banking (CLDB) supports local authorities, associations, and the local economy. Ongoing dialogue via a Local Finance Steering Committee. Product innovations include “advance on subsidy” for associations, green/social loans (from €50,000) for essential services and responsible real estate, and an end-to-end donation collection solution; extensive partnerships with major nonprofits. Objective: enable a just and sustainable transition for the sector.

- Financing local authorities: 25% market share; comprehensive offer from cash management and bond solutions to short/long-term loans. Emphasis on responsible/social financing and Subzen grant-seeking support. Targeted impacts: modernizing public infrastructure, advancing sustainable mobility, supporting energy transition, and reducing regional disparities, including rural/remote areas.

- Support for other local public sector players: financing for hospitals and medico-social establishments (including Ségur de la Santé projects), nursing homes, and social housing (partners with 8/10 social housing operators; solutions for rent collection, receipts reconciliation, cash investments, and responsible production/renovation finance; second-largest commercial bank in the market). Ongoing financing for associations in social inclusion, health, and social protection.

- Tailored financial instruments to regional needs: real estate and equipment leasing, factoring, and asset securitization to enhance liquidity and reinvestment capacity.

- Capacity building for local decision-makers: publications, conferences, and tools (e.g., DOB budgeting aid); 2024 studies presented to the French Congress of Mayors; partnership with I4CE on climate action financing challenges; joint studies with the French Hospital Federation on hospital investments.

- Regional network impact: leveraging La Poste’s extensive footprint to maintain essential services, prevent banking deserts, support local development projects, and strengthen financial inclusion, with coordinated outreach to promote sustainable finance—especially in small towns and rural areas.

- Societal sponsorship: L’Envol program supports around 100 underprivileged youths for 3–8 years with mentoring and personalized monitoring; effectiveness assessed annually. Resources include a €2 million annual budget, dedicated staff (4 FTEs plus a work-study student) and community outreach hours (439 in 2023).

- MicroDon subsidiary enables embedded giving: checkout rounding (over €47.7 million raised to date), payroll giving, and time donations to associations, fostering a culture of solidarity and skills-based volunteering.

- Broader civic and ESG partnerships: strong engagement with the social and solidarity economy (150,000 association clients), participation in national campaigns (Téléthon, Breast Cancer Awareness, Pièces Jaunes), collaboration platforms on banking inclusion and budgeting education, WWF partnership for decarbonization, and ongoing dialogue with consumer associations.

3.3.3.1
Financing of  local authorities,  
associations and the local economic sector
La  Banque  Postale, through the Corporate and Local
Development 
Banking (CLDB), implements strategic initiatives
and concrete actions aimed at maximising positive impacts
for the affected communities and is committed to local
authorities and associations.
La  Banque  Postale maintains its ties with local public-
sector players, notably through its Local  Finance Steering
Committee, composed of elected  representatives,  former
members of parliament and experts. This Committee has
a 
forward-looking, observatory and advisory role:  risk
assessment, monitoring,  proposing new services,  etc.
La  Banque  Postale remains a  true partner to the social
and solidarity economy: one in every ten associations is a
customer 
of La Banque Postale. Its advisors work in business
centres throughout the territory, supporting  4,000 of the
main associations, which are foundations and associations
in the health sector, educational institutions, charitable
associations and social-purpose organisations.
Launched in 2020, La Banque Postale’s "advance on subsidy"
offer 
allows associations to benefit from advance cash
flow while waiting for the actual payment by the national
public 
authorities. Thanks to this offer, they can continue
to develop, finance their needs and support their public
interest missions.
In 
2022, La  Banque  Postale innovated by developing
green and social solutions supporting projects related to
responsible  real estate or promoting access to essential
life services such as health, education or housing through
accessible social loans of  €50,000  and  more.
In 2023, to meet  the challenge of donations, a major issue
for the sector, La  Banque  Postale has developed a new
"donation 
collection" offer to  boost associations' online
collections through a comprehensive process for the donor.
It has forged more than a hundred partnerships with
associations  or foundations recognised as being in the
public 
interest, such as the French Red Cross or the
Hospitals Foundation, to support them  in their  actions.
Aware of the challenges of the sector, La Banque Postale
has set itself the goal of supporting associations in their
efforts towards  a just and sustainable transition. [S3_4_03]Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 2132Sustainable performance
Social information
Financing  of local  authorities:  
supporting  regional  development
La  Banque  Postale has a 25% market share in financing
awarded to French local authorities.
La  Banque   Postale  provides a comprehensive  offering,
ranging  from cash flow  and investment management
(open  payment solutions or  OAT government bond
purchases , etc.) to short- and long-term banking and
bond financing solutions.
•Responsible financing banking offering.
•Range of social loans for local authorities.
•Subzen, 
a grant-seeking and grant-management support
service  to optimise funding  plans  for local authorities.
In addition, La Banque Postale , through its Corporate and
Local  Development  Banking  (CLDB),  actively  supports
local authorities  (municipalities, departments, regions) by
offering them strategic financing to modernize their
essential  infrastructures and strengthen their  resilience.
These actions aim  to maximise  the positive impacts for
the regions and their populations while promoting the
ecological  transition.
Modernisation of public infrastructure: financing of projects
to renovate schools, modernise  municipal facilities and
improve  public  transport.
Sustainable mobility: support for low-carbon public transport
projects  such as electric buses and trams, improving
cycling  infrastructure  to promote soft mobility.
Energy transition: support for energy renovation projects
for local administrative buildings; financing of renewable
energy solutions such as the installation of solar panels or
wind farms.
Reduction 
of regional  divides: directing  financing to rural
or remote  areas  to bridge  regional disparities. [S3_4_03]
Financing  of local  public sector players: supporting 
essential  services
In addition to local authorities, La Banque Postale supports
other  key players in the local public sector to provide
essential  services to  populations.
Hospitals  and medico-social establishments
•Ségur de la Santé Plan: financing of projects to modernise
public 
hospitals and health institutions to ensure better
access  to care,  particularly  for vulnerable  populations.
•Infrastructure development  support for nursing homes
and other public and  private non-profit healthcare
institutions.
Social housing
As a leading  bank  for social  housing players, with  8 social
housing operators out of 10 as partners, La Banque Postale
offers 
complete solutions for rent collection and reconciliation
of receipts, and dynamic cash investment vehicles over
short -, medium-  and long-term  periods, together with
responsible  financing for the  production and renovation
of housing. This innovative financing helps to meet the
growing need  for affordable  and  sustainable housing and
positions  La  Banque  Postale as the second largest
commercial  bank  in the market.Associations
La Banque Postale  finances the  activities of associations in
the areas of  social inclusion, health and social protection.
[S3_4_03]
Responding  to the specific needs of the regions
La Banque Postale offers structured financial tools adapted
to the specificities and diversity of the projects carried out
by local authorities and the local  public sector:
•real estate leasing: financing of public facilities such as
schools, hospitals or cultural centres;
•furniture  leasing: financing of professional equipment
for local authorities or public institutions, meeting specific
operational needs;
•factoring: solution to improve the cash flow of local
players,  allowing them to manage their financial flows
with more  flexibility;
•asset securitisation: activating loan portfolios to free up
financial capacity and enable local  players to  reinvest in
their priority projects. [S3_4_03]
Supporting  local elected officials 
and regional  public servants
La  Banque   Postale regularly  provides  regional elected
officials  and public servants with  its expertise in local
finances through  documents  and  conferences. In  addition
to its traditional publications such as its "Note de conjoncture"
update on local  finances or  its "Financial insights" in
partnership with  associations  of elected  representatives,
every year La  Banque  Postale offers a tool called "DOB"
(budget policy direction debate), a tool to  help prepare
local authority budgets. It consists of an analysis of the
finance law, supplemented by a selection of information
and graphs useful  for the preparation of  their budget.
In 2024, La Banque  Postale  was  invited to present a study
of its “Regional Access” collection, dedicated to local
authority 
cash flow, at the French Congress of Mayors.
This is a particularly pertinent topic in the context of rate
increases. 
In partnership with I4CE (Institute of the Economy
for 
the Climate), it carried out an overview of the economic
and budgetary challenges of  the  financing of climate
action by local authorities in the context of updating the

decarbonisation levers for the regions. Individual studies
can also be carried out  at the request of  local  authorities

Finally, also in 2024, La  Banque  Postale published the

title: Regional network
heading: 2.3.3.3.2 Regional network
start_phrase: La Banque Postale, through its integration within La Poste Group, plays a role in maintaining the regional network of essential services in France.
summary:
- Role of La Banque Postale’s regional network within La Poste Group:
  - Maintains essential banking and postal services nationwide, including rural and remote areas, via a dense post office and retail network.
  - Prevents “banking deserts,” ensures service continuity where other financial institutions are absent.
  - Supports local development and environmental transition through financing for regional planning and essential infrastructure (schools, hospitals, social housing).
  - Promotes financial inclusion with tailored solutions such as controlled-rate loans and inclusive banking products.
  - Synergy with La Poste: leverages postal presence to engage local elected officials on sustainable financial solutions; adapts services through ongoing dialogue with local authorities.

- Societal sponsorship and community impact:
  - L’Envol programme:
    - Long-term support (3–8 years) for ~100 youths per year from modest backgrounds to foster academic success, social inclusion, and access to higher education.
    - Personalized mentoring by monitoring officers and La Poste volunteers; oversight by the Deputy General Manager; annual satisfaction surveys to assess effectiveness.
    - Resources mobilized: €2 million annual budget; 439 outreach hours in 2023; 4 FTEs plus a work-study student seconded to the association.
  - MicroDon subsidiary (embedded giving):
    - Checkout rounding: over €47.7 million raised since inception.
    - Payroll giving: small, recurring donations from employees.
    - Donation of time: skills-based sponsorship and volunteering during work hours.
  - Broader commitments:
    - Banking partner to the social and solidarity economy, serving 150,000 association clients (around one in ten associations in France).
    - Supports major national campaigns (Téléthon, Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Pièces Jaunes) and partners with leading NGOs (Secours Populaire, French Red Cross, Fédération des Banques Alimentaires).
    - Collaborative initiatives via Alliance Dynamique and the Club de l’Initiative contre l’Exclusion Bancaire on community causes, banking inclusion, and budgeting education.
    - WWF partnership since 2021 to advance decarbonization and sustainable solutions.
    - Regular engagement with consumer associations to bolster mutual aid and social inclusion.
text:
3.3.3.2 Regional  network
La Banque Postale, through its integration within La Poste
Group, plays a role in maintaining the  regional network of
essential  services in  France. By relying on a dense
network 
of post offices and retail outlets, La Banque Postale
ensures  proximity to residents,  local authorities and
economic  players, particularly  in small municipalities.
This regional network is a strategic asset for meeting the
needs  of populations far from urban centre s and for
supporting local  authorities in their development  projects.
A direct  impact  on small municipalities
The La Poste network, which has thousands of post offices
and 
branches throughout the country, guarantees universal
access  to banking and postal services, even  in rural and
remote  areas. In  collaboration with La Banque Postale, this
regional network contributes to:
•prevent ing “banking deserts” by ensuring continuity of
service  in areas in which there are no  other financial
institutions;
•supporting local initiatives by facilitating access to financing
for environmental transition,  regional planning and
essential infrastructure projects (schools, hospitals,
social  housing,  etc.);
•supporting financial inclusion by offering solutions adapted
to the needs of  residents and local  authorities, such as
loans  at controlled  rates or inclusive banking  products.
Synergy  between La Banque  Postale and La Poste
This  collaboration enables  La Banque Postale to draw on
the expertise and presence of  the postal network to
maximis e its positive impact. For  example, post offices are
becoming contact points to raise awareness among local
elected  representatives of  the sustainable  financial
solutions offered  by La  Banque Postale .
The regional coverage assured by La Banque Postale and
the La Poste  network embodies a strong commitment to
small towns and rural areas. By maintaining a constant
dialogue with local authorities and adapting its services to
the specific needs of each region, La  Banque  Postale
actively contributes to financial  inclusion and sustainable
development, thus strengthening its role as  an essential
partner of local  authorities. [S3_4_03]

title: Societal sponsorship
heading: 2.3.3.3.3 Societal sponsorship
start_phrase: Through its L'Envol programme, La Banque Postale implements practical actions which have positive impacts on society.
summary:

- Synergy with La Poste to maximize impact, including using post offices to inform local elected officials about sustainable financial solutions; ongoing dialogue with local authorities and adaptation of services to regional needs.

  - Resources for L’Envol: €2 million annual budget; 439 hours of employee community outreach in 2023; 4 FTEs plus one work-study student seconded to the association.

text:
3.3.3.3 Societal  sponsorship
“L'Envol”  programme
Through  its L'Envol programme, La   Banque  Postale
implements practical actions which have positive impacts
on society. This  program, intended to support around a
hundred  young  people  from  modest  backgrounds each
year, reflects the Company’s commitment to social inclusion
and  educational  success.
This is a support system intended to support young people
from  modest backgrounds over a period of three to eight
years.  It aims  to promote their academic success, their
social inclusion and their access to higher education
through 
personalized monitoring, mentoring and educational
opportunities.
The young beneficiaries of the Envol program regularly
interact  with the association’s  monitoring officers andLa  Poste Group’s volunteer sponsors. These  interactions,
which can be remote or face-to-face, make it possible to
meet their specific needs and foster a bond of trust.
The  Deputy General Manager of Envol is responsible for
supervising  interactions.  The  effectiveness of  interactions
is assessed annually via satisfaction  questionnaires, the
results of  which are  analysed to improve the program.
For the Envol program, La  Banque  Postale  is mobilising
the following  resources:
•an annual budget of €2 million, which the Group allocates
to the association;
•number 
of hours of working time devoted to community
outreach:

•4 FTE employees and a work-study student from
La Banque Postale made  available to the association.
MicroDon
La Banque Postale, through its subsidiary MicroDon, promotes
“embedded” giving by offering simple and effective solutions
to support community causes:
•rounding up  at check-outs: this system enables customers
of 
partner retailers to round  up their purchases to the
nearest euro, with the cents being donated to associations.
Since it  was created, more than €47.7 million has been
raised through  this programme;

each month to associations, to create a community-
focused culture;

devote part  of their  working time to  association projects.
These initiatives have a strong impact on community activity
and  demons trate La   Banque  Postale’s commitment to
responsible  and  community-based  finance.
The Group’s  other  commitments to charities
La Banque Postale is  also a committed partner in  the  non-
profit sector and the structures of the social and solidarity
economy (SSE). With 150,000 customer  associations
nationwide, it has one in ten associations as customers.
La  Banque   Postale also plays a major role in promoting
giving 
through its subsidiary MicroDon. It actively supports
emblematic 
national initiatives such  as the Téléthon,
Breast  Cancer Awareness Month and the "Pièces Jaunes"
operation,  and works closely with leading associations
such  as Secours Populaire, the French Red Cross and the

Thanks to bodies such as Alliance Dynamique and the

title: Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
heading: 2.3.4.1 Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
start_phrase: All customers and end-users, whether natural or legal persons (individuals, companies, local public entities), likely to be affected by material impacts related to the activities of La Banque Postale Group (financing, insurance, investment, banking services) are covered by the information disclosed under ESRS 2.
summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information), focusing on ESRS S4 (consumers and end-users) and impact finance monitoring.

- Impact finance monitoring indicators:
  - Lending to local authorities, social housing, health, associations, and the local economy supports regional development, combats inequality, and advances a just transition.
  - Community loans tracked via sub-indicators: green loans aligned with the EU Taxonomy, social loans, and impact loans.
  - All indicators improved from 2023 to 2024; annual origination to local authorities already exceeded the 2025 target.

- Key metrics (2023 → 2024 vs 2025 target):
  - Annual loan premium income with local authorities: €4.5bn → €5.8bn (target €4.5bn) – surpassed.
  - Of which green & social: €1.6bn → €1.87bn (target €1.1bn) – surpassed.
  - Social housing, healthcare, non-profits: €1.0bn → €1.53bn (target €2.5bn) – progressing.
  - Of which sustainability loans: €0.4bn → €0.71bn (target €0.3bn) – surpassed.
  - Local economy: €1.9bn → €1.94bn (target €2.4bn) – progressing.
  - Of which sustainability loans: €0.5bn → €0.32bn (target €0.32bn) – target met.

- Scope of S4 (consumers/end-users):
  - Covers all customers and end-users of banking, insurance, investment, and services, including users of financed companies’ products.
  - Special focus on vulnerable customers (youth, elderly, financially fragile, disabled, low financial literacy).
  - Universal exposure to privacy risks due to sensitive data (banking secrecy, GDPR).

- Material impacts:
  - Negative (one-off):
    - Service activities: data leaks/cybersecurity incidents affecting sensitive personal data.
    - Financed activities: potential harm to consumer health/safety from financed operators; complex global value chains make detailed monitoring difficult; responsible investment strategies mitigate.
  - Positive:
    - Improved customer service, accessibility of bancassurance, and protection of customers’ financial security.
    - Strong emphasis on inclusion and support for vulnerable customers; regional development via public financial division partnership and local public player focus.

- Risks (consumers/end-users):
  - Abusive commercial/marketing practices (compliance and reputational risks).
  - Financial loss from inadequate customer protection practices.
  - Financial loss from insufficient partner assessment amid social inclusion transition.
  - Customer service failures.
  - No material opportunities identified in this scope; risks can affect all customers, not only vulnerable groups.

- Governance and stakeholder engagement:
  - Supervisory Board oversight of vulnerable customer issues.
  - Ongoing dialogue via the “Club de l’Initiative contre l’Exclusion Bancaire” to address banking exclusion.
  - In 2024, La Banque Postale is the only bank in France entrusted with a banking accessibility public service mission.

- Policies and ethics:
  - As a mission-led company (since 2022), LBP pursues social and environmental goals for a fair, accessible transition.
  - Group entities (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée, Retail Banking, LBP Consumer Finance) implement policies to maximize positive customer impact and reduce data security/confidentiality risks.
  - Ethical code of conduct (updated 2024) centers customer interests, fairness, transparency, accountability, regulatory compliance, and avoidance of conflicts of interest; available internally and publicly.
  - CNP Assurances’ code reinforces customer protection and ethical business practices.

users.
In 
particular, La  Banque  Postale Group has created the
“Club de  l’Initiative contre l’Exclusion Bancaire” (Initiative
Against Banking Exclusion think-tank), which brings together

commitment, 
in order to meet the needs of customers
experiencing financial difficulties.  These discussions give
the Group a detailed understanding of the challenges
faced  by vulnerable customers. They may be particularly
affected by abusive sales or marketing practices, as well as
failures in customer protection or customer service.
In 2024, La Banque Postale is also the only bank in France
in charge of a banking accessibility public service mission.
[S4_SBM_3_07]
The risks  concerning customers and end-users are not limited
to 
these categories, however, and may cover all customers
and end-users, regardless of  their situation. [S4_SBM_3_08]

title: Applicable policies
heading: 2.3.4.2.1 Applicable policies
start_phrase: La Banque Postale, a major international financial player and a mission-led company since 2022, places its customers at the heart of its model.
summary:
- Scope and purpose: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document covering CSR social information on consumers and end-users, including material impacts, risks, opportunities, policies, human rights, and stakeholder dialogue.
- Material impacts:
  - Service activities: key negative impact risk is data breaches/cybersecurity incidents due to sensitive personal data handling.
  - Financed activities: potential negative impact from financing activities that undermine consumer health/safety across complex global value chains.

- Key risks identified for banking services: abusive sales/marketing practices; financial loss from weak or unmet customer protection; partner assessment failures amid social inclusion transition; customer service failures. No material opportunities identified.
- Focus on vulnerable customers: topic overseen by the Supervisory Board; engagement through the “Club de l’Initiative contre l’Exclusion Bancaire”; La Banque Postale acts as France’s public service operator for banking accessibility in 2024.
- Customer-centric policies and governance: mission-led company since 2022; updated 2024 Ethical code of conduct (fairness, transparency, avoidance of conflicts of interest); customer protection embedded across entities (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée, Retail Banking, LBP Consumer Finance).
- Inclusion and accessibility measures:
  - Banking: “Simplicité” account package, “Atout Simplicité” program, universality of Livret A, transparent pricing, financial education tools.
  - Consumer finance: LBP CF policy (Dec 2024) to detect/support vulnerable customers, prevent over-indebtedness, and adapt offers.
  - Insurance: CNP Assurances commits to accessible, tailored protection solutions.
- Data protection and cybersecurity: Group IT Systems Security policy and ISS framework (annual updates; Group Risk Management Committee oversight); GDPR compliance, professional secrecy, CNIL notification protocols; Privacy by Design at CNP Assurances; internal codes and regular audits at Louvre Banque Privée.
- Responsible investment and exclusions:
  - LBP AM SRI Charter excludes financing with significant negative consumer health/safety impacts; ESG due diligence to prevent controversies and promote responsible consumption.

  - “Voice of the Customer” program: benchmark surveys (BVA Insight), post-contact and journey-specific surveys; results shared via dashboards to inform corrective actions and “irritant” resolution.

text:
3.4.2.1 Applicable policies
La  Banque  Postale, a major international financial  player
and a mission-led company since 2022, places its customers
at the heart of  its model. Building on its civic vocation, it
pursues ambitious  social and environmental targets to
promote a fair and accessible transition for all. Through its
various 
entities, in particular CNP  Assurances, LBP  AM,
Louvre Banque Privée, Retail Banking and La Banque Postale
Consumer 
Finance, La  Banque  Postale Group has
implemented specific policies aimed at maximising
positive 
impacts for  its customers while reducing the risks
related to the security  and confidentiality of  their data.
Customer service,  banking  accessibility, accessibility
of  insurance services, protection and financial security
of customers (Positive impact)
Focus on customers ’ interests
La Banque Postale places  the interests of its customers at
the heart of its commercial strategy. This commitment is
governed by the Ethical code of conduct. Updated in 2024,
it reiterates the principles of fairness, transparency and
accountability. The Code applies to all Group entities and
guarantees that all products and services offered meet the
real 
needs of customers and comply with the regulations in
force, and that employees act without any conflict of interest
and  systematically  prioriti se the interests of  customers.
It is available to all employees on the Group’s intranet.
A 
public version is also available to all on the
La Banque Postale Group website.
CNP Assurances’ code of conduct also covers customer
protection and respect  and ethics  in business conduct.
Specifically, it embeds the Company’s principles concerning
the protection of customers’ interests and business practices.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 2172Sustainable performance
Social information
Protect  vulnerable  customers
La  Banque  Postale takes action to protect the 1.7 million
customers experiencing  financial  difficulties, primarily
through  its "Simplicité" account package and the “Atout
Simplicité " programme for difficult  times. In addition,
1.2  million customers fall within the scope  of accessible
banking, in line with the Bank’s status as a mission-led
company. 
This mission is based on the universality of the
Livret A passbook savings account (more details are
available  in paragraph 2.3.4.5.2 “Actions implemented to
generate  positive  impacts”).
La Banque Postale Consumer Finance (LBP CF) has adopted
an internal  policy  for managing vulnerable customers ,
released  in December 2024, which governs the practices
and  processes to detect and  support these customers.
The initiatives include increased vigilance in the granting
of loans, the prevention of over-indebtedness and offers
adapted to  vulnerable populations.
These  commitments  are  documented in the
La  Banque  Postale Group’s 2024 mission report, which
illustrates  the Group’s efforts to promote banking and
social  inclusion.
La Banque Postale designs accessible  and inclusive products
to meet social and regional challenges. With  regard to
banking accessibility, there are offers adapted for vulnerable
customers, 
with transparent prices and educational tools to
strengthen 
the understanding of financial products. For the
accessibility of insurance services, CNP Assurances undertakes
to offer insurance solutions that are accessible and adapted
to the specific needs of its customers, by contributing to
their  social protection. Details of  these offers can be found
in Section 2.3.4.5  “Action  plans and  resources”.
Negative  impact in the event of a data breach
or cybersecurity  incident.
Risks related to cybersecurity and personal data protection
are considered critical, as they could compromise the
confidentiality  and  security of customer information.
La Banque Postale’s  IT Systems Security policy provides a
structured response to these challenges. It is based on an
ISS Reference Framework, which includes the General ISS
Policy,  charters of obligations for employees and thematic
policies specifying the security requirements of information
systems. These policies are updated annually and validated
by the Group  Risk  Management  Committee.
As a bancassurance institution and in accordance with the
various legislation in force, La  Banque  Postale Group's
priorities 
include  protecting personal data, complyi ng
with  banking  secrecy and  tackling  fraud.
The data protection policy focuses on confidentiality, fairness
and  access  to information for  clients. It  is governed  by the
Ethical code of  conduct, which specifies the obligations of
employees in  terms  of professional secrecy and data
processing. In the event of a data leak, procedures for detection,
notification to the CNIL and corrective measures are
systematically  applied.
CNP Assurances applies the principle of Privacy by Design,
incorporating risk analyses from  project design, with
measures to prevent data breaches and rigorous monitoring
of incidents by  the Compliance  Department.Louvre Banque Privée, through its internal code of conduct,
adopts policies to guarantee  the confidentiality and security
of 
its customers’ data. The application of the GDPR is
accompanied  by policies on the management of consent
and the retention period of  data. In addition, regular
audits  are carried out by  the Legal Department and the
Compliance Department to ensure the effectiveness of
the systems  in place.
Negative  impact in  the event of financing of activities
which undermine the safety and/or health of consumers
(Negative impact)
Through its Socially Responsible Investment Charter (SRI),
LBP 
AM undertakes to exclude from its financing any
activity 
that has a significant negative impact on the
health 
and safety of consumers. This charter sets strict
criteria to avoid supporting sectors or companies whose
practices could harm consumers, such as the production
or distribution of  products dangerous to public health or
activities that do not comply with international regulations
on safety of products or environmental, social and health
impact.
In 
addition, LBP AM incorporates in-depth ESG due diligence
processes to assess the risks associated with financed
projects, 
particularly in terms of violations of consumer
rights or non-compliance with regulations. These practices
aim 
to reduce the risk of controversy and strengthen the
positive impact of investments by directing financial flows
to 
companies and projects that promote responsible and
sustainable consumption.
Louvre  Banque  Privée has developed an exclusion policy
for directly invested securities that covers several specific
segments. These are primarily  sector-specific exclusions
extended to activities that are either controversial or not in
accordance 
with international conventions or  national
regulatory frameworks:
•hazardous chemicals: companies that generate more
than  10% of their revenue by producing pesticides;
•pornography:  companies  that generate  more than 10%
of their revenue  from the pornography or adult
entertainment services sectors;
•controversial  weapons:  companies that  generate more
than 5% of their revenue from arms and that are involved
in controversial weapons;
•gambling: companies that generate more  than 10% of
revenue from gambling services or products;
•tobacco: companies that generate more  than 0% of
revenue from tobacco production. [S4_MDR_P_01_06]
The 
various risks identified are effectively managed by
being integrated into the Group’s risk matrix and included
in the corresponding reduction action plans. As a result,
special attention is paid to each risk identified, ensuring
proactive  and rigorous management. Internal procedures
are in place to ensure compliance with the regulations in
force, although there is no dedicated policy for them.

Results feed management dashboards and drive corrective actions, including a structured program to identify and resolve recurring “irritants.”

text:
3.4.2.2 Respect  for Human Rights
As a subsidiary of La Poste Group, a  signatory to the  UN
Global Compact since 2006, La  Banque  Postale upholds
the principles set forth by the Global Compact on Human
Rights,  labour  standards, environmental  protection  and
the fight against corruption. It undertakes to comply with
the legal  texts  governing  its activities  as well as the
international agreements signed by France. In this context,
it considers the United Nations Guiding Principles, the ILO
Conventions  and the OECD Guidelines as a reference
base. As part of its Responsible Financing and Investment
Charter, La  Banque  Postale undertakes to verify, before
investing  or financing, that the  company in question is not
involved in an ESG controversy, and especially one concerning
a Human Rights  violation. For  more information, see focus
point: La Banque Postale's Financing and Investment Charter.
For 
details on the LBP AM Human Rights policy, please refer
to the paragraph on Applicable policies. [S4_1_02] [S4_1_03] [S4_1_07]
Human  Rights  remedies
LBP   AM uses its  sphere of influence with companies to
allow  or support a remedy in the event of an actual or
potential material impact caused by an invested company,
or to which an invested company has  contributed, in
accordance with its Human Rights policy and its Engagement
policy. Additional information is available in Section 2.3.2.2
“Workers  in the upstream  value chain”. [S4_1_05]
Compliance  with international standards
As a sustainable bank, La  Banque  Postale is a signatory
to  seven  international  agreements . These partnerships
strengthen its positioning  as a responsible player  on social
and environmental  issues. [S4_1_06]

title: Dialogue mechanisms with customers and end-users
heading: 2.3.4.3 Dialogue mechanisms with customers and end-users
start_phrase: On a day-to-day basis, interactions with customers take place directly within the network, either through complaints channels or through surveys.
summary:
- Human rights commitments: La Banque Postale adheres to the UN Global Compact, UN Guiding Principles, ILO Conventions, and OECD Guidelines, and complies with relevant laws and international agreements. Its Responsible Financing and Investment Charter screens investments for ESG controversies, especially human rights. LBP AM uses its influence to support remedies for actual or potential human rights impacts per its Human Rights and Engagement policies. The bank is a signatory to seven international agreements reinforcing its social and environmental responsibility.

- Customer and end‑user dialogue: 
  - Retail Banking: A 16‑member Customer Council meets three times a year; regular round tables at Customer Relations and Expertise Centres address specialized topics. Extensive “Voice of the Customer” research (benchmarking, post‑contact, and journey‑specific surveys) informs corrective actions, dashboards, and governance. A program targets and tracks resolution of recurring “irritants.”
  - Corporate and Local Development Banking: No current satisfaction survey; projects are underway to measure and monitor satisfaction and to formalize centralized handling of business customer complaints.
  - CNP Assurances: Uses a customer dashboard for Executive Committee oversight; tracks service quality and perceived quality via NPS, CES, and CSAT; runs email surveys and twice‑yearly overall satisfaction checks; operates the “You & Us” online community for co‑creation and insights; follows up with dissatisfied respondents; does not use intermediaries.
  - LBP AM: Cannot engage directly with end‑consumers but incorporates stakeholder and end‑user perspectives into its Human Rights policy and company engagement; participates in initiatives such as Ranking Digital Rights, the Coalition for Ethical AI, and the Access to Medicine Foundation to inform engagement.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Uses an annual satisfaction barometer; no specific measures for particularly vulnerable consumers due to its wealth‑management focus.

- Support for customers facing financial difficulties: Engagement with stakeholders through an Initiative Against Banking Exclusion think‑tank. Spot NPS measures satisfaction of customers supported by the L’Appui banking and budget platform. A QR‑code pilot collects feedback from cash‑counter users, with nationwide rollout targeted for September 2025. LBP Consumer Finance proactively contacts “vulnerable” customers and a dedicated Support division offers tailored solutions and referrals (e.g., CRESUS, Banque de France, social services).

- Reporting and remediation: 
  - LBP Consumer Finance’s Customer Relations Centre manages complaints and escalates to a Complaints Department, with regular reporting to the Quality Committee and root‑cause analysis.
  - Retail Banking has a dedicated complaints department focused on continuous improvement and processing times. Multiple channels are available (call centers, online banking, social media, in‑branch and remote advisory, Business Centres). The Supervisory Board and Risk Committee conduct annual regulatory monitoring of complaints.
text:
3.4.3 Dialogue  mechanisms 
with  customers  and end-users
On a day-to-day basis, interactions with customers take place
directly  within the network,  either through complaints
channels  or through surveys.
For end-users  of invested companies, particularly  in the
case of LBP AM, interactions are indirect through legitimate
representatives. [S4_2_02]
Customer  advice
La Banque Postale coordinates a “customer council”, which
is a body representing so-called “individual” customers.
As  a partner of the  Executive Committee,  the Customer
Council is composed of 16 members who  reflect the
diversity of the  Bank’s customers and the French people.
It is called upon  three  times a year to collect customer
opinions  on projects intended to improve the  offer, the
quality of service  or the customer  experience.
This  Customer Council is  supplemented by regular
customer  round tables held at the Customer Relations
and  Expertise Centres (CREC),  which focus on  specialised
areas  such as Real Estate  Loans, Protected Adults and
Specialised  Savings. These bodies make it possible to
discuss  face-to-face with customers about their lived
experience  and adjust the local arrangements for  theircare. Their expectations which do not fall within their
scope  of intervention are compiled and reported at the
national 
level for analysis and consideration. [S4_2_01] [S4_2_02]
[S4_2_03] [S4_2_04]  [S4_2_05]
The voice  of the customer
La Banque Postale carries out numerous studies to regularly
collect 
the views and expectations of its Retail Banking
customers. The main “Voice of the Customer” study,
carried  out by BVA Insight, measures La Banque Postale’s
performance  in terms of customer experience compared
to its competitors. Each year, it interviews retail bank
customers from a representative national sample of French
people.  The surveys are carried out throughout the year,
and  the results are published quarterly. This benchmark is
supplemented by  post-contact surveys  (online banking,
customer call centre, post office advisor, reception in the
Commercial 
Centre) and by interim surveys measuring
the level of satisfaction for key steps (account opening,
granting 
a home loan, the underwriting of an insurance
product  or filing  a claim).
The results of these studies are made available to the
managers of the Customer Relationship Management
teams.  They are then shared by managers with their
teams  in order to implement corrective actions.  This data
is included in monthly and quarterly dashboards made
available to the management bodies of both
La  Banque   Postale and La  Poste Group in order to
monitor the effectiveness of the actions implemented
with 
regard to the chosen strategic  priorities. Finally, all of
these  systems are supplemented by  an approach to
resolve “irritants” (frequent  niggling  issues  that irritate
customers and employees and lead to a worse experience).
The progress of the treatment of these irritants is
communicated via the platform, in governance bodies
and  by an internal communication plan.  [S4_2_01] [S4_2_02]
[S4_2_03] [S4_2_04]  [S4_2_05]
Dialogue with business customers
Currently, for Corporate and Local Development Banking,
there is no satisfaction survey for business customers.
La  Banque  Postale is working  on severa l projects to
measure and monitor  customer satisfaction. [S4_2_01] [S4_2_02]
[S4_2_03]  [S4_2_04]  [S4_2_05]
A project is underway for  Corporate and Local Development
Banking 
to formalise a procedure for centralising business
customer complaints.  [S4_2_07]
Dialogue provided by CNP  Assurances
CNP   Assurances also incorporates the perspectives of
customers 
and consumers in the improvement of its
activities and services. A customer dashboard is periodically
presented 
to the Executive Committee in order to manage
customer 
satisfaction indicators. These indicators measure
the quality of service (telephone accessibility, complaint
processing 
times and decision-making times for all
customer journeys)  and  the  perceived quality (Net
Promoter Score (NPS)), which measures customer loyalty
based  on how likely they are to recommend the products
and  services,  and Customer Effort Score (CES), which
measures 
the effort made by customers to obtain a
response to their request).Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 2192Sustainable performance
Social information
To 
measure customer satisfaction, since 2015, CNP Assurances
has used questionnaires sent by email to measure
customer  satisfaction , and  since  2022, some  customers
are asked about  their overall  satisfaction twice  a year.
[S4_2_01] [S4_2_02]  [S4_2_03]  [S4_2_04] [S4_2_05]
CNP   Assurances has also created the "You & Us" online
community  in France  to better understand the uses and
expectations of prospects  and customers.  This "You & Us"
digital platform is thus a privileged and direct space for
exchanges,  making it possible to involve customers in a
variety  of projects in  order  to make  them actors  in the
evolution of offers  and services. The platform is structured
around discussion  forums on various topics (digital uses,
lifestyles), thematic workshops for co-creation of products
and  their pathways connecting the Company’s customers
and  employees, and online surveys to identify the first
trends.
CNP   Assurances does  not  use  legitimate  representatives
or trusted intermediaries for  interactions with customers.
CNP  Assurances uses indicators  such as the  NPS and the
CSAT  (Customer  Satisfaction Score,  which  measures
overall customer  satisfaction).  Systems for  contacting
customers who have expressed  dissatisfaction in their
response to a  survey  are  then  rolled out in  France and
abroad.  [S4_3_02]
Dialogue  provided by LBP  AM
As an asset management company, LBP  AM cannot
interact  directly with the end consumers of the
companies  in which it invests. However, the  perspectives
of stakeholders,  including end-users,  are taken  into
account  in the establishment and monitoring of its
Human  Rights policy , and in its engagement activities
with the companies  involved.
LBP   AM consults with external stakeholders to raise its
employees’  awareness of the  risks related to the rights of
consumers  and workers in the value chains of the
companies involved, to refine the analysis of the risks or
controversies  related to  the products or services of the
companies involved , and develop sectoral tools  or policies
adapted to  specific challenges.
LBP  AM also participates in sectoral initiatives such as the
Ranking  Digital Rights (RDR), the Coalition for Ethical AI
and  the Access to Medicine Foundation. This enables it to
feed into its engagement policies with companies on
issues  affecting end users. [S4_2_01] [S4_2_02] [S4_2_03] [S4_2_04]
[S4_2_05]
Dialogue  provided by Louvre  Banque Privée
For its part, Louvre  Banque  Privée has tools for dialogue
with  consumers and users, such as an annual satisfaction
barometer, which can be quantitative or qualitative,
depending  on the year. It  provides key information on
customers'  main concerns. [S4_2_01] [S4_2_02]  [S4_2_03]  [S4_2_04]
[S4_2_05]
Louvre   Banque  Privée has not implemented specific
measures  for consumers and end-users likely to be
particularly  vulnerable to the impacts and/or to be
marginalised. These vulnerable consumer profiles are less
frequent  due  to the  focus on wealth management. [S4_2_06]Dialogue with customers experiencing 
financial difficulties
Understanding 
the exposure to banking exclusion risks for
consumers  and  end-users with particular characteristics
is informed by dialogue with the relevant stakeholders.
With this in mind, La  Banque  Postale  has created an
“Initiative Against Banking Exclusion  Think-tank” (see
Section 2.3.4.1 – Material IROs and links with strategy and
business model).
In 
Retail Banking, a spot NPS has been in place for the
past 
year for customers experiencing financial difficulties.
It 
measures the satisfaction of the customers supported
by the L'Appui banking and budget  platform by
telephone  interview.
As far as accessible banking customers are concerned
(holding a Livret A passbook savings account and carrying
out 
many cash transactions at the counter), La Banque Postale
is currently trialling a satisfaction measurement system
for customers carrying out cash transactions at the counter
via a QR Code in selected post offices throughout the
country. At the end of the tests, this  system should be
rolled out in September  2025.
In addition, La  Banque   Postale Consumer Finance (LBP
CF) sends a letter to  customers classified as “vulnerable”,
inviting  them to contact the Support  division if they feel
the need. They can then re-express their specific concerns
or needs.
The support division is a team dedicated to helping
La  Banque   Postale Consumer Finance’s vulnerable
customers. Its role  is to analyse the customer’s situation
with 
them and identify whether the vulnerability is short-
term or permanent, with the aim of providing the most
appropriate  solution. The solutions provided are varied:
carrying 
out management actions, moral support or providing
information on structures that can help vulnerable customers
(CRESUS, Banque de France, social worker,  etc.). [S4_2_06]

title: Reporting and remediation process
heading: 2.3.4.4 Reporting and remediation process
start_phrase: In the event of a negative impact, La Banque Postale has several departments tasked with providing solutions to customers.
summary:
- Focus on customer satisfaction measurement across Group entities:
  - CNP Assurances uses email surveys (since 2015), twice‑yearly overall satisfaction checks (since 2022), NPS and CSAT tracking, follow‑ups to dissatisfied respondents, and the “You & Us” online community for co‑creation, forums, workshops, and surveys.
  - Louvre Banque Privée runs an annual satisfaction barometer (quantitative/qualitative by year).
  - La Banque Postale runs spot NPS for customers supported by the L’Appui banking/budget platform; pilots QR‑code surveys for cash counter users (nationwide rollout targeted for Sept 2025).

- Stakeholder dialogue and integration of end‑user perspectives:
  - LBP AM embeds stakeholder and end‑user views in its Human Rights policy and corporate engagement; consults external stakeholders; participates in sector initiatives (Ranking Digital Rights, Coalition for Ethical AI, Access to Medicine Foundation).
  - Louvre Banque Privée has fewer vulnerable consumer profiles given its wealth‑management focus and no specific measures for such groups.

- Support for vulnerable customers and those facing financial difficulties:
  - La Banque Postale set up an “Initiative Against Banking Exclusion” think‑tank.
  - LBP Consumer Finance proactively contacts customers flagged as vulnerable and operates a dedicated Support division to assess situations and propose tailored solutions or referrals (e.g., CRESUS, Banque de France, social services).

- Complaints and remediation mechanisms:
  - LBP Consumer Finance: Customer Relations Centre triages and forwards to a Complaints Department; regular reporting and root‑cause analysis.
  - Retail Banking: dedicated complaints department; multiple access channels (call centres, online, social media, face‑to‑face and remote advisory); supervisory oversight by the Supervisory Board and Risk Committee.
  - Insurance (CNP Assurances): leverages Brazilian consumer/government platforms (Reclame Aqui, Procon, consumidor.gov); enhanced service (incl. WhatsApp); RA1000 certification and award nomination.
  - LBP AM: published Complaints Management policy with multiple channels.

- Communication and accessibility of channels:
  - Extensive physical network (17,000+ retail outlets, including 7,000 post offices; 43 corporate/local development business centres).
  - Complaints can be filed via Customer Service or a dedicated online form.

- Request management and continuous improvement:
  - Daily triage of emails/letters; SLA checkpoints (10, 35, 60 days).
  - “Footprint Labs” to review response quality; root‑cause analysis of major complaints; PEPS continuous improvement deployed across Customer Relations and Expertise Centres.
  - Dedicated team analyzes customer journeys; monitoring of service quality (phone accessibility, post‑contact NPS).
  - Corporate and Local Development Banking customers briefed on complaint processes.

- Whistleblowing:
  - Group‑wide whistleblowing system open to consumers and end‑users, in line with duty‑of‑vigilance requirements.

- Cybersecurity governance and incident management:
  - Defined process for security event/incident management with anticipation (threat monitoring) and reaction (incident response) pillars; crisis management procedures for critical ISS/cyber cases; post‑incident reviews and action plans.

- Action plans addressing privacy and cybersecurity risks:
  - 2021–2027 cybersecurity strategic plan (50 key projects): continuous monitoring/detection (SOC) and deployment of safeguards to protect data.
  - Crisis unit for incident handling (including potential system lockdowns), eradication, and regulatory notifications as required.
  - Ongoing employee training and anti‑fraud awareness.

- Personal data protection and GDPR compliance:
  - Privacy by Design integrated into product/service development; tools (customer dictionary, marketing plan) to personalize communications and avoid mass campaigns; staff GDPR training.
  - Subsidiaries:
    - CNP Assurances: Privacy by Design with upfront privacy risk analyses and technical/organizational safeguards.
    - Louvre Banque Privée: data confidentiality policies, consent management, limited retention, and regular audits.

- Governance and assurance:
  - Annual updates to security policies validated by the Group Risk Management Committee; General ISS policy and topical policies; regular internal audits of controls’ effectiveness.

- Monitoring of effectiveness and resources:
  - Use of indicators (including for vulnerable populations) to track outcomes.
  - Monthly committee monitoring Online Banking and Mobile App incidents to prioritize fixes and drive continuous customer‑experience improvements.
text:
3.4.4 Reporting and remediation process
In 
the event  of a negative impact,  La Banque Postale has
several departments tasked with providing solutions to
customers.
LBP Consumer Finance
La Banque Postale Consumer Finance’s Customer Relations
Centre handles complaints from customers or third parties
made 
by telephone, and refers dissatisfied customers to
the Complaints Department for follow-up by letter. Complaints
are 
subject to regular reporting, particularly during the Quality
Committee 
meetings, and an analysis of any shortcomings
they raise is carried out in order to provide a solution. [S4_3_01]
Retail Banking
For 
its part, Retail Banking has a department dedicated to
handling customer complaints, facilitating the continuous
improvement of  complaints  processing methods and
managing processing times. [S4_3_01]
Customer concerns and  needs are raised via the specific
channels made available to them. Retail Banking customers
can 
use call centres, online banking, social media, the
Commercial 
Banking Line face-to-face  and remotely (via
La  Banque  Postale Chez Soi), or communicate with
customer service advisors  at Business  Centres. [S4_3_02]
The Supervisory Board and the Risk Committee  carry out
the annual regulatory  monitoring  of complaints.  [S4_3_04]220 La Banque  Postale      2024 Universal Registration  Document Please see the glossary on page 808 for definitions of  the main CSR terms2Sustainable performance
Social information
Insurance
In addition to the pre-existing reporting and complaints
systems  (online complaints forms,  email, phone, social
media,  etc.), CNP  Assurances relies on consumer or
government organisations in the Brazilian market, such as
Reclame Aqui , Procon and consumidor.gov.
In 2024, Caixa Seguros Holding reviewed the service
processes  of Reclame Aqui, the largest  complaints
website in Latin America. The service has been brought in-
house,  prioritising quality and agility with the addition of
WhatsApp to expand interactions  and encourage positive
customer  reviews. Thanks to this system, CSH has
achieved  the  RA1000  quality certification, the platform’s
max imum  approval, having obtained the best rating in
the insurance sector.  CSH was  also nominated  for the
Reclame Aqui award  in 2024. [S4_3_01]  [S4_3_02]
LBP  AM
LBP   AM has a Complaints Management policy which is
available on the website. Several channels are made
available,  in particular  via the account manager and the
generic customer  service  address.  [S4_3_02]
Communication on the channels available  
to customers
La  Banque  Postale relies on its France-wide  network to
ensure that its customers  are aware of  all of the
communications  channels. With more than 17,000 retail
outlets,  including 7,000 post offices, it has a strong
network to support  all of its markets. For business
customers, 43 Corporate and Local Development Banking
business  centres  are spread across mainland  and
overseas  regions. This structure  enables customer service
advisors  to be based near to their customers to ensure
that  they are  satisfied with the service. Customers who
wish to  file a complaint can do so by  contacting Customer
Service, which will explain the procedures related to their
complaint. 
Customers may also record their complaint
using  a dedicated  form available  on the  Bank’s website.
[S4_3_03]
Request  management
Requests  from Retail Banking customers are processed
every  day by triage teams, who ensure timely response to
emails  and letters sent to La  Banque  Postale’s various
processing  departments. When targets are not met, the
departments in question readjust their processing priorities
to reduce delays. At the same time, drafting committees
(“Footprint  Labs”) are held to assess the relevance of the
responses  provided and whether they are in line with the
Bank’s 
relationship charter. More specifically, La Banque Postale’s
Complaints Department ensures compliance with customer
response times at 10 days, 35 days and 60 days. It monitors
the main complaints  filed and analyses their  root causes
for discussion with the business lines, and processing of
these causes. It also cross-references this information with
the expectations  of customer  claimants expressed during
the barometer dedicated to this activity to improve the
methods for handling and processing complaints. Where
appropriate,  when the  differences  and  customer  issues
are significant,  progress  projects are implemented to
improve  the quality of care. The “Power to be a Driver of
Solutions”  (PEPS)  continuous  improvement  approach  is
now in place in all Customer Relations  and Expertise
Centres and  their  respective  departments.A team was also set up to  analys e customer journeys and
recommend improvements to the business  lines.
The  approach relies  on the direct involvement of
employees  to improve  customer  relations and develop
the resulting quality standards. It always begins with a
dedicated collection of  customer opinions.
Finally, the  quality of service indicators (telephone accessibility,
post-contact  NPS) are monitored by managers, enabling
them to  react quickly  in the event  of a discrepancy. [S4_3_04]
Consumers and end-users of Corporate and Local Development
Banking 
are aware of the procedures for reporting and
processing 
complaints. If in doubt, they can contact their
business advisor or Customer Services, as well as dedicated
experts (flow management, investments,  etc.), who are
available 
to listen to their concerns and meet their needs.
[S4_3_05]
A whistleblowing system
In 
addition and in accordance with the law  on the duty  of
vigilance, the entities of the La  Banque  Postale Group
have set up a whistleblowing system that is open to
consumers  and end users. This system is described in data
point  2.4.1.3.5 “Independence and  accessibility of the
whistleblowing  system”.  [S4_3_06]
Cybersecurity
A process for managing security events and  incidents has
been deployed within La  Banque  Postale Group.
This 
process is described in  the Topical Security Policy
entitled “Managing Security Events and Incidents”.
The challenge  is to ensure that  the method of identifying
events  and breaches related to information security allows
corrective action to be implemented as soon as possible,
as 
well as the implementation of a consistent, efficient
and  tracked approach to the processing of events and
incidents  related to information security.
The treatment of  ISS threats and vulnerabilities aims to
take 
into account security notifications as soon as possible
in order to categorise them with regard to their impact
on the La  Banque  Postale Group’s IS  and provide  an
appropriate response.
This 
system is based on two main focus areas: an
"anticipation" 
focus, with the  implementation of external
monitoring/IS  security monitoring systems; as well as a
"reaction " focus to respond  to IS security  events/incidents
in order to minimise their potential impact.
For cases that require it, the management of security
events  may be based on the La  Banque  Postale Group’s
crisis management  process, depending on  their criticality.
La  Banque  Postale Group has put in place a crisis
management procedure for ISS/cybersecurity incidents.
It  is  intended to establish the organisation, roles,
responsibilities, process and principles of governance as
part  of the implementation of the incident and crisis
management system 
applicable to  the Group’s ISS.
Feedback and  lessons learned are analysed for  each
significant security incident.  Where  applicable, action
plans are established and monitored.Please  see the glossary  on page 808 for definitions of the main CSR terms 2024 Universal  Registration Document     La Banque Postale 2212Sustainable performance

title: Actions taken to address negative impacts
heading: 2.3.4.5.1 Actions taken to address negative impacts
start_phrase: La Banque Postale and its subsidiaries, including CNP Assurances and Louvre Banque Privée, have implemented action plans to manage risks related to privacy and cybersecurity, which are recognised as potential material negative impacts.
summary:
- Scope: CSR/Social information focusing on action plans, resources, and outcomes related to privacy, cybersecurity, customer accessibility, and inclusion across La Banque Postale Group and subsidiaries (CNP Assurances, Louvre Banque Privée).

- Managing negative impacts (privacy and cybersecurity):
  - Cybersecurity strategic plan 2021–2027 with 50 key projects:
    - Threat identification via a 24/7 monitoring and detection center.
    - Deployment of safeguards to protect customer information and personal data.
  - Incident management:
    - Dedicated crisis unit, potential partial/total IS lockdown, eradication actions, post-incident analysis, regulatory notifications as needed.
  - Training and awareness:
    - Anti-fraud team with preventive measures and regular staff training to identify risky behaviors.
  - Data protection and GDPR:
    - Privacy by Design embedded in products/services.
    - Tools (customer dictionary, marketing plan) to personalize communications and avoid mass campaigns.
    - Employee training on GDPR.
  - Subsidiaries:
    - CNP Assurances: Privacy by Design, privacy risk analyses at project launch, technical/organizational safeguards.
    - Louvre Banque Privée: confidentiality policies, consent management, limited retention, regular audits overseen by Legal and Compliance.
  - Governance and audits:
    - Annual updates to security policies validated by the Group Risk Management Committee (General ISS policy, topical policies).
    - Regular internal audits of compliance and effectiveness.

- Monitoring effectiveness and resources:
  - Use of indicators to assess impacts on consumers, including vulnerable populations (referenced in Section 2.2.1.11.1).
  - Monthly committee overseeing incidents on Online Banking and Mobile App, prioritizing fixes and continuous customer experience improvement.

- Generating positive impacts (accessibility, protection, financial security):
  - Commitment to quality service, universal access to bancassurance, and customer protection.
  - Accessible banking mission:
    - State-entrusted mission ensuring universal, non-discriminatory access to essential banking.
    - Livret A as a universal, free product; withdrawals/deposits from €1.50; authorized transfers for benefits and essential bills; additional free services.
    - 1.2 million customers excluded from traditional banking served.
  - Access to products and services:
    - Simplified contractual documents for better understanding.
    - Banking/insurance products:
      - Simplicité low-cost account for 1.7 million customers in difficulty, with capped annual fees (€1,500).
      - CNP Assurances: 14 inclusive insurance products (2024), 828,000 policyholders; affordable funeral cover (up to €2,500); microinsurance in Latin America for low-income families; Italian offers enabling credit to low-income retirees with repayments capped at 20% of pension.
      - Clear language governance for customer documents (since 2024); 24% of management letters revised in 2024.
      - Broad distribution via post offices (France) and lottery points (Brazil) for reach into remote areas.
    - Credit solutions:
      - Youth-focused loans (e.g., one-euro-a-day driving licence loan; Student and Apprentice Loans).
      - Personal microloans via associations (CCAS, Restos du Cœur) for social reintegration projects.
      - Professional microloans for small businesses and micro-entrepreneurs to combat exclusion and support activity.
      - Temporary personal loan for temp workers.
      - Three-instalment financing via Django app using open banking analytics.
      - Home loans including no down-payment options and social home loans for low-income households.
  - Protection of vulnerable customers:
    - Dedicated systems and services to safeguard and support vulnerable clients.
text:
3.4.5.1 Actions taken to address negative impacts
Description  of actions
La  Banque  Postale and its subsidiaries, including
CNP   Assurances  an d Louvre  Banque  Privée, have
implemented  action plans to manage risks related to
privacy  and cybersecurity, which are recognised as
potential  material  negative impacts.  These  issues,  which
are essential to preserve the  relationship of trust with
customers,  are  addressed through structured strategies,
dedicated governance systems, and  specific actions
aimed at guaranteeing the  protection of personal data
and preventing  cybersecurity incidents.
Cybersecurity  risk management
Cybersecurity  strategic plan  (2021-2027)
La Banque Postale has drawn  up an ambitious cybersecurity
strategic  plan for the 2021-2027 period, including 50 key
projects.  This  plan  is based  on two  major  target s:
•identify cybersecurity threats: a security incident monitoring
and  detection centre provides  permanent oversight to
quickly detect cyberattacks and respond to them effectively;
•develop  and deploy safeguards: tools  and  protocols are
implemented  to protect customer information and
personal data  from  unauthorised access.
Cyber security  incident  management
In the event of a threat or incident, a dedicated crisis unit
assesses the situation and decides on immediate measures,
such as total  or partial  lockdown of the information
system.  Eradication  actions are  then  implemented,
followed by a  post-incident analysis  to identify the causes
and  prevent recurrence. A notification is made to the
competent authorities if necessary, in accordance with
the regulations  in force.
Team  training  and  awareness
A proactive fight against fraud is carried out by a dedicated
team  through preventive measures and regular training
for employees. The teams are thus made aware of the
risks of fraud  and trained  regularly to  identify risky
behaviours.  These actions make it possible to strengthen
cybersecurity  skills within  the field  and  head  office teams.Protection of personal data
La  Banque  Postale guarantees rigorous management of
personal data, in  accordance with the  GDPR, based on:
•the principle of Privacy by Design,  which incorporates
data protection into  the design of products  and services;
•dedicated tools, such as the customer dictionary and
the marketing plan,  to personalise communications and
avoid mass campaigns, thus boosting customer satisfaction
and  confidence;
•specific  training on GDPR  (see Section 2.3.1.2. “Employee
policies”), which raises employee awareness of confidentiality
and data protection  requirements.
Commitments of La  Banque Postale  Group subsidiaries
CNP   Assurances adopts a proactive approach with a
Privacy  by Design policy, which includes privacy risk
analyses  from the launch of new projects as well as
technical and organisational measures  to secure personal
data against  any unauthorised access or processing.
Louvre Banque Privée applies data confidentiality policies
(see  Section 2.3.4.2.1. – Applicable policies), supervised by
its 
Legal Department and Compliance Department, including
managing customer consent, limiting the data retention
period and regular audits to  guarantee the application of
data protection policies.
Governance and regular audits
Every  year, La Banque Postale  updates its security policies,
validated by the Group Risk Management Committee.
These policies include:
•the General Information Systems Security  (ISS) policy;
•the topical security policies, which specify the requirements
applicable to all Group entities;
•regular internal audits  to assess the compliance and
effectiveness of protection measures. [S4_4_01] [S4_4_02]
Monitoring the effectiveness of actions 
and allocated resources
To 
monitor and assess the  effectiveness of actions for
consumers and end  users, La   Banque   Postale relies on a
set of indicators to measure the impact of its systems, in
particular on the most vulnerable populations. These indicators
are 
presented in Section 2. 2.1.11.1 “Additional indicators
specific  to the  entity”.
In addition, La  Banque  Postale has set up a monthly
committee to monitor and manage incidents related to
Online Banking  and the Mobile App in order to ensure
reliable 
service adapted  to the expectations of end users.
This committee identifies any issues, prioritises their
resolution, and ensures continuous improvement of the
customer experience.
